And if they also willingly follow this calling, the author says as if to a filthy city: 'Shake off your dust, Jerusalem' (Ps 17:43). But the Lord, or His imitator, the just, licks these even as mud in the streets. But this mud being licked will not be able to become an earthen vessel useful in the great house in which there are golden and silver and wooden and earthen vessels; but since the golden and silver are for honor and the wooden and earthen are for dishonor, the one cleansing himself from these becomes a vessel of honor, having been sanctified and made useful to the Master, prepared for every good work, while those who remain such mud in the streets—that is, the mire of pleasures and desires—are being freed from all roughness from the passions.

He who says these things, by instilling a uniformity through the licking, is now making them earthen vessels, if they should cleanse themselves by a spontaneous impulse as if to become vessels of honor, golden or silver. For just as some have become earthen vessels from golden and silver ones (For the precious sons of Zion, exalted with silver, how were they reckoned as earthen vessels of the work of hands? [Ps 51:7]), so from their own domestic choice they shall become golden or silver from earthen ones.

Regarding the second meaning of the name of knowledge, he shows both the knowing and the being known and being recognized by the one knowing the one being known. According to the former meaning, God knows all, and not only the diligent ones. For toward the lowly the Savior says: 'You justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts' (Mt 6:1); and in the prophet: 'Because I knew all your sins' (Ps 40:3). And according to the second [meaning]...

It is said that he recognizes only the righteous. For the Lord knew those who were his, but he ignored the wicked. The Savior says to them: 'Depart from me, workers of lawlessness, I never knew you' (Matt 7:23). And the people from the nations, not being known by the Savior, though he healed both demons and idols and practiced all manner of evil, having changed through repentance to serve Christ, came to him. And even the saying 'He did not know' is true. For it is not said: 'A people I do not know served me' (Matt 15:22). For he who is doing the works of wickedness is not known; but he who has ceased from sins was not known before, but is known now.

To this the apostolic word agrees, saying: 'But formerly, not knowing God, you served those which by nature are not gods; but now, having known God, and even more having been known by God' (Gal 4:8). For they did not know God, and they were unknown by him, but having known him, they were known by him. Perhaps it will seem to some that the spoken thing passes by: 'To the hearing of an ear I obeyed' (1 Sam 13:30), meaning to obey with an ear that obeys all things. But the ear is not intended to pass by or to be superfluous for the one obeying all things, so as to use a non-human and mortal hearing, but a divine ear added to the one approaching; for he added to me an ear for hearing.

'Alien sons have grown old' (Heb 1:6), and the following. God the Father, becoming the beginning and source of the good, becomes the source of those doing good works, and those who are found in doing what is necessary are truly sons of God, partakers of his only-begotten Son. But if those who did not draw near participate in the opposites (and these are the evils), they would be alienated from God, and the growing old would follow. For participating in virtue, in bright and imperishable wisdom and incorruption, they were finding constant renewal; but falling into wickedness, they would be growing old through their own corruption (if indeed it is so), being worn out.

And since the verse is about the Jews, they are not sitting by the oldness of the letter, nor are they falling by quantity, enduring the newness of the spirit, 'Alien sons and having grown old have become'; but they are also said to be double-minded and double-souled, reeling from their many tribulations. For to be double-minded...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The King and Priest Christ
english: To limp, as Elijah says: 'How long will you limp with double inclinations?' (1 Ki 18:21). 'If he is Lord, go after him.' And perhaps everyone who has clung to the divine scripture, not meditating upon it as is necessary, is said to be limping in it, because he has not accepted it, neither walking nor limping in it.

Regarding Ps 17:47a: It is said that God lives, not by taking life but by providing it. And He himself indeed often says concerning Himself, 'I the Living am, says the Lord.' But also the Savior, saying, 'Just as the living Father sent me, and I live through the Father,' demonstrates that he lives not by a participation in life; for He himself is the life, from whom the Son, being consubstantial with the Father, is drawn. For if the Son is life, not by a sharing of life but by himself being life-giving to those who partake of him, and the Father also lives by providing life according to the same manner, the Son being given to the Father by the same energy, the same essence of the Father and Son exists. And this is what the word demonstrates: 'The Father lives,' he says, 'and I live through the Father,' as if he were saying that because of such a Father, he himself, living, exists by essence. He is the living God and is blessed, having blessed the saints with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places (Eph 1:3). It is said that he is blessed if all blessing is in him. For everything said, thought, and spoken or thought blessedly is about him.

Regarding Ps 17:47b: 'The God of my salvation is exalted, having taken my senses to his greatness; for great are his works, and they themselves are great.' Since the salvation of the rational animal is not a small work, it is necessary that the cause of this be great. And God is exalted, not by changing from a lowly place to a high one, but by those having recognized great things concerning him.
Regarding Ps 17:50: For he confesses thanks for this progress and salvation, having taken their sins into himself, becoming an ambassador of their repentance.

For the voice 'I will confess to you' signifies both. For the Son also sings in the name of the Father, doing all things according to the will of the Father. The Father exalts the salvation of the King Christ (Ps 17:51a); it is not that the King himself is saved, but he provides [salvation] to those being saved with him. And God is the King, not as reigning of the God, but of those reclining with God. For when we say ruler of those who are ruling, we mean as a leader of them; but when we say ruler of the king, we mean according to his laws.

The voice of Christ signifies priest and king (Ps 17:51bc). If the word is about David—that is, all who are capable by hand—it shows God showing mercy to practical men, being capable in their activities, and if some of their seed happen to be from the teaching and imitation of his life; then he does mercy to these not for a passing moment or for a little while, but for an age. But if the word is about the true David regarding God ('For I will arise for you a shepherd like my servant David' [1 Sam 2:25/2 Sam 7:12]), he provides eternal mercy to him and to his seed, and his anointing and his priesthood are to be indestructible; for the old priesthood being transferred, the priesthood of Christ is inviolable.

The heavens declare the glory of God (Ps 18:2); and the glory of God is the only-begotten according to the radiance of glory, the order and the supremacy of his kingdom, according to 'And the glory of the Lord shall be seen' [Isa 60:1]. These [the heavens] declare by singing and theologizing, the powers dwelling in the heavens, named homonymously as dwelling in heavens according to the manner of metonymy. And the firmament announces the work of the active powers of God, called his hands, not only by words but by the works themselves (Ps 18:3-5b). Those who are the contemplative...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The distinction between sounds and spiritual words
english: Those grasping life treasure in heaven, having their heart there; the heavens are narrating the previously spoken glory of God through the contemplation of intelligible things. But those who have accepted the practical [aspect] accomplish a firmament through works, that is, they become stable and immovable; they announce the making of the hands of God, working the works of God and through them crying out as works becoming the works of God.

But also the day, that is, the luminous intellect, being not in harmony with another luminous intellect, searches out a word, which is why the Old Scripture says the day is luminous: for God called the light Day (Gen 1:5). This, having been filled with the nourishments of the Spirit, being searched out from the fullness, a word is brought forth in the New Covenant; allegorically also this day is so named.

And the night, the deepest discourse of things, announces knowledge to another such night. For if anyone searches the Spirit who searches all things and has the depths of God, he searches some of the deeper mysteries of God; having known it from this, he proceeds to the similarly obscure, and will come to the knowledge of those.

And the pre-preparations and those making the way forward are mere babblings, but the words were those setting forth the spiritual narratives and fully bringing their faiths demonstratively. The sounds and words for the obedience of God are not, since their voices are not heard as Being. For this reason it has been said by the Lord, so that they might be heard (Matt 25:4): therefore no word of apology is left to those not doing nor thinking; the voices of the previously spoken babblings and words are being narrated. Their sound has gone out into all the earth (Ps 19:4), and the following.

You are a land suitable for seed (Matt 13:23), but you do not receive the sound of the babblings and words, that is, the word according to the sensible [aspect] of the Scripture; but those having surpassed the state of these will receive the words of the babblings and the words, being clearly instructed in all things. Even the precursor of the apostles is not hearing the sound of Jesus but words; 'Words,' he says, 'you have of eternal life'; and the Savior himself: 'The words I have spoken to you are spirit' (John 6:63). For those which he said to the apostles, no longer...
tabernacle of God
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Hidden Sins and Divine Cleansing
english: The Lord's testimony, which testifies through good works and the knowledge of truth, is faithful. It is called faithful not from the act of believing, but from the worthiness of being believed, just as the Word 'Faithful' is said of the Faithful One, and concerning God it is said, 'God is faithful and there is no injustice in him' (1 Cor 10:13) and 'God is faithful through whom you were called' (1 Cor 1:9). For because of worthiness and the being worthy of being believed, it was so named, but also because of the certain and unchangeable nature. Thus indeed the Lord's faithful testimony makes wise those who have turned and become like children according to the will of Jesus.

And it makes wise even the newborn infants, those born through the gospel. Perhaps it also makes wise those little ones who have not been trained by disciplines and with the exercises of human words, but the unlettered and the laypeople. And the commands of the Lord, being outside of all crookedness, are straight, making straight those who receive them, so that they might cast off all sorrow and become in divine joy the soul.

And the fear of God is said to be pure, not a passion that casts one out from perfect love, but the same one that is characterized by piety and divine reverence. It does not work out the state of those who are merely fittingly pure, but it extends even unto the age to come, not being transient and short-lived. The judgments of the Lord are true. He who performs all things according to His own truth and judges, judges truly; as the apostle says: 'For the judgment of God is according to truth upon those practicing such things' (Rom 2:2). God judges according to truth, and the judgments are true—it is said 'true' in contrast to false and unjust judgments.

These true judgments are justified in the same way, whatever may happen, and in the same way it may become. For perhaps if anyone wished to see its truth and justice by itself, he would not clearly see it; for they testify to one another as whatever is, is to be held as testifying. These things, having been foreseen by the one who applied his own mind, are desirable, more precious than those among men. For he who has turned away his own desiring power from gold and precious stones, with longing toward the...

He will consume all of it into truly desirable things, and he will perceive the sweetness of these things more sweetly than the sweetness of a garden and honey in the senses. He will not taste it bodily, but by a divine sense he will perceive the sweetness of the things mentioned before. The servant of the Lord keeps these things. For indeed your servant keeps them; he is not saying this about himself alone, but also about every servant of the Lord. If one turns toward the guarding of these things something temporary and sensible, the recompense is not great; but since the recompense for the guarding of these things is supra-cosmic and supra-heavenly, it follows that it is great.

Everyone is aware of the manifest and effective sins, but the transgressions occurring in secret in the thoughts and reasonings, the one who sees them is rare; for who declares what is rare here? Paul, therefore, not being aware of anything to himself, knowing what is the rare thing to understand the aforementioned transgressions, says, 'Not in this [I am justified]' (cf. Rom 3:28). Furthermore, regarding the transgressions, who will understand? It lies [to say], 'From my secret things cleanse me' (Ps 18:14c). This is said only by the righteous, since defilement occurs in the secret reasonings of the heart, which not only others but I myself am ignorant of; you, remove it, being a knower of those things which happen in secret. For this defilement, if it is not destroyed, becomes an increased starting-point and pretext to be captured by others; sparing your servant, do not let him be captured by others, having cleansed him from the secret things. For the sins occurring in secret, if not being cut off, may at some time pass over into practical sin, through which one might be involved with the things of God or with evil powers. God will spare his own servant, but if he does not spare his own Son, having handed him over above all, it is the loss of the Son for all, and not sparing leads to being [lost] for the salvation of all. And the Son himself will be outside of all harm, not receiving this even by nature.

He says [it is] a great sin, the effective one (Ps 18:15). For if he is not cleansed from my secret things, these transgressions remaining carry over into bad practice, and I become responsible for a great sin. If these...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Beauty of the Savior and the Fulfillment of Prayer
english: If [the words] exist from you, then the words of my mouth are for acceptance; for I have previously prayed to you, praising you and thanking you; and the words of acceptance are worthy. The study of my intellect, occurring in thoughts and notions, is found always before you, free from all reproach. However, the praiseworthy study is not from another but has risen from you, having cleansed me from my secret faults. With you helping, O Lord, I fall not to any who fight against me spiritually. But if, through my inattention, I should be seized by the adversaries, you redeem me from those who have seized me, as you are found to be my helper and redeemer.

The one who is afflicted, making him joyful, is the word that exists in the soul, or the Holy Spirit who awakens him, he says (Ps 19:2–4): 'The Lord will hear you in a day of affliction.' Through progress, the afflicted learns not to be meager nor to cast down hopes, but to pour out [himself] to God through prayers; for prayer leads to hearing God. He does not urge the afflicted to pray in order to appear [pious]; 'The Lord will hear you in a day of affliction, and the name of the God of Jacob will protect you' (Ps 91:15). The presence of God, which has been made to dwell in Jacob, being a shield, is from you. One should seek why, God having enriched Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, the name of the God of Jacob, and not the God of Abraham and Isaac, protects the afflicted. Perhaps it is because, since Jacob has become in many sufferings and hardships as if his life were a symbol of the athletic life, the afflicted, practicing to endure tribulations and contending against them, is protected by the presence of God, which is that of Jacob, so that he, having become a wing-beater because of that, may flutter and strike down the afflictions and the evil spirits working them.

And from a holy [place] the help is sent, that of the heavenly temple (for the temple is called holy among the Hebrews), which is from the holy of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, it is said concerning: 'God from the heights and the Holy One from the strong Pharaoh shall overshadow like a dense cloud' (Ps 89:10). But the explanation will be mastered from the approaching verse. 'For from Zion shall He take hold of you, from there...'

The splendor of the Savior's beauty shines upon the race of men according to 'Out of Zion'. The first reading is understood as 'Out of the heavenly Zion of God'. 'May all your sacrifice be remembered', he prays, signifying this for the one being afflicted: that he will be released from this affliction as if he had offered a sacrifice thankfully, so that God may remember all your sacrifice, which is not such a sacrifice as is being approached, but a spiritual one. 'But also accepting your burnt offering, let it ascend'; it should be noted that a burnt offering differs from a sacrifice. For perhaps the name of sacrifice is laid upon the soulless things brought to the altar, whereas a burnt offering is a living victim.

Ps 19:5: God gives according to the heart of the one praying, whatever such things he requests; and it is proper to give to God, and it is beneficial to the receiver. For the prayer concerning these things, being done rightly, satisfies God. And 'to fulfill all your counsel'; counsel, that is, to fulfill the counsel being done rightly. And a counsel is fulfilled if it does not fail in its intentions, but meets those things about which it was pre-counseled.

Ps 19:6: And this is what is said concerning it: 'Behold, a Savior was born to us, who is Christ the Lord.' It is said that to speak of salvation is to speak of the salvation which is being saved, to whom God hearkens in a day of affliction, in which salvation there will be rejoicing. And 'we shall be magnified in the name of the Lord our God'. Unlike those being magnified in worldly things, we 'shall be magnified in the name of the Lord our God'. 'We shall be magnified' signifies progress in such goodness. For it does not say: 'We are great'. In this way, Isaac, as he went forward, became greater, as he became very great. And someone is magnified in the name of the Lord by performing the work of a genuine and perfect servant. A great encomium regarding that about which the word is: 'all his requests shall be fulfilled by the Lord, asking nothing which God does not provide'. And the fulfillment of requests is to emerge and come into abundance regarding those things for which someone was worthy.

Ps 19:7: The voice of Christ, sometimes upon the priest, sometimes upon the king, and sometimes upon the economy of the Word of God according to the flesh; one will say it was spoken upon David, and another upon Ezekiel regarding...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Crown of Precious Stones
english: The hypothesis of the psalm is taken, and it is spoken regarding the human economy. Perhaps it is also for all those believing, fulfilling the body of Christ according to the teaching that not even Christ is one body, but many members; Christ is said to be saved, and those who have become his body and members may have salvation (1 Cor 12:27). And also to say 'Now I know'—for 'now' means in this present age we know Christ is saving, receiving the earnest of salvation from hereafter.

He hearkens to Christ according to every foretold repayment. And the right hand of God, that is, his Word, makes salvation, not by chance, but with power, like a best general or king. Regarding Ps 19:8, thinking of horses, the skittish powers of passions that ride upon them; and chariots, the concord of the rushing passions prepared against us. But even if not in these things, the unvanquishable defense of us is the approach of God. Regarding Ps 20:2–3, the one established as king upon Zion is truly and certainly king, rejoicing in divine joy from the power of God present to him. And let the whole psalm be interpreted concerning Christ the king and the one co-reigning with him, so that we are not compelled to signify this for every single word.

He does not fulfill the desire of the flesh, but walks by the Spirit (Gal 5:16). One strengthened by the Spirit receives the desire of the heart from God. For he, having abstained from the cravings of the flesh, hungers—that is, the mind hungers—and receives from God, who implants his desire in good things. But even if someone happens to be in need, he was not denied by the Lord because of the prayer of his lips. Regarding Ps 20:4–5, from 'Because you have preceded him in blessings of goodness'—by the causal connection of 'Because,' having used [it], he showed what rejoices and exults in having been preceded in blessings of goodness. And regarding the contrast of blessings, not of goodness...

Here, goodness is set forth; for Jacob, in blessing the sons, will answer the sons in a manner of blessing who have some toil, as their anger is the accursed one. And if such a thing is to be lacking, God foretells a king and his imitator in blessings of goodness, lifting them up to the supra-cosmic promises, which are sent to be a pledge.

One is crowned from his own works and practices. Without doubt, he who has justly pursued the just shall receive the crown of righteousness (2 Tim 4:8), and he who has rightly glorified the Trinity shall bring the incorruptible crown of glory (1 Pet 5:4). And one having been satisfied by the Lord's crown of luxury protects himself, and he being saved by grace receives a crown of graces for his own head.

But also he who has treasured precious stones with gold and silver, from which he worked precious stones, shall be crowned, God restoring to him the head of the soul with the crown of precious stones; and being adorned with divine power in every virtue, he is called, 'All a good stone you have bound.' God crowns not in mercy, but will crown with precious stones a crown made of them, as also in hope he crowns those watching for it; for the Lord Sabaoth is the crown of hope, spread with glory (Isa 66:14).

And since the apostle writes to his own disciples, 'Joy and my crown' (Phil 4:1), perhaps also those who are known to Christ, being precious stones through virtuous character, having placed a crown, will be set upon the head of Christ, as Paul says to the disciples, 'Joy and my crown' (Philem 1:21). He asked life from you and you gave it to him. If the imitator of Christ is the one concerning whom the Word is, God has given eternal life to him who asked life from him; for the gift of God is eternal life (John 6:40). But if he speaks concerning Christ, regarding the one who asked life from him, the Father gave, so that he might vivify the dead (Eph 2:5). Length of days unto the age of ages; toward the life...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Hand of Judgment and the Right Hand of Salvation
english: He asked to have obtained the length of days, so that he might have them immortally and without end. The length of days is received also by the one who has enlightened himself with the light of knowledge, as if he had a doctrine of truth enlightened within him; for each description of thought is a certain day.

The salvation of God acquires great glory for the king raised from the dead and for everyone rising together with him (Ps 20:6-8a). You will lay glory and majesty upon him, this glory which is according to the resurrection. And 'you will lay upon' signifies that even before this glory he had another, according to 'I glorified and again I will glorify.' And majesty is that which is becoming in great things. The becoming in great things has not happened concerning the Savior alone. For what is greater than to raise the dead and to walk upon the sea and his enormous miracles among those nearby? But even from his rising from the dead, the becoming in great things has exceeded for him; for he was taken up into the heavens and sat at the right hand of the Father, 'For you will give him blessing unto the age of ages.' All these things have exceeded for him, that blessing is given to him for the age of ages from the Father, by which he blesses those approaching him; then especially the curse having been turned for our sake, he redeemed us from the curse of the law regarding becoming mortal, through the blessing of Abraham (Gen 12:3). 'Rejoice him in joy before your face' (Ps 16:11). Oh, the same grace and peace are given from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ, the seed from God, such that the same joy from God and from his face comes to be; for the face is the character of his subsistence. And these things shall happen concerning the king, hoping in God the Lord, finding himself being of those who hope. For having approached the expected things through experience, he rejoices before the face of God. And otherwise: since your image is a face, and this is the God the Word, the king becoming with this face makes his temple profitable and, becoming conformed to him, rejoices in joy.

Having received oil from the Most High to be anointed with oil of exultation, he possesses an impassable priesthood from the anointing, according to the order of Melchizedek, a priest unto the age (Ps 20:8b-9). For that he shall not be shaken shows that he will not soon see the worthiness from which he is shaken.

Changing into something else. His hand is not found for a few, but for all the enemies of God, bringing punishments upon them and warring against those set against the divine law, according to 'The Lord fights with a hidden hand against Amalek' (1 Sam 15:30). And perhaps he means by enemies those bringing in thoughtlessness and embracing ungodliness. For if these do not set God before them, the hand would be found distressing them and bringing rebuke upon them, so that then they might know what God stands over of those who sin. He says 'hating God' here regarding those committing sin. For if in keeping the commandments the love of the perfect God is completed, according to 'If anyone loves me, he will keep my word' (John 14:23), he who does not keep the word and the commandments of God hates God. And he who hates thus is said to be perishing. Since there is no expectation of the Savior coming, the right hand of God, to seek and save the lost, it is fittingly said: 'May your right hand bring all who hate you to prosperity' (Ps 20:10).

But by what does the right hand differ according to the writings? One should consider the hand set upon punishments, as 'Your hand has utterly destroyed them' (Ps 6:10), and 'Now having sent the hand, I will strike you' (Ps 77:10) (and indeed 'The hand of the Lord has laid hold of me' [Job 10:1]); but the right hand is upon salvation and other good things; for 'His right hand saved him', and 'He made the right hand of the Lord a power', and 'The right hand of the Lord saved me' (Ps 18:35), and such things. It is fitting, then, that even here he says the hand is found punishing the enemies, but the right hand is found for those who hate [Him], so that they might be found no longer in destruction.

Regarding Ps 20:10a, I think it is meant that they shall be cast upon the enemies; not that anyone is handed over for punishment to be cast as a furnace of fire always and continually, but as at the time of the shining of the divine face. And there also, 'the time' signifies not a duration of time but the kind of state of those capable of receiving the face of God. And I think also that the mention of the furnace was not in vain; for just as a furnace does not burn in vain or by chance, but for some useful purpose in baking bread or something similar, so also God sets punishments at the time to encounter such [people] as may be able to behold His face. Ps 20:10b The...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Face of God and the Morning Perception
english: Those being disturbed by wickedness and false glory, being agitated by the allurements of pleasure, God shall shake in His wrath, and those being disturbed by the expectation of punishment.

But these are not consumed by a fire that is entirely physical, but by that which follows the disease of the soul; rather, when the soul repents for the evils it has done, a penalty of fire pierces it, or when dissatisfaction arises in it, a fire analogous to the diseases of the body is generated.

For just as bodily foods, when consumed beyond what is necessary, having a disease-causing quality, raise fevers in those who have eaten them, so too, from these foods, a fitting fire will follow the wickedness and the worthless doctrines; it consumes them not by destroying their soul's essence (for it is indestructible) but their quality, according to which wood becomes hay, stubble, or weeds, so that when the things that joined them are consumed, the pure essence that was bound remains visible.

And here it is shown not that their essence is perishing, but that they bore fruit badly: 'for your works are weary and worthless' (Ps 20:11). Just as plants bearing perfect fruit project seed from that fulfilled fruit to become plants similar to themselves, so those having borne the seed of teachings in wickedness and impiety are cast down to make others like them, worthless and impious. God destroys this seed from among the sons of men.

'They turned evil toward him' (Ps 20:12) [referring to] the false doctrines concerning Him, attributing the cause of wickedness to Him; and the traitors and enemies of Him, having been proven, turned evil toward the Savior. It should be noted that evil is accomplished by turning aside, and not by straightness, as the good are [seeds].

For all the worthless, having turned aside, act against the incapable; for they deliberate treacherously against the one who will not suffer harm. Perhaps also every evil man, through whom one sins, deliberates a plan that is unable to stand, because wickedness is unstable and not abiding. 'For you will set them low; with the remnant you will prepare their face' (Ps 20:13). God does not turn away; He sets these low, making them capable of being a face. And just as those who do not see the...

The silence of God allows one with a pure heart to contemplate His works and those following Him, so that observing His creation they may grasp His mind, and having cast off weakness to have a pure face, they approach God and give Him the face of God. Therefore he says: 'And in your remnants you prepare their face' (Ps 20:14a), for the remnants of God are those things above His sensible creations.

Since descending with our weakness, you took up something weak, O He who is stronger than men, having been crucified out of weakness, 'Exalt yourself in your power' (Ps 20:14b). It is terrible to take up through contemplation, but to sing is to act according to virtue. Contemplating the intelligible of the powers and acting according to them, we see and sing of your powers, you who ruled as a triumphal king against the devil and the opposing powers. It is also possible to declare the graciousness: we cry out to you, having ruled against death.

Morning perception is made straight by the rising of the sun of righteousness and the making of the beginning of the day; for the rising of the true light has laid an end to the night of ignorance and error and has shone a spiritual illumination. And that which begins toward the end of perfect illumination will arrive, through which all other spiritual things were spiritually completed at the end, not because of all other things, but it itself is nothing, which they also call the last, because no one desires anything above this, this being the ultimate good.

The prophecy of the present psalm points toward the end of the morning perception of David, that is, of him who was born of his seed according to the flesh. And this must be kept: he who guards the face, saying from beginning to end, no single change is found regarding the saying 'face'. And since the New Testament has taken words from the psalm as if spoken by Christ, it is necessary to interpret all of it from the face of Christ. Let us declare the words which the New Testament used, having reached them. It is to be noted that instead of 'calling', 'falling' has been used correctly; instead of...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Nature of Salvation and the Divine Origin of Christ
english: For to say, 'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?'—that God, my God, is what he does in many places in the Scripture (Ps 21:2). He does not wish to say this specifically: that the general and true God, being my God, is encountering me while I am being fought against and experiencing many afflictions; for why have you forsaken me? The voice is inquiring about the cause of the abandonment. Since he possessed a great purity with himself (for sin was not necessary), he did not believe he was being forsaken because of sin, but because of something else that is beneficial to the whole. He does not wish this to become manifest through himself suffering, but through those seeing him; for having known what was forsaken for their sake, they will praise him as Savior.

Therefore, let us speak the words of the transgressions, not the pronunciations concerning the transgressions. For just as we say a word of heaven by which it has become, and a word of the sun by which it has risen, so also we shall say the words of transgressions, and not that the transgressions themselves drew the Savior into his own body. But his body brought these words of transgressions before the passion, and having risen from the dead—he who is also said to have saved—he held the words of the aforementioned sins far from his salvation, having stripped off the ruling principles and powers that work the transgressions, and he triumphed over them in himself, speaking boldly upon the cross.

It is allegorical that the cry 'O how I suffer something' to you, my God, is not only regarding those surrounding him in affliction and darkness at night (Ps 21:3), but also regarding those who are bright and shining, to whom I will again cry 'O how something harmful might come from the snare.' The Savior, confessing these things concerning us, says: 'O how will you hear when I cry to you?' For it is to be read with an undertone: 'And at night I will cry out,' not being considered by me as madness; the ones surrounding him are the dark ones, those darkened by many circumstances, just as he himself says 'Why must I cry out to God?'—is he ignorant? For I know what kind of night-state is around me.
The fathers from whom I am according to the flesh (they are not the patriarchs) have hoped in you, desiring my illumination (Ps 21:5). But having hoped, they did not fail; they were rescued.

For they were delivered and rescued from death and the devil by me. For they themselves, having cried out to you, abstained from the salvation which is through me and from me. For they did not become despondent toward you, hoping; for they abstained from the things of hope and expectation.

Those saying these things are law-learners, being promise-givers, falsely glorifying regarding providence. For the same things would be said by one being struck by Isaiah, and others have suffered for the sake of piety. For we do not say that to be rescued and saved from those standing around as oppressors means to become something outside of them, but to bravely and through toil endure them, so that the mind might not be harmed by the right intention being cast out by the pains. We say, indeed, that the witnesses of the truth, having suffered ten thousand things and having died by tortures, were rescued and were saved from the tribulations; for those having come to be outside of the tribulations through denial were not only not rescued and saved from the temptations, but were also exhausted by them.

For perhaps he who is conceived of seed, having been brought to completion in the womb, having been filled with the time of birth, is thrust forth from that womb to the outside. But the Father alone thrusts the Savior out from the womb of the Virgin, not having been cast into her from the outside by seed, but having been thrust out from her, from the divine offspring. To other men, hoping and expecting the things to come happens after the fulfillment of the word has come to pass with ages. But the child from Mary alone hopes for perfection; for God holds the hope; for he was never born in wickedness, unlike all men who grasp at the good through ignorance and malice. And Isaiah says this: Before he knows good or evil, he disobeys in wickedness to choose the good. Before the becoming-man, Jesus alone possessed intimacy toward the Father; for his Father was God, and he himself was the Son of God. But after becoming flesh, he came forth from the womb having a relationship like the relationship to God. Therefore he says: 'Even if you are always my Father, you are also my God, I will rescue you from the womb of the mother.' When the tribulation is present, God is with him who is...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Body of Christ and the Dissolution of the Soul
english: To provide endurance as if to bring forth the one being afflicted, but in the absence of God, those surrounding him are strong. He does not rejoice, the one saying the psalm, which becomes a type for us humans and teaches us in trials not to pray that such things might happen to him, so that God might be absent, since in the presence of God he would strike down those raising up affliction. For if God were to depart from someone, there would be no helper for that person (Ps 21:13-14).

And if calves and the evil powers working around earthly and bodily things (for this animal is a tiller of the earth), and those presiding over false doctrines through deceptive words and sophisms, they turn out to be fat bulls with horns, being so because of being ostensibly learned and adorned in phrasing. And it is also possible for the Jews, diving into the law from which they find calves, named [as such], to surround the Lord hostily; and Pontius Pilate and if there are others existing in the pride of horned bulls, are striving to enclose him.

The Savior says these things also concerning his own body, the church, seeing men as low-dwellers and working the earth, hostily surrounding his body: 'Many calves have surrounded me.' And setting aside from them the thing awakened to evil and the preparation for affliction, he says: 'They opened their mouth against me like a lion seizing and roaring' (Ps 21:15). For their mouth is opened to seize the deceived; the sophist is the word. Perhaps 'like a lion seizing and roaring' refers to the devil, from whom the good shepherd was torn by two legs and an earlobe, consuming through disobedience the ear of the man of the soul, and through the legs its course. Since those who have believed are the body of Christ, the [things] of those who have believed...

Taking upon himself the suffering, he says these things: it has happened to those who complete his body. Since the sheep did not remain scattered when the shepherd was struck, he says, as Hosea says, 'a gift was poured out' (Hosea 14:7); for the gift having been emptied is scattered. But also concerning the apostles he says, 'All my bones were scattered' (Ps 22:14); for they themselves are his bones because of the good tension and the holding together of the whole body.

Perhaps someone's heart is melting like wax in the midst of the belly (Ps 22:15), and the soul sees those who have suffered labor pains and those bearing calamity born by it. Since, therefore, the things foretold concerning the disciples of Jesus have happened, his heart being divided toward them lovingly, he endured the passion of wax, burning in the midst of the belly, sympathizing with those he bore. But also the sweetness of the heart was like wax that was melting, and the food became and entered into the stomach; for the thoughts of the heart, having been eaten like wax, descended into the belly, melting and thinning through continuous study, in order that the substance of the eaten might be restored.

But also the strength, having been brought into the furnace of life, was dried up like an earthen vessel; for after the experience of tribulations, as one coming out of a furnace, he will receive the dryness of an earthen vessel, no longer being moistened by the moisture of the clay and the flux of pleasures. Of the scattered listeners, no longer being present, the tongue is not active in teaching and conversing, being inactive if it is stuck to the throat; for the one bringing forth a word moves, not being hindered by the sticking to the throat.

'Dust of death' perhaps is to be said, the 'body of death' being named by Paul (2 Cor 4:4); for this is truly fashioned from the earth. And 'dust of death' is said regarding the one who is born and will die. For if the being laid up is to be entwined with the body, it is necessary also that a dissolution take place, which is death.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Soul's Defense against the Sword of the Devil
english: This is not the body which the Savior, having entered into the womb from the Virgin, says, 'You have brought me into the dust of death' (Ps 22:14). Perhaps he also descended into mortality and the Hades, which for us is the dust of death; for it happened in the heart of the earth for three days and three nights. Ps 22:17c–19: 'They pierced my hands and my feet' signifies the death of those coming to this, having their hands and feet dug out through the piercing of the nails. 'All my bones were counted.' All the bones of the body can be counted, if they are stripped of the joined flesh; and regarding the body of Christ, the apostles declare the bones, but his flesh is spoken of by those believing more superficially and more bodily. For the body is not the same thing: the bones hold the flesh together, and the flesh happens to be around the bones, covering them. If some fear should disturb those fleeing, the superficial believers, only the hard and zealous ones are left, as if they were counted [as remaining] having been stripped after the fleeing of the crowd. 'They understood and looked upon me; even though they did not cause my [death] to happen (for I took these things willingly), they divided my garments among themselves and cast lots upon my clothing' (Ps 22:18).

Regarding the history, the words of the Scriptures are more allegorical concerning the garments and the clothing of Jesus; for the God-Word, subsisting according to spiritual meanings, both wears and is surrounded by these. The heterodox, the executioners and the spirits of the slayer, divide the garments of the Savior. For each of them receives the words of the Scriptures, and [receives] those not [of the Scriptures], even though the seamless tunic of Jesus is seamless because it is woven; for it does not consist of joined parts but has a unified nature. And it is also from above because it is divinely inspired, woven through the Spirit; for the Scripture is from above by all power. But the Church does not divide the garments nor casts lots upon them; for she has and puts on, standing at the right hands of Jesus, a Queen clothed in golden attire, variegated. Having ascended above these garments, she will clothe herself with Jesus himself, becoming wise and powerful, possessing the wisdom and power of the Father. Ps 22:20: And doing these things...

Regarding his words: 'Do not withdraw your help from me; for if you do not help and attend to my understanding, I shall rise a third time from the dead to show the vainness of the plot against me' (Ps 21:21a).

Since the surrounding enemies, seeking to kill, possess a sword capable of wounding not the body but the soul, he asks to be saved from these blades, kept unharmed from disturbance and cowardice (Ps 21:21a). For even if our soul has been sufficiently prepared, seeing the devil with the whole phalanx of demons and the swarm of opposing and evil human energies acting through them, it becomes disturbed (for its nature is changeable) and calls upon the One capable of saving from the enemy's sword.
Perhaps even the devil himself is allegorically called a sword, since he dares to wound every soul by pre-meditation; thus, he asks to be saved from this sword.

He does not previously call the dogs surrounding him in the plural, but now calls them in the singular because of their kind (Ps 21:21b). And his soul is called 'only-begotten' because it is isolated and separated from all other souls; for all those there have known sin, but this one has not. And while God the Word visits those others at intervals, this one remains unseparated and indivisible without distinction until the end. Because of these exceptional qualities, he is called his only-begotten.

Perhaps also the glorious church standing before him, having no flaw or wrinkle and being filled by the blameless and perfect, is his only-begotten, though progressing into many ranks divided by the difference in progress: sixty indeed of queens, and eighty of companions and maidens whose number is countless; one of them is a perfect dove above all, an only-begotten one to her mother, the upper Jerusalem.

He asks to be saved now from the devil, previously spoken of as a lion, but also through his own humiliation, by which he humbled himself, becoming obedient to the Father unto death, even the death of the cross (Ps 21:22). And he wishes to be saved also from the horns of the unicorns, which are an opposing power promising a kingdom; for the horn is a symbol of a kingdom. And those who consider the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Two Kinds of Wealth and Prayer
english: To signify a cross from the preceding word, having the shape of a horn (Ps 21:23).

The Epistle to the Hebrews says that this word is spoken from the person of Christ, as he says to the Father: 'O Father, your own name, that is, your own property and peculiarity, I will declare, making it manifest to my brothers who were born of me, to whom you sent my spirit; to whom it will be said, What you are, God sent the spirit of his Son into your hearts. For they are not those who have received the spirit of adoption from God, so as to be sons of God and brothers of the only-begotten. And having indeed risen from the dead, having appeared to the women, he says, "I have gone to my brothers." And in the midst of this gathering assembly, he will sing praise to the Father, sending up theological thoughts and songs.'

In many ways he is called Jacob (for the typology signifies this: when he is the divine man, the son of Isaac, the father of the twelve patriarchs; when he is the twelve-tribed people proceeding from him; when he is the ten tribes alone having split from David and having followed Jeroboam; when he is the savior himself, 'Jacob my servant, I will take hold of him'; 'Israel my chosen one, my soul has received him'; for Matthew wrote this prophecy concerning the Savior), it should be sought why it is said, 'O all the seed of Jacob, glorify him' (Ps 21:24). And one might say: the twelve-tribed seed of the patriarch Jacob, having been immersed in the reading of the law and the prophets, wishes to glorify God also through thoughts and words and good works. But perhaps, since this is a falsehood, many of those descended from Jacob being unfaithful and traitors to Jesus, someone will say: what [is said of] the seed of Jacob the 'plucked-up' and 'beaten-down' by death and the opposing power (and Jesus is that [seed]), his seed who came from teaching, will be able to glorify God. And since Israel is also the one whom the soul of God has received, the chosen seed of his, Israel will fear God. And each of those imitating...

If Jesus has a struggle against the principalities, powers, and rulers of this darkness, Jacob is one who beats back the opponents; but if he has a pure heart and a clear mind, he will see God, Israel being such a person. No seed of such a person will fail to fear God.

Since he did not reject the prayer of me the poor man nor crush it (Ps 21:25), for this reason, becoming thankful that the prayer for us was heard by the Lord, you praised, glorified, and feared him. For even though I prayed to him as a poor man, but you ought to know what I am: a rich man, a treasure of the fullness of goods; through you I became poor so that through my poverty I might make you rich; for those who are surrounded by the flesh did not receive my wealth, knowing and prophesying only a part of it. Having become poor for you, I cried out to the Lord on your behalf, and he heard me, giving you those things by which you were found rich. For in my interceding for you, he did not turn his face away from me, but rather he shone it upon me; therefore he also applied his attention to my cry.

Men indeed praise based on visible works and conveniences, but God, seeing the hidden, praises based on perfect virtue and surpassing knowledge (Ps 21:26a). It is not for anyone to say with boldness: 'O God, my praise is from you, not based on chance things, but on a great assembly'; for a great assembly is the one gathered from the great according to their kind, just as a great assembly is the one gathered from many (Ps 21:26b).

A prayer is a confession made in thanksgiving, if one should obtain these things from God (Ps 21:27). Concerning the two kinds of wealth, as the Scriptures say, to be the one rich in good works and in every word and in all knowledge, and the other to be rich from false-glorious dogmas and unpleasant deeds, being a poverty contrary to each kind of wealth. And he who possesses the divine wealth, being deprived of the worthless, possesses the contrary poverty, yet as a rich man and a poor man, I praise him as being such; just as he who possesses the laborious wealth possesses also the false poverty opposed to the wealth that...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Spiritual Worship of the Poor
english: Concerning those who labor not in a praiseworthy way, the saying 'The poor shall eat and be filled' is spoken. But you say 'the poor' according to the saying, meaning those from the nations who previously had no hope and were atheists in the world, who are coming to faith and shall eat and be filled (Ps 22:28). Remembering God at the ends of the earth and turning from the nations, those who have passed from the earth shall have their citizenship in heaven. And all the families of the nations shall worship before Him.

The Jews also seemed to worship before God coming to Jerusalem and the temple which Solomon built. This typical worship in a place, however, is not what the nations dwelling even unto the ends of the earth are to perform; rather, they were taught to worship in spirit and truth, remaining where they are, performing worship before God, as God wills them to live as citizens. With this, the prophecy also agrees, saying: 'And all the islands of the nations shall worship before Him, every place from its own place,' as Zephaniah says (Zeph 3:9).

Those nourished in the earth can be 'poor of the earth' (Ps 22:27), those who, having been called to repentance in spirit, are killing the deeds of the body so as to no longer think of earthly things, having eaten the spiritual food offered by Jesus, worshipped God in spirit and truth. And it is possible to call 'poor of the earth' those on earth who are departing from worldly wisdom, those becoming rich and ruling sensually; for these, having eaten the food from Jesus, being not a remedy for those foreseeing evils, shall worship God, finding Him above all wisdom, wealth, and rule.

But descending into the earth, if anyone is like those angels descending from heaven to earth and worshipping the Lord and Savior, according to 'Let all the angels of God worship Him' (Ps 97:7); but He stood ready if those receiving common death can descend into the earth, some of whom shall worship the Lord on behalf of them, having become in the lower parts of the earth (Ps 22:30c, 31a). It is good to live one's own soul, but not to serve it, but to serve Him. For the nature received...
by the divinity having taken hold of it
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Table of Spiritual Food
english: It has happened through wandering to sin, but the shepherd turned my soul back to the strayed. It should be noted that no one is bad by nature if they are receptive to returning. One returns to where they began. Since sin has happened to those turning away from God, it should be abolished.

Regarding the shepherd, he says, 'He led me' (Ps 22:3bc), leading forward and making a way so that we may step into it, himself treading the paths, following his own tracks. For if he drives out the sheep, he goes before them, and the sheep follow him. He speaks of righteousness, that by which the practitioners are righteous, and the paths of it are the things performed according to it. Perhaps righteousness is the general virtue, and the paths of it are the specific virtues. Because of this, the one called upon me led me onto the aforementioned paths of righteousness.

When God is with [one], nothing harmful can harm or injure, as the prophet says: 'Behold, the Lord will help me; who will harm me?' (Ps 22:4ab). If indeed one has walked in tribulations and pains, which is called the shadow of death (Ps 22:4c), I will not fear the harmful things, having God with me. The evils here are not the strictly [evil] things, but the painful ones: poverty, sickness, distress, and the like, concerning which Job says: 'We shall not suffer evils' (Job 1:21). For no one having God with himself encounters evils that are the opposite of the strictly good; for sin is far from all that is in union with God.
He speaks of the rod to rebuke and to discipline, according to [the question] 'What do you want? Shall I come to you with a rod?'; and the staff to support through counsel, exhortation, and advice.
In the beginning, we say that the one in the progresses dwells in a place of grass. Since the one progressing reaches even to the end, there is no remaining sheep.

But having been shown to be rational, a table of rational foods has been beautifully prepared by the Lord. For the Lord, being the one who prepared His own table with wisdom, upon which He set the holy sacrifices, says, 'I have prepared a table before me' (Ps 23:5), which is not an inductive and ethical teaching as before, but a mystical one and the contemplation of the truth.

But consider, even if one is, in this life, seeing the truth through a mirror and through an enigma, being a sheep led by a shepherd, having passed over to the coming age, approaching truth face to face, he approaches the spiritual table according to the promise: 'And I will make a covenant with you to eat and drink at the table of the Father in the truth'; therefore, 'I have prepared' is said. For the God prepared from that place—'Eye has not seen and ear has not heard, and it has not ascended into the heart of man' (Ps 22:5)—God prepared for those who love Him.

And 'Before me' indicates that the Table has been made manifest to me and known to me in the presence of those distressing me, many desiring to contend with me and therefore distressing me. The Lord, wishing to establish me strongly against them, prepared a table before me, upon which solid food is set, so that, having been strongly equipped with this, I might be able to stand bravely against those distressing me. For we do not only attain to the good and perfect, but we have strong and many opponents; as the apostle says, 'For a great door is opened to me, and the opponents are many' (1 Cor 16:9).

This is to say, applying the mind lavishly to it; and this is the priestly anointing, the ointment which Aaron bore as a symbol; for he says, 'Like ointment which descends upon the head, upon the beard, the beard of Aaron' (Ps 133:2). Since wisdom prepared not only a table but also mixed her own wine in a bowl, having been made from a true vine, He mixed this...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Cup and the Fullness of the Earth
english: The Holy Spirit, having mixed divine decrees with human words, divides from this vessel a cup to each; and the cup that is strongest for the one is the most precious and exceptional to the one receiving it, for it is said that the Holy Spirit makes this a matter of profit. To the one who has received, He says, 'And my cup' (Ps 23:5). If your cup were to carry such a thought, it would be the cup of you, the Lord, 'whom you have given me to drink' (Ps 23:5). For the aforementioned mixture proposed toward wisdom is not human.

No one reaps such a salvation from works, but from the grace of God being merciful (Ps 22:6a). For God, being rich in mercy, through the great love approaching Him toward men, has made alive in Christ the dead who had come to be through sins and trespasses; therefore the Holy One says: 'And your mercy shall pursue me, always coming and overflowing for me' (Ps 23:6). Not indeed at times or sometimes, but all the days of my life it pursues me (Ps 23:6). And all the days of life are the various illuminations of the truth through which we happen to be made alive, namely the Christ who is present with us through life.
He settles in a place of pasture, and in the house of the Lord he dwells (Ps 22:6b), not for a certain time but all the days of immortal life, being illuminated unceasingly and repeatedly.

The earth has become more mystical of the Lord; how greatly he descended and liberated it from those who tyrannically hold it, the demons, destroying all the deceits being performed upon it: magic, sorcery, the divinations of the demons upon the earth along with the laws concerning idols and sacrifices. But also its fullness is of the Lord, namely all the mortal things dwelling upon it; the fullness of goods He cast upon it according to the Psalm, 'The earth is full of the Lord's mercy, and full of His praise' (Ps 32:9). But also the inhabited world; and this is His church under the sun, apart from those dwelling in it. But this inhabited world is inhabited by those who think and live ecclesiastically. He himself established it upon the seas, and the seas being understood as the many storms and salt-spray of the trials that occur. For then the church receives a foundation and a steadfastness, and the...
Against the onslaught of the three-fold waves
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Lord of Powers and the Pantokrator
english: The inquiry has become directed toward a holy place, not as an answer concerning a single person, but concerning every pure person with clean hands and a pure heart. Therefore, the text also brings forth the generation of those seeking him, instead of saying 'All such are'; and the generation having possessed the virtue of the aforementioned are seeking the Lord. They seek in order to find the face of God, as Jacob, whom they wish to behold, might be improved by the understanding and the illumination of it in some way: 'The light of your face has been signaled to us, Lord' (Ps 23:8–10).

Running forward, divine angels were addressing those standing at the heavenly gates: 'Lift up your gates, O rulers; you are leaders and you are guards.' For just as he, bowing, bent the heaven and did not open it, so having been taken up, he did not enter through opened gates, but through those being lifted up. Since these gates also are spiritual, and the angels say toward them: 'Be lifted up, eternal gates.' But these spiritual gates are not temporary, because they are not bodily, but eternal because of the incorporeal and unblemished nature; yet they say that the gates should be lifted and be lifted up, not so that the glorious ones might enter, but that the King of Glory might enter.

And it is said that the Savior is the King of Glory to rule over all the glorious ones according to God, and as one bringing glory from all and possessing the true and lasting kingdom. Providing this to the worthy, and he is its Lord, it is said according to: 'For if they had known, they would not have crucified the Lord of Glory' (1 Cor 2:8). But since not God the Word alone ascended, but coming forth he was taken up in flesh, being animated by a spiritual soul, the powers above were astonished, asking: 'Who is this King of Glory?' For seeing the one spoken of as the King of Glory surrounding himself with flesh, they marveled.

Again, those running forward said, 'Lord, mighty and powerful,' shouting contrary to this: 'Not the one surrounding himself with a body, but the one having excelled against those who fell from us and having taken on a tyrannical power, the Lord who is mighty in war,' having seen that he had utterly defeated all, to contradict and to wish to stand against [them]. Having heard these things, the rulers along with the eternal gates...

They were not satisfied with doing only what was commanded, but they also stood over the higher powers and the gates of the higher heavens, as they reported, proclaiming the gates of the Most High, your rulers, and so on. And when they were questioned again, the angels answered them, and this was their answer, saying, 'Lord of Powers,' He is the King of Glory. But they call Him 'Lord of Powers' as a commander of armies.

It should be noted that those who have been precise regarding the Hebrews say that the voice of Sabaoth is lying in the Hebrew. The Seventy translate into Greek either 'Lord of Powers,' 'Lord of Armies,' or 'the Pantokrator.' They say, indeed, that in this place where Sabaoth is located, the translation into 'Lord of Powers' has occurred. But if Sabaoth lies concerning the Savior, it is also translated into 'the Pantokrator,' so that it is fitting the voice of the Pantokrator should be attributed to the Savior; for if all things came into being through Him, and He is before all things, and all things consist in Him, and He holds providentially all things having come into being through Him, and He is before all things consisting in Him, it follows that He is called Pantokrator. For it is His face speaking in Zechariah: 'Thus says the Lord of hosts: I have been sent after glory' (Zech 8:2), and 'You shall know what the Lord of hosts has sent me to you' (Zech 8:13). For the Son is the Pantokrator being sent by the Pantokrator, being sent by the Father. And most clearly in the Apocalypse of John, the Savior is called Pantokrator: 'These things says the Lord, the faithful and true witness, the one who was and the one who is and the one who is coming, the Lord God the Pantokrator' (Rev 1:8). For these things have been said about the Son without dispute.

Let me not be put to shame, as those who trust in others are put to shame; for he who trusts in wealth shall not fall (Ps 24:1-3). This is to be said synecdochically concerning all temporal things. For I pray, having trust toward You, not to contend with those who are striving, lest I should be made a laughingstock by the enemies; and my enemies are the devil and the other evil powers and men except the God-fearing. For having learned this through all, I am emboldened, not to be put to shame by all those...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Divine Mercy and the Two Ways
english: Enduring you. Perhaps these things suit the saints before the arrival. They await him and endure his coming descent. For when he has come, the laughter of the enemies will reach its end, those who mocked against those hoping in God.

The [way] through emptiness, the vain and empty, signifies this (Ps 24:3b). Such is that in Proverbs 14:12: 'The way of all those who work iniquity, bringing shame to those who sin in vain'; for they do not perform the things of iniquity toward any perfection like the guardians of the law. The paths of the Lord, his commandments one must speak (Ps 24:4-5). But he also says that one must teach them as paths worn by foot-traffic, so that having trodden the tracks, I may make my course unerring. And since the practical life alone is not sufficient for perfect salvation, so that with this I might also perfect the contemplative [life], 'Guide me pedagogically upon your truth.' And furthermore, according to the place, it will be said: of the law and the prophets, encountering the paths of the Lord, no one else will make them known to the one desiring to be tested by them, who is the Lord himself. For having made known to his paths and having taught the foot-traffic, through having spoken to the fathers in the prophets, 'Guide me upon the one who said: I am the truth' (John 14:6), having spoken in the Son at the end of days. And indeed you, O God, are my savior; for through whom you taught me, you will provide salvation to me.

As the proper energy of light is to illuminate and of knowledge is to know (Ps 24:6), so it is the proper energy of God to have mercy and to show mercy, and 'God and Father of mercies' is said. The saint does not wish to say it is such a thing; being a Father who is a source and beginning of them, [he says] 'Remember these, your offspring.' For even if you were angry for a little while with those who sinned, but the anger is not according to your nature, but having endured usefully in order to stop iniquity, let him cease, taking memory of your mercies which are according to your nature. And we also have become accustomed, being indignant at our own, and to speak to weak men, 'Remember your goodness and imitate yourself, reconciling with those under indignation.' Just as the mercies will stand in reconciliation with God, so also the [mercies]...

His [mercy] according to nature, being present to him, are from the age, therefore they remain unto the age according to 'His mercy is unto the age' (Ps 24:7ab). And to whom does God say, 'With eternal mercy I have had mercy on you'? No one confesses upon those present and actively committing sins, but upon those having ceased and those no longer being [sinners]. This indeed he says even now, asserting, 'Do not remember the sins of my youth and my ignorance.' For those having sinned and acted ignorantly in youth are no longer actively committing them to the one having passed through youth. Perhaps the term 'youth' does not signify age here, but the unstable and uncertain state of that period. For anyone who is in such a condition, he is ignorant and sins, as the Scripture says, 'That I might give cunning to the guileless,' whereas a young child is given perception and understanding. Having deemed it worthy that he should not remember the sins and ignorances of his youth, he immediately brought forward: 'According to your mercy, remember me' (Ps 24:7c). For according to mercy, God remembers; he does not recall the faults. By nature, being merciful and God being good, he possesses kindness by nature; he remembers the one repenting with mercy (Ps 24:8). And he is straight because he is not disposed toward sin, and because he requires the sinners to be straight; therefore, he will legislate for those sinning in the way (Ps 24:8). For he subjects those actively committing evil to law, so that, having been prevented from sinning, they might walk the way of salvation (Ps 24:9).

The God who legislates will guide those having gentleness and stability in judgment—that is, having been examined and scrutinized (Ps 24:9). For having learned the two ways before the face of man, the way of life and the way of death, and having turned away from the way of death and walking the way of life, he walks in judgment, being led by the Lord, because of the calmness and stability of the mind; for the gentle possess tranquility of thoughts. The Lord himself, after having led the gentle in judgment, will teach them and his own ways, which are the ways leading toward him; for he himself travels them; for one traveling behind the Lord learns his ways (Ps 24:10). All the ways leading toward the Lord, he himself walks in the manner having been said (Ps 24:10).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Monogenes and the Guiltless
english: Those things established according to truth and becoming [present] with goodness are mercy and truth. For it is necessary to be shown mercy first, lest anyone fall upon them and, through this, outpace the one traveling upon the truth. But the ways of the Lord are not viewed as mercy and truth by all, but by those seeking His covenant and His testimonies; for he who is outside the covenant and the testimonies is a stranger to the goodness and the beauty of the Lord's ways.

One must seek the covenant which God set forth for the fathers, leading them out of the spiritual Egypt, that is, of the much-willed wandering. For having sought and having searched it, we shall enter into it and also the new covenant which Jesus confirmed with His own eyes; for every covenant is powerless if death has not overtaken the one establishing it, as the apostle says; for a covenant is established upon the dead, lest perhaps the one establishing it were not living. Therefore, to fulfill His own covenant, Jesus, willing, accepted death. And one must seek in the covenant also the testimonies of God, those having testified and having been inspired by Him with words.

For the sake of Your forgiveness, O Lord, I, Your servant, will seek Your covenant, expecting freedom from it and the inheritance which You appointed as if I had become a son (Ps 24:11). But also, be propitiated toward my sin, not toward the sin being worked, but toward it being ceased. For the required purity is great, not according to quantity but according to the comparison of that which is owed to be offered.

He who fears God is indeed rare, but is not unfindable (Ps 24:12). By this, the Lord does not legislate a way which He Himself preferred, but the one who fears Him. The soul of the devout, if it does not go further into the good things, is satisfied in them, always working them (Ps 24:13). Therefore, the seed will generally obtain the inheritance of the land, not the one under the feet, but that of the gentle ones (Ps 24:16b–20). His only-begotten self...

He says according to the one saying: 'I also was left alone, and they seek my soul.' Therefore also I am poor, for I do not have the support of those of the same mind. And it is to be known what the 'monogenes' means: the only, just as you would say the only sun; it is not the same as the 'monogenes' Son. For what pertains to the monogenes Son, the only-begotten from the Father, is said to be the only one from Him.

And you will perceive the tribulations of the heart and those driving through with opposing thoughts. 'Bring me out of my necessities' (Ps 25:1); from those surrounding, forcing and necessitating the departure of my intention, just as 'bring me out of great necessities' (Ps 25:1). One, having taken the perceptions of his own sins, humbling himself because of the lack of boldness and suffering because of the fruits of repentance, says: 'See my humiliation and my labor, and forgive all my sins' (Ps 25:7).

When someone ceases to have previously been active in sins, he will hate the demons who are active in them. And indeed many, becoming against the one being plotted against, hate him unjustly; but unjust hatred is that which happens against those doing things not worthy of hatred, [while] justly hating the evil things. 'Preserve the soul, lest it fall to those who hate unjustly' (Ps 24:21); but also to rescue it from deeds such as those which they will be able to hold onto.

'Guiltless' he says, either referring to those being deprived of malice or the more simple, and 'upright' to those having accomplished perfect virtue. 'Not clinging to me (through unanimity), what I endured, O Lord' (Ps 25:2). Perhaps also 'guiltless' refers to the diligent among men, and 'upright' to the divine angels clinging to Him and becoming of divine powers concerning the diligent. 'No one sins and wishes to be judged for those things which he has done, and especially before Him who sees the hidden things' (Ps 25:11). And he who has walked in guiltlessness, that is, having progressed, is worthy to obtain this; for he shall not receive a wage of inheritance, but upon the Lord...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Tabernacle, Divine Protection, and the One Thing
english: Hoping, I shall not be weak; for I am contained by the hope toward God, being strengthened by it, I shall not be weak. Scripture is carried forth saying: 'I shall not be shaken.' And through this it is not made manifest: because the hope toward God provides for me something firm and immovable, 'Hoping in the Lord, I shall not be shaken' (Ps 25:2).

Since it is not the one recommending himself who is proven, but the Lord establishes, having testified to himself that one should walk in integrity and desiring that one should not be weak, [he] wants [one] to be tested and tried by struggles, so that the righteous may be revealed, and [one] may be tried so that, having received a trial, he might have endurance that is proven. And previously, having an analogy between the kidneys and the heart, it is said. That these two things should be purified through painful struggle, so that they might be shown as proven gold (Ps 25:3).

I would not have been worthy to suffer the aforementioned painful things, unless your mercy had considered me, coinciding with me so as to enable me to endure them. Your mercy, which has been seen by me in front of my eyes, works together to please in your truth; for God's mercy makes one please according to truth and not by affectation (Ps 25:6,7).

One washes the practical powers of the soul, called hands tropically, in innocence, doing nothing trivial but something significant in them. Perhaps also the one who stains them in the work of evils washes and cleanses them, using good works instead of water. Having become outside of all the aforementioned evils and having washed my hands in innocence, I shall surround with the justice of an innocent priest the spiritual altar of the Lord, upon which someone offers up spiritual sacrifices, namely the pure prayers or the lawful acts. To have heard the voice of angels, souls, and spirits of the righteous praising you, to have become around the altar, to have washed my hands in innocence and to have abstained from all those leading astray, but also to perform the narrating of all your wonders in a vast and paradoxical way (Ps 25:8,9).

He who loves the Lord from his whole soul and all the things of God, to whom also the decency of his house belongs, loves; and the decency of God's house is the truth of the dogmas and the command of the canons of the church, being considered his house. Toward these...

And he says that even the tabernacle of the glory of God is loved. Perhaps the tent of witness which Moses constructed in the wilderness is the tabernacle of the glory of God; this is a symbol of progress. But that which Solomon built after the journey to Jerusalem is the temple, bearing a type of the beauty of perfection.

However, he does not wish for the ungodly to possess it, lest his soul be destroyed along with them; for one possessing a pious intention will not be persuaded by this. He also exhorts [one] not to become a murderer, so that his life may not be destroyed along with men of blood; for in the practice of these things there is injustice and total wickedness.

Even if he is conscious of the most beautiful things foretold to him, fearing [to sin], he is not justified by this alone, through many hidden sins; he deserves to be redeemed and to receive mercy (Ps 25:11b). God our Savior is the one rescuing us from sins and from death, and a light that dissolves the darkness of wickedness and ignorance, and illuminating with the light of knowledge (Ps 26:1bc). He who has thus been united and enlightened by the Lord, whom shall he fear? For no one is able to harm such good ones who have attained security. The Lord is the defender of my life; from whom shall I dread? (Ps 26:3,4). These things shall be said, and concerning perceptible enemies and concerning a phalanx of invisible enemies; for if he says, 'war rises up against me,' in this heart which does not fear them, I hope, having become bold, in a God who fights for me. It is also requested and sought to dwell in the house of the Lord, that is, in the church, through thinking on ecclesiastical matters all the days of his enlightened life. 'One thing I asked, which I sought: to dwell on earth, even if I should find many good things, I beseech you, before all things I asked this one thing, to dwell in the house of the Lord (Ps 27:2) in order, and not in confusion, in all the good things that become [one];' perhaps the 'One thing I asked' is to be heard as the exceptional or the great. Since he also says in the beforehand that he has loved the beauty...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Sacrifice of Victory and the Seeking of the Face
english: Regarding the dwelling of the Lord, he who desires to behold this rejoices in becoming a dwelling, approaching it closely and genuinely, not only approaching but also surpassing, as if the Lord visits and surrounds his temple, perhaps not even wishing to depart, imitating Samuel. He who simply, having grasped the established dogmas of the church, beholds the delight of the Lord, differs from one who approaches the Lord by surrounding his temple regarding the Trinity (Ps 26:5,6).
