translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Danger of Listening to Sophists
english: For they say that it is not possible to be in my flesh, because my soul has been played with by the mockeries of the present; for the flesh, flowing and lacking self-control, is very weak, and so he who commits fornication in the body sins (Ps 37:9b,10).

From the depth of repentance, bringing forth groans through repentance, not from superficiality or pretension like the hypocrites of repentance; therefore also, daring, he says: 'To you, Lord, as truly the desire of my heart is before you' (Ps 37:9b,10); for indeed all the vile impulse is far from you and is hidden from you, but the desire of my heart, desiring to pass from wickedness into genuine virtue, possesses a good desire, which one does not find in dreams. He may also speak concerning the vile desire: since the vile impulse lying within me has not eluded you, confessing concerning this I groan, as if the groan concerning it, being bold, would not be hidden from you; for it is praiseworthy to groan over evils (Ps 37:11–13).

Of my heart—that is, of my intellectual power—undergoing turmoil, my strength according to common understandings has abandoned me, but also the knowledge of the truths, the light of my eyes—that is, being the mind—is not with me; for having determined according to reason, I will not be able to conceive clearly or to think strongly. There may be strength in him saying this, and the light of his eyes is the right reason according to which it is rational. The right reason did not abandon him, and it no longer seems to be with him, the strength of the heart being called so according to the guidance of the practical [sciences], and the light of the eyes according to the illuminating by the clarity of those seeing.

And he lived, he says, loving friends and neighbors, having found these standing warily and as enemies, having rushed to turn away from evil and to do the good. But also they were previously near me in relationship and disposition, from afar enemies...

One should speak thus: if anyone falls by various circumstances, he is abandoned by all those who were previously near him, both friends and neighbors, just as he is also accused by the one he formerly loved. These images are found in Job. And those who, seeking my soul harmfully and through strife, came forward and wished to surround me with violence, thought they were leading me down with coercive words as if they were proofs; but they hurried to subject me to the investigation of evils, through which vanity spoke to me. For the argument was not as a proof, but as a vain and deceptive sophistry. And the vanity through which they sophistically argue all day long, that is, through life, they practice deceit, not bringing proofs to the things, but deciding to seize [the mind] sophistically.

He who judges to guard himself will be deafened, not receiving vain hearing toward the deceitful and deceptive words, not wishing to have their sense from hearing (Ps 37:14-15); and much more, he would not wish to answer or to refute such words, like a senseless person. For it is said in other places that it is foolish to refute very gentle words. 'I became, he says, toward such men as if not hearing and not having reproaches in my mouth.' For there is much danger in hearing defamatory words and in conversing about proposed problems [which lead to] punishment. Therefore, it is blessed to be deaf to such things and to be considered as if one were not refuting them.

Since, having despised all others, I hoped in you alone, O Lord, and You being God, will hear me; having prayed, I began, O Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger (Ps 37:16). For often those who associate with me, even if they sinned, bring the past deeds as insults, as if through this to hinder my repentance.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The struggle of the repentant against the accuser
english: Having been tested and having experienced the despair of salvation, I myself am being subjected to such thoughts, being deaf and unable to hear, not wishing to refute them, lest by being found guilty of this, I should lose the brief readiness for repentance. For, O Lord, not hoping, I do not dare to assume I will be heard. For, being unable to defend myself, I endure the defense, knowing: 'Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but leave room for the wrath, for it is written, Vengeance is mine, I will repay, says the Lord' (Ps 37:8).

I am ready and well-disposed toward the lashes of the senses. Indeed, even my pain, through which I suffer for past deeds, is before me, wounding and scourging me. And it can be so; since my pain is such that, while I suffer for the evils I have done, it is necessary to receive lashes besides the sins, I am ready for these, that is, I am ready to be struck for the sake of returning.

The clear sympathy toward us is the memory of the one's own suffering throughout. For, as Paul says, since he himself has suffered, he is able to help those being tempted. Just as according to the law, he who commits sin was mindful of those being offered as a sacrifice for it, so it is to care for one's own sin, hurrying to make the work of repentance right.

While I care for my own sin, those who hate me because I have repented live according to the bad life, being strong and powerful to make me weak according to this life. If even they cast me off as a dead thing to be loathed, but You cover me under Your mighty hand; for when You are present, the enemies are weak and feeble.

Since I am surrounded by enemies, both evil men and invisible powers, I need help; I do not require help from another, but from You, Lord; for You also are found to be the God of my salvation, and the cause of this salvation is God.
King David, having brought the ark of God into Jerusalem, arranged certain men as singers for its liturgy and order, so that the hymns of God might be [heard].

Regarding these, even Jeduthun, as in the list and numbering of the previously mentioned songs in the Chronicles, carries something like this. He who composed the present psalm himself on behalf of David, or having received it from David, proclaimed it. And in the present psalm, the one proclaiming is introduced from repentance into virtue.

Since almost every beginning of sin occurs through speech, he intending to guard his ways through actions sets covenants with himself, so that he might not sin with the tongue. For if the sinless state regarding speech is kept by him, the cleansing from sins according to action will follow; 'For by your words you shall be justified,' he says, 'and by your words you shall be condemned' (Ps 38:2ab); and 'Amen I say to you: regarding every idle word you shall give an account on the day of judgment' (Ps 38:2c).

After the verse, the sinner and there the devil and the evil angel present with the man are called. If anyone, intending to guard his ways for himself so as not to sin in tongue, sets a guard for his mouth, the sinner, representing himself as such in opposition to the one repenting, reminds him of former things, bringing them into the midst as a reproach, wishing to mock through the reminder, so as to drag back into the former sin the one who has turned away from it.

Not so, he says, the one standing as a sinner before me, I was struck dumb toward the words from which I began to speak good things; for having begun not to speak concerning sinlessness, having understood from good doctrines what one must not answer toward provoking words, I was silent, having said nothing to them, so as, the one saying the aforementioned things, not the pain, but having been freed from sins through sense, being renewed and made new, having been pained again by those whom he reproached, saying the things done to me (Ps 38:4ab).

From the words of the one standing as a sinner before me, my heart was heated, being consumed by fire. But since I said nothing from such thoughts within me, the heating was guarded, and 'In my meditation fire shall be burned' (Ps 38:4c). He who meditates on the divine things not casually but earnestly and with fire will say the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Participation in the Image and Divine Discipline
english: With the verse set before him, the fire of such study consumes the pre-existing exhaustion.

Regarding the sinner he says: 'I was deaf and humbled and was silent' (Ps 38:4c); but regarding God: 'I spoke in my tongue' (Ps 38:4c). He who brings forth words in his own tongue from genuine desire and intention is different from him who speaks deceitfully in a foreign tongue. And since we have a tongue even within the human being, which is strictly our own tongue, by which it is possible to speak from a disposition.

Since I have begun to live according to human life and expect its end, this is not clear to me; make known to me my end, so that having learned the multitude of the years of life in the flesh, I may know whom I must aim for (Ps 38:5). What have I accomplished, and what is lacking to me for the completion of perfection? And so it is: since every wise man acts and works toward a certain perfection and goal, it is necessary to have knowledge of this, to know what the end is set for living and what is the number of the days according to the decrees of truth. For one is not wise if he does not know what he lacks for the fulfillment of the goal; just as one intending to take up a certain science asks the teacher: 'Show me how many the decrees of the science are, so that I may know which they are, and by which I lack the peak.'

Having passed from life into the struggle, I was enrolled to contend, as at the beginning having the wrestling match against blood and flesh, but having surpassed the child and becoming a man, I am at the beginning against the rulers of the powers of this darkness, so that the struggle may be mine (Ps 38:6ab). This signifies that the Wrestler is the same as 'In the struggle, set my days' (Ps 38:6ab). Now it is possible for Substance to be said instead of Essence, such that the saying is this: my existence, being compared to yours, does not seem to be anything.

Another scripture contains: 'Behold, you have set my days of old, having a familiarity toward the old man whom I clothed' (Ps 38:6). Therefore also my substance, by which I existed in things prior to faith, is that nothing is before you except all things are vanity. All things on the earth—animals, plants, and the like—say all is vanity. Man alone living...

By these things, he is a participant in immortal life. As Psalm 38:7 says, he who, as he progresses, is being led through an image, makes this his work, being one conformed to the image of the Son of God.

But indeed every man lives being led through an image, either through that of God, observing what is according to the image, or through that of some other animal, becoming female or irrational according to its nature. And indeed the sensible and apparent world is an image of the intelligible and invisible. Man is not led through this world, which is an image, by his own will.

Having said these things concerning the common man, he says concerning each individual that they are in vain, being tossed about in the strivings concerning mortal things. For regarding each one, he says, 'He stores up and does not know for whom he gathers them' (Ps 38:8). For the one storing up upon the earth does not know who will inherit the wealth for which he himself labored; but the one storing up in heaven, having stored up for himself and not for another, knows the wealth that is inexpressible and unremovable from him.

If essence is said instead of substance, it is also from God as from a Creator; just as we exist, so this substance of ours is from Him, imparting to us the existence of things happening by necessity. Since, having hoped to be delivered from all my iniquities, I have not attained this (Ps 38:11), the fool reproaches, as if holding your handiwork in his hand: 'From the strength of the power of your hand I have been cut off' (Ps 38:12). For if the striking hand lashes strongly, the one being lashed is cut off by such a thing.

And from the present word we learn that the things being said are not other than the lashes of God, not rebuking [us]. For after saying, 'Remove your lashes from me,' they have come to be in reproofs concerning iniquity. For man is disciplined by reproofs offered concerning iniquity, his soul having been stretched out to cast away all fleshy thickness. Then indeed he is able to weave according to the spider, not having matter lying outside him, but bringing forth this from where and from himself. The word is able also to make manifest the unsubstantial nature of the evil thoughts of the soul, just as it is said in Isaiah concerning the sinners, 'They weave a spider's web' (Isa 59:5).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: True Madness vs False Divination and the Fulfillment of Sacrifice
english: Let the spider-like webs of the reproaches against lawlessness be destroyed; the soul of the one reproached is spun like a spider's web (Ps 38:13-14).

Since he is not himself asking for much, he prays that he might be granted something to spend his life in, so that he might find refreshment after being worn out by perfect goods. For if he departs not as he should but as one lacking, he shall no longer exist—not in the sense of being destroyed into non-existence (for the soul is both immortal and indestructible), but in the sense of no longer being in participation of Being. For this is what truly is being: to participate in the One who says, 'I am the Being,' meaning that those not having this participation do not exist according to what was said in prayer to God: 'Do not give your scepter to those who are not' (Ps 39:3ab). Longing to participate in this existence, he prays that time might be given to him to find refreshment in the participation of Being, so that he may truly exist.

He calls idolatry a pit of misery, as those drawing from it are being miserable; for they draw nothing from that which is useful for life, just as Jeremiah, reproaching the Jews, said: 'They have dug for themselves broken pits, in which no water can be held' (Jer 2:13). Pleasures are a mud of clay, since they are dust and corruption of bodies and mere pits; whereas on the other hand, Christ saved the mortals through the faith in him and through the preaching.

Those who think that nothing is made manifest in the Scripture apart from the Word say: 'As one having attained a small good, he set the feet of the body upon the sensible rock, and thus he thanks the one who gifted this.' But we say that he who, having been freed from the aforementioned pit and mud, has been established upon the unshakeable and immovable perfection according to virtue, proclaims the things to come; for he follows the one standing on the rock, and his steps are directed by the passing Lord from evil to virtue and from mortal things to immortal things, and indeed according to every progress (Ps 39:4ab).

It is fitting that the moral discourse is new by the novelty of the spirit, and perhaps even new by Aisma, while theology is a hymn. He says that life's pursuits are to be called vanity, and false teachings and false prophecies are to be called madness. It should be noted, however, that as...
He added 'false' to 'madnesses' in contrast to true madnesses; for perhaps those seized prophetically possess a true madness, while false diviners possess a false madness.

Regarding Ps 39:6b, he speaks of the thoughts of God, meaning the deliberations occurring according to God's providence. To these, he says, no created thing shall be found resembling the mind of the Lord which knows all. Regarding Ps 39:6c, 'Your wonderful works and your thoughts'; for if anyone wished to examine something regarding depth, he would find it even more obscure than before: 'If I said, I will act wisely, but it has escaped from me far away, and a deep depth, who can find it?'

Regarding Ps 39:7, the Epistle to the Hebrews says that these upcoming verses are spoken from the face of the Savior concerning the Savior: 'Therefore, entering into the world, you said, a sacrifice and an offering you did not desire,' and the rest. This provided an occasion for him to speak the whole psalm, maintaining the same person until the end of what is said. Now, having passed the time of the shadow, according to which sacrifice and offering were brought, God, not wishing for worship through these things, perfected a body from the Virgin for the Son, so that whole burnt offerings and [sacrifices] concerning sin would no longer be pleasing. When the Savior said to the Father, 'Behold, I have come to do your will,' according to the will by which He [removes] the sin of the world, He himself, having been taken and brought forward for the sin of all, so that once remission has occurred, there is no longer a need for the sacrifice concerning sins.

Regarding Ps 39:8b-9a, he says the heading of the book calls all the God-breathed writing both legal and prophetic: 'For in this it is written concerning the coming conduct of the Savior.' And it is a heading because it summarizes all into one. And it is the becoming of the Savior a man, so that the will of the Lord might be done. It should be noted, however, that the concurrent will is something else, standing as a different will from the deliberative hypostasis which is of the one Willing.
Regarding Ps 39:9b, 'You have written it upon my leading principle.' And everyone who does according to the spiritual law has the law in his heart, that is, in his own disposition.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Repentance and the Care of God
english: Regarding Psalm 39:10, 11a: A great assembly is being filled from many and perfect ones. In this, the righteousness established through the faith of Jesus is being preached. Proclaiming this unceasingly and continuously, he says: 'My lips I shall by no means restrain.' He himself says: 'I knew my righteousness, having accepted this and being at home in it.'

Regarding Psalm 39:11c: He speaks of a great gathering collected from all nations, in which he says he is proclaiming the lion of God and the truth with boldness, saying these things are not hidden. Perhaps he proclaims the lion by declaring the forgiveness of sins occurring according to the lion, and the truth by being set in opposition to the shadow.

Regarding Psalm 39:12, 13: While I am doing the things foretold, You, O Lord, do not let Your mercies be far from me; have mercy on those who benefit through me. For the greater part of salvation does not arise solely from the working of God's mercy, but also the truth, taking hold, preserves [one] lest they be caught in a deception or some other error. For lawlessnesses pursue the judgment of enemies against the one fleeing them; if they do not grasp [them], the visual power of the soul is hindered so as not to be able to see the one catching [them]. Perhaps the lawlessnesses are being pursued by the evil powers working them. And they have multiplied beyond the hairs of my head; that is, the evils surrounding us are multiplying unperceived. With these many things having happened, being deprived of thinking rightly, we have been left abandoned from the heart.

Regarding Psalm 39:15, 16: Since the psalm is single-personed and is said of Christ, it must be said that those who have only the body saying, 'You used the Body for me, what also the soul confesses to have sought,' are lost—those who wrongly think this, praying lest they also be ashamed and fall into error. Just as those hurrying toward virtue have a command not to turn to the rear (for this is destruction), so the...

As evils rush upon them, let them hasten to turn back to the things behind, setting aside the bad intention; for then they are able to be shamed even in the sense of perception. Let those saying to me 'Well indeed, well indeed' immediately bring upon themselves shame. He who accepts sinlessness desires that no one should come into sin. But if anyone should go astray, 'well indeed', how he is immediately shamed for the bad and arrogant things he is doing, saying 'Well indeed, well indeed' (Ps 39:17, 18a).

Those seeking the Lord have an end to the seeking, which is to find him; and upon having found him, they rejoice and are glad with rejoicings and gladness. For someone having sought and having found God, and desiring to magnify him, wants to love the salvation of God, either the salvation from him or the Savior himself. And he loves [him] through all things and not for a little while. Toward the possession of good things, having confessed himself to God as weak, poor, and needy, he entrusts the care concerning himself to God, casting his care upon the Lord as upon a guardian (Ps 40:2b).

An evil day is the day of judgment, in which the God who pitied may pity the one pitied, and he is saved from every punishment; and perhaps even the whole existing life is an evil day, in which the Lord himself saves from those standing around (Ps 40:2b, 3a). Let the evil day and the day of punishment be understood. But he says 'to live' [him] the true life in the land of the gentle (Ps 40:3b, 4).

And he who is prevented from being delivered into the hands of his enemies is such as these, namely the souls of the enemies. And he will add to the one who understands concerning the poor and the needy, and these things following: 'For the Lord will help him at his bed of pain, and will turn his whole bed in his sickness, delivering him from human sickness, also granting him the health of the soul, even if there should happen to him some sickness of the soul (of which many things happen, as the apostle teaches, saying: 'Because of this among you...')
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Thirst of the Soul and the Divine Springs
english: the standing of the apostles

Having come to be. Ps 40:14 Blessed indeed is the one whom the Lord blesses, and blessed means that which is worthy of being blessed eternally. Since the one is being blessed by the God of Israel, the 'may it become' prays 'may it become'; not that the prayer makes God blessed, just as neither the name of God is sanctified by the prayer of those saying, 'Hallowed be thy name.' This was said concerning these things in the previous parts.

Ps 41:1 But the three sons of Kore were arranged with others to sing the awesome psalms, which the Scripture also calls hymns, in which also the names are carried in Chronicles. So not the three, being equipped with the same mind and the same judgment, having been united in that which agrees concerning all things, in a unified way pronounce all things in the present psalm.

Ps 41:2a The deer, a creature warring against the eyes and eating them, if ever, having eaten, were to burn from the approaching venom of the serpent, seeks with haste the springs of water to quench the thirst. But those saying that she who wishes to see herself in the waters traces the springs, so that she might know the pollution having happened to her from the blood of the eyes, so that she might cleanse it; for in the scattering of the eyes, they sprinkle the divine blood into it. And the holy one, not lifting up the eyes against serpents and scorpions by which he received authority from Jesus, but also avenging every disobedience, being a spiritual deer, hastens to track out divine springs of water, since the God says, 'You abandoned me, a spring of living water' (Jer 2:13), and concerning the savior it is said to someone, 'You abandoned the spring of wisdom' (Prov 5:2), and the Holy Spirit concerning whom the Word announced, 'I will cause him to drink from the water, I will give to him; there shall be made in him a spring of water springing up unto eternal life' (John 4:14). Perhaps also every inspired Scripture proves to be a saving spring.

Ps 41:3 The intention of the diligent toward God is like that of the deer toward the springs of water with longing. And since they, in the present life, through a mirror, present him to God, having the face to face set aside for the things after this, pray that a time may be established through which, having come, he might appear before the face of God. And it is: since a shadow...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Sea of Life and the Mercy of God
english: As it is said that the law contains the things of the future, the festivals according to the flesh were seen as shadows and symbols of future festivals; one prays to come into the spiritual festivals, so that the face of God may be seen perfectly, being nothing other than the icon of the invisible God.

He who does not toil in vain with tears but from a disposition for the sake of virtue, his own tears shall be fed as a just reward; he calls the day not only in the bearable circumstances but also names the night in the accidental circumstances (Ps 41:4a-b). Those deceived in all things stumble, and concerning the thinking that God is in a place; mocking indeed they say, 'Where is your God?' (Ps 41:4b-5a). For after this desire, you comforted my spirit and the being mocked by those holding me as if there were no helper; and besides these, the memory of the things being performed in those places is for my healing. And 'These things I remembered, and I poured out my soul' instead of 'From despondency I was dissolving' (Ps 41:5a).

Since I am progressing and not yet perfect, and the tabernacle is a symbol of progress as it is often said, for this reason I am troubled; but the tabernacle according to God wonderfully bears upon His own dwelling, that is, the perfection through which we dwell in God (Ps 41:5bc). I shall pass through a wonderful place of tabernacling, as the dwelling of God, in a voice of rejoicing and holy confession according to the manner of those celebrating spiritually; for those celebrating spiritually hear themselves rejoicing and confessing (Ps 41:5bc).

If I were in the land of the Jordan, that is, if I were made worthy of the holy baptism, I will remember your victories (Ps 41:7b). And they also interpret 'Hermon' as the way of the lamp, as the holy baptism opening for them a way of light and radiance into the mind and heart.

The deepest words about Him are the waterfalls of God, or the divine prophets (Ps 41:8). The teaching of this Jesus calls upon the abyss, calling upon the abyss from the Old Scripture. Perhaps also, since the judgments of God are a great abyss, it is presented what is said of the judgments of others as judgments, and even those of all others are from the word of God, which is said to be a small stream (Ps 41:8).

Having the cause; for the God Word is a great sea, but a small sea through which he voluntarily remained in a state of emptying for our sake. All your billows and your waves have passed over me. The sea, which is tropical to human life, not shipwrecked in it but sailing uprightly, having experienced storms and the swellings from the winter of the sea, having arrived at the harbor of salvation, will say the verse: 'For they did not pass over me, but they passed over' (Ps 41:9a).

We have all deeply sought God manifestly as merciful, but not all of us see how he shows mercy; for often, those things occurring according to his mercy, those experiencing them painfully and not sweetly, we think they are not mercy. But he who has deeply sought, whatever God brings, he brings advantageously, that one will not say such a thing as 'Why have you forgotten me?' (Ps 41:10), unless he is discussing his own repentance.

As a dejected one goes gloomily, I inquire what the cause of this is, whether it is from myself or if I shall lift it up through repentance. For we have all deeply sought God manifestly as merciful, even if not all of us see how he shows mercy; for often, those things occurring according to his mercy, those experiencing them painfully and not sweetly, we think they are not mercy, and because of this we say: 'Why have you forgotten me?' (Ps 41:11). The one who has deeply sought, whatever God brings, he brings advantageously, and he will not say such a thing, unless he is discussing his own repentance (Ps 41:12).

Through the advancing bones of the soul, its pleasant doctrines and powers are said to be. Since it often happens to be crushed by terrible sophists, the deceivers reproach, not saying 'Where is your God upon whom you prosper?', but saying to his wisdom that it has been educated, and also concerning this suffering he reasons with his own soul, saying 'Why are you dejected? (Ps 42:5/11) For you hoped to confess upon the Lord; for certainly his face will shine upon you (Ps 42:6/12)', nothing other than the truth, as you are able to loose the deceits of those crushing your set-before bones through the truth from God. If the Lord's face is this, saying: 'But a nation not...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Ears of the Saints and the Horns of Strength
english: not righteous

They are not [the ears of God] but the ears of men themselves, just as musicians are said to be men. Musical instructions are heard by the ears of musical men. Therefore, when they say 'to our ears' (Ps 43:11), they are not saying it for any other reason but by distinguishing the common things, they say 'to our ears.' The command 'let the one who hears, let him hear' agrees with this.

Our fathers announced to us; those fathers according to instruction announced the divine things, and the ancestors announced what was done through them. 'Your hand has destroyed and planted them' (Ps 43:3b). Regarding the thought of Israel, after the betraying of the Savior from the hand of God, those from the nations, having been destroyed, were planted by divine instruction in the God-breathed writings. God, having maltreated the people of the circumcision, cast them out from the holy training of the law. But the ones from the nations, having conquered not by a law of war, inherited the land spoken of as peaceful. Nor did their own arm save them, that is, their own work. For they have obtained salvation by grace under your right hand and the arm, that is, of the only-begotten Son. 'And the light that finds your face is illumination' (Ps 43:5b); what you have been pleased to save in them by grace, not by their work, so that they should not boast.

The salvation of Jacob, which shakes off the worthless things, is commanded by God to the holy spirits sent for ministry, for those intending to inherit salvation, so that they may quickly arrive at understanding and give help through themselves. Just as God has granted a horn of protection to certain irrational animals so that they may escape those able to harm them, so the horns of Jesus are powers for the saints, goring their enemies. Therefore, also all animals using horns are considered clean, and the food is brought up upon the divine altar.

'God has turned away from himself' (Ps 43:10), not entirely because of sin, but also because of other things for which He is not the cause. And not everyone turning toward the things behind experiences this; for if someone, leaving the worthless things, flees far away by withdrawing from them, not everyone having turned toward the things behind has left what he left behind.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Allegorical and Tropological Interpretations of Psalm 43
english: One falls into destruction. If someone, having left Zion, that is to say, virtue, rushes toward the evil called Babylon, turning back to the things behind, he receives a blessed thing; but those saying the things set forth, since they have become among the enemies, having turned back to the things behind, fell into filth (Ps 43:12).

Those saying these things are like certain sons who, similarly to a sheep being led to slaughter, are given to be food for those approaching them for their own benefit with words and life; but even among the Gentiles they were scattered by God, sowing the seed like farming, so as to change the Gentiles into the same quality as themselves. For one must not pay attention to those saying that God's portion was scattered among the Gentiles in the manner of captivity.

Not for honor, he says, having taken the people, he sent them away, but because of their sins they have been made submissive to enemies (Ps 43:13a); for through their sins they were given over according to the prophet.

Since we have fallen away from the aforementioned things through a life fearing destruction, we face our own disgrace (Ps 43:16), the shame of our face covering us so that we no longer have boldness, with the face of the soul uncovered to reflect the glory of the Lord.

From the voice of the one reviling and acting unjustly and speaking wrongly, he sees that the day of ruin is before him (Ps 43:17). And from the one displaying his terrible face, driving out an enemy, the shame of it covered his face.

The voice, having taken up perfect courage (Ps 43:18): for having heard many and various afflictions upon them and being coerced into forgetting God, they say, as it were, 'In the affliction of the Lord I remembered' (Ps 43:19b). God turns away some of the troubles from...

He abandons his own way, handing himself over to the desires of his own heart and to an unproven mind (Ps 43:20a). The earth and the underworld are a place of affliction; thus those having experienced the body of death are humbled (Ps 43:22b). The impressions in the heart must be addressed and examined (Ps 43:26).

If one speaks these things tropically, what is meant is this: since we are currently surrounded by the composite of pleasure and other passions, because of this, 'Our soul was humbled to the earth, having become low-minded, and also our belly was stuck to the earth, feeding on nothing heavenly but eating all things according to the nature of earth all the days of their lives.' But if the present text is explained allegorically, the soul stepping into the body says, 'Our soul was humbled to the earth.' Having fallen away from itself and from the blessed life of the heavenly, while thinking of the lower things, it says, 'Our belly was stuck to the earth,' for it feeds on nothing other than earthly things (Ps 43:27).

These say that they are worthy to receive help and deliverance, not by the grace of another but by His name. And these things are also said regarding the Savior, being worn down in the heart of the earth according to the season of passion, so that having risen, He might provide help and giving deliverance, giving His soul as a ransom for many. And He does these things for the glory of His name.

A goal for those making progress and changing from quality to quality is that the one at the summit of qualities should hasten (Ps 44:1), by which the corruptible and the immortal might be proven. Concerning this, the end being attained. Concerning those who shall be transformed, that is, those who are changed and have become eager from evil, sons of Kore turning all things into a song concerning the beloved, bringing forth and shouting. And the beloved here is the only-begotten Son of God. Concerning this, the triumphal song is sung, through whom He transformed, having given incorruption instead of corruption.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Arrows of Christ and the Rule of Virtue
english: If the person is the Father, he says: 'Since I alone am good' (Ps 44:2a), 'it is necessary that the one becoming the word of my own essence also be good.' But if the prophet is the one saying: 'Since a good man brings forth good from the good treasure of the heart' (Ps 44:2a), it is necessary that one having much good, having been fed with fornication foods, also brings forth a good word seeking it. For just as one having eaten an apple sends forth a scent of apple breathing, so one having eaten good things, having accustomed his soul to good things, brings forth a good word seeking it. Just as the quality of these foods is what becomes, so also regarding spiritual teaching, such things were sought and eaten.

Writing also certain instructions (Ps 44:2c). For just as the word of the gospel, being compared to a grain of cinnamon, if it should happen to be agriculture, becomes greater than human words of vegetables because of the temporary names given, so the word of God writes with his own pen and timely demonstrates these things, touching the thoughts and piercing the souls, apart from the writings of men.

Those hearing the words of Jesus, being full of grace (Ps 44:3bc), will say the upcoming text: 'He has poured out abundance' shows the grace; this agrees with 'I will pour out from my spirit upon all flesh' (Acts 2:17) and 'The love of God is poured out in our hearts' (Rom 5:5); for in these the abundance of the spirit and the wealth of the love from God is shown. Because of this poured-out grace, 'God has blessed you with your lips' (Ps 44:4), testifying of blessedness to you for all eternity.

Since regarding the testicle the things of generation are at work, and shameful desires grow around these, there is a need for the divisive word called a sword, in order that, having been made alive regarding the testicle, the unrestrained pleasures be cut away. The Savior, descending according to the human pattern, girds a sword around his testicle for the sake of self-sufficient purity, possessing beauty and loveliness because of the virtue coming forth in sinlessness; and what the symbol of the testicle of the aforementioned things is, let it be clear. For even Abraham, when sending the child for a bride, says his hand...

[...] upon my thigh, and I adjure you, the God of heaven. Perhaps, because of Him who is to become Savior through it, the Word who became flesh is able according to the flesh. The Word is understood and believed as a sword, while the flesh is a thigh from which the beginning of the flesh comes from there. But the Word, having escaped all weakness, is powerful, possessing the brightness, beauty, and splendor of divinity.

As for Psalm 44:5, the archer directs his best bow, wounding those who are thrown into divine arrows. It must also be read that he directs [them] to provide joy; and along with these, 'reign, O King, among the wounded' (Ps 44:6). The reason for your reigning is the perfection of virtue, not in practice alone but also in knowledge, because of truth, gentleness, and justice; for he says, 'reign, because it is necessary for the truth, gentleness, and justice to be known and established by those under your rule.' And 'your right hand shall guide you marvelously' (Ps 44:7). He who does all things according to God is marvelously guided by the right hand of good practice, using that path toward the Savior. And the Savior, performing paradoxical powers by his right hand, is marvelously guided.

As for Psalm 44:6ab, the words of the mighty Christ are like arrows that strike those who hear, so that they may judge the following of those toward Him. The apostles, being wounded by these arrows, having sent all things into the world, fell well to judge Him. And the peoples, who previously held a bad position, were struck by these arrows to be established in good, falling under Him; that is, they were made subject to Him and have become His.

As for Psalm 44:6c, the enemies of King Christ are all those who sin. If these spoken arrows do not exist in the hearts of these [sinners], they fall from the throne, prostrating themselves before the King. Perhaps the peoples who stand in the hearts of the King's enemies, being confirmed according to the will of their enmity, fell by the arrows under Christ, falling into the heart of His enemies.
As for Psalm 44:8, if these things are toward the only-begotten Son of God, the Son of God, having hated the life lived before His coming...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Change of Face and the Daughter of Tyre
english: Having loved iniquity, but having been granted righteousness through faith which comes from his presence by a paternal good pleasure, a man becomes and is anointed with the oil of gladness, that is, with the Holy Spirit. The garments of Christ breathe the scent of kingship and hierarchy through the death he undertook (for this is the fragrance imposed upon the buried dead), but also a continuous, unceasing scent of myrrh because of having something more than Christ's death for the salvation of others and the destruction of the devil, and of cassia because of his word being fiery; for this ointment is warming. The garments of Christ are those which are reasonably theologized about him. Since he did not take up along with the others that which is praised as being like a corpse, it is fitting that from his garments the aforementioned things breathe; with this, 'The fragrance of your myrrh is above all ointments' (Ps 44:9b) accords.

Kings are spoken of here as those co-reigning with Christ, while he himself is King reigning over them. Their daughters have become, according to teaching, educators of souls, or rather of the church; these daughters, in honor of the one being praised, have glorified the King, Christ. From heavy ivory. But 'heavy ivory' you say, [meaning] the high things of theology; for ivory, it happens, is a symbol of the Word, since the musical instruments and the teeth are vocal; and the great houses are heavy. Since they did not magnify their own word as the greatest of contemplations concerning God, many of the kings' daughters, from the aforementioned heavy ivory, have glorified Christ.

The soul, having truly become a spouse to the true King Christ, is the church, and is named queen because it is the bride of the king, standing at his right hand to hold the right position, possessing its foundation in virtue and faith. And she also holds golden garments, having clothed herself in Christ; and she is also draped and variegated, taking up the manifold wisdom of God. And one should not stumble because he himself is both bridegroom and clothed; for in one relation and another, and in one thought and another, these things exist, just as shepherd and lamb, and ten thousand other things are found in the Gospels.

A change of face appears to have happened (Ps 44:11); for God is the one calling the church from the Gentiles and naming her his daughter. He says: 'Having received my words, O daughter, listen and see their mind, having understood it for them; for what more will you desire to incline your will more fully toward them and to hear and long for them more effectively? And the forgetting of your kin will follow you, no longer desiring to restrain those same things and your fatherland; and the memory of your father who begot you according to the malice of the devil will also come upon you.'

Because of this I call you, daughter, says God to her, on account of the doing of the things commanded to you; since my son the king has desired the beauty existing in you according to the image and according to likeness having been made mine, and he, the king desiring your beauty, is not among your equals (Ps 44:12-14). For he is your Lord; for he is not an angel or an archangel or any other created being; for all worship him. Since it is not of God to be worshiped, be a god, the king desiring your beauty, who is also your Lord. Toward this also you undergo much change. For you, daughter of Tyre, because of which you had fear, have been made my daughter, so as to bring all the rich of the people as suppliants to your face. For all of the people from circumcision are becoming rich for you according to faith and are coming to you the truth of the gospel, beseeching your face to become a spouse to the king. For just as formerly those from the Gentiles, coming to the Godly service of Israel, were adhering to his face entreating him, so now those from the Jews, repenting, flee to the church of the Gentiles, deeming themselves worthy to be received by it. All the glory of the daughter of kings is Asbos. Asbos is interpreted as 'thoughts'. And the king of the thoughts being righteous is the Lord. The glory of the daughter of Tyre, which is being praised, is not other than that from the king of the thoughts. And it is to be understood that often in the Scriptures instead of the intelligible essence, gold is taken, as it will be timely shown. Since
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Christological Interpretation of the Psalms
english: Virtues are not merely found in the garments of the bride, nor is the discourse concerning the intelligible realities, especially that concerning the Trinity, adorned with golden embroideries; rather, it is made diverse through the manifold and many-formed teaching of Christ. Regarding Psalm 44:15a, since the word has an obscurity, we shall take its meaning from another. The discourse says that in the Vision of the Souls, it interprets the differences of the souls approaching Christ: 'There are queens and concubines and maidens without number; my dove is one, my perfect one' (Ps 44:15a). As it has been said concerning this: 'Her daughters have given her, and they shall bless her; queens and concubines shall praise her' (Ps 45:9), from which it is shown to one another that through the daughters they have been called maidens, concubines, and queens. It is made manifest from these words that the souls approaching Christ are such that some, having not yet the time for marriage, are maidens; but those coming to him after having been restored, some are noble and have ascended far above the world that became [existent] in six days. 'Sixty are queens,' [referring to] those having received the eight-day circumcision and possessing the spirit of the maturity of slavery. 'Eighty are concubines;' but the one surpassing them all according to the Spirit, having been perfected, to be a perfect dove of the Word, is the glorious Church, which has no nest, no wrinkle, or anything of that kind. The psalmist, in the verses preceding this, says that he hymns this Church, that she shall be brought to her bride with those [others] being embraced by him, the queens being the maidens who formerly did not have the time for cohabitation, but now, because they have been perfected, are being led into the bridal chamber, so that, having slept with the king, they might be taken up to become members of the one perfect bride, no longer being such as they happened to be when they were imperfect.

Regarding Psalm 44:15b, even if many are incorruptible, it is a custom to call souls virgins, but not all are brought to the king, but only those having become near and close by the disposition of the perfect bride. And also 'they shall be brought'; for those not having experience of the Word of the bride are not such as they are to go to him by themselves; but those handing the preliminary educations to them bring them to him; for they are not law and prophets.

Since almost everything of the psalm is said toward Christ, this verse says that although you have children according to the flesh from fathers, that is, those from circumcision, there have been born to you from the same race sons resembling the evangelical word. And these you also have established as rulers over all the earth, saying to them, 'Having gone, make disciples of all the nations' (Matt 28:19), they are his witnesses, having become the beginning of the king, even to the end of the earth.

Because of this, peoples will confess with thanksgiving (Ps 44:18), not for the sake of the second age, but even unto the age of ages. For we do not permit the confession concerning sins to be named now. For it never happens even unto the age of ages; only in this age is it possible to repent and to confess. But if they shall be remembered, according to another writing, instead of 'Those having been bequeathed to rule with you,' they shall be remembered by your name in all generations and generations, by extending your kingdom unto all the ages.

It is customary to call the things said unclearly 'hidden' because of a certain economy; for according to this also the wisdom of God is hidden in a mystery. Just so, 'The treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden' (Prov 2:6) have been said. And the end or purpose of these hidden things is not to let the unworthy find the knowledge of divine things, so that those having a desire for the attainment of divine knowledge, having given themselves to labors and exercises, might attain the purpose.

God is not the God of all, nor of those who have renounced all human refuge and power (Ps 45:2). For those fleeing toward God have all safety and power to partake of him, as the apostle says: 'I am able through him who strengthens me to do all things' (Phil 4:13). A help in the tribulations that find us intensely. The 'intensely' lies uncertainly; for the help is intensely in the tribulations that find us, or it is a help in the intensely finding tribulations.

Mountains being moved in the hearts of seas (Ps 45:3b), one should not consider the sensible parts of the earth being moved, but evil powers being moved into the souls disturbed by storms, a salty drink of wickedness and bitterness of character. Even the Savior toward the disciples...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Stability of God and the Shaking of Nations
english: a mustard seed

The Lord is in the midst of her, in the midst of threats (Ps 45:6). There is another scripture saying, 'God will help her with His face.' For He preserves her beauty, which is both vulnerable and incorruptible, the intelligible [beauty]; clearly, the intellect will receive disturbance from opposing things. For when the soul holds faith within itself as unassailable and assigns to itself the refinements of all virtue, the intellect possesses beauty and Christ Himself is revealed to it. Since the immediate, visible, and unchangeable is set aside, the Church, he says, will not be persuaded by this; for He preserves her beauty.

He calls the nations the hordes of demons warring against her (Ps 45:7). And when these see the incarnate appearance of the Savior, they are troubled against His Church and are filled with dread. Furthermore, the falling of the seven kingdoms over which death and sin reigned will follow. Even if you call those reigning 'kingdoms,' they too have fallen, flowing from error into the knowledge of truth and from wickedness into virtue.

Regarding the silence of God, the earthly and material things seem to have stability and standing, being shaken by God's having given a voice (Ps 45:8). For if God assists the intellect, immediately everything earthly is moved. And upon God having given the voice according to the Gospel, the earth has been shaken, with all customs, local laws, useful things, and even the impious deception being changed; the nations are troubled and the kingdoms are falling. While the earth is shaken, we are courageous, having the Lord of powers with us, the God of Jacob taking hold of us (Ps 45:9). Just as he who does the works of Abraham is His child, so he who imitates the asceticism of Jacob becomes His son, having an understanding from the God of Jacob.
And the Holy Spirit calls upon the acute [minds] for the understanding of these things.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Calling of Apostles and the Nature of Psalmody
english: Seeing [them] through the 'Second' to draw them near, and through the 'Behold' to dazzle them with the truth, he prepares [them]. 481 Ps 45,9 The apostles also filled the inhabited world, running everywhere and recounting what had happened through him and performing wonders in his name. The Word is able also to call the nations to know the Creator of this [world] from the wonders seen concerning creation. 482 Ps 45,10 Having come and having destroyed the devil, the holder of the power of death, and the other evil powers, he has abolished wars even to the ends of the earth, that is, those passing from the lands; smashing the bow, the burning arrows of the evil one which were being shot, but also consuming with fire the door of unbelief opposite the door of faith. 483 Ps 45,11a No one sinning and being occupied with wandering is able to know God; for everyone sinning has not seen him, nor has he known him. He who desires to know God, having renounced every occupation, will know who God is, as the present saying says: 'Be at leisure and know.' This, therefore, the tyrant of Egypt, having perceived, subjects the Hebrews to occupations so that they may not attend to God, saying, 'Be at leisure' [as in, 'you are mere laborers']: for this reason they say, 'Let us go forth and serve our God.' 484 Ps 46,2a Since hands are often said to be instead of deeds, and the nations perform various things according to diverse customs before the visitation, the Savior, having visited men, commands a tumult to occur, that is, a harmony of the practical powers of the nations, tropically called hands. 485 Ps 46,2bβ Not only is a harmony of deeds sufficient for salvation, but also a right mind with these things. Therefore, he commands the nations to shout aloud in a voice of rejoicing along with the tumult. 486 Ps 46,3a And he is fearsome and worthy of reverence to those who hold piety toward him. 487 Ps 46,3b It is not doubtful that he reigns over the super-celestial [beings]. Concerning those wavering about the earth, even if he holds even it, the preceding verse is spoken, and especially because those describing providence even unto the lunar sphere do not wish [to admit] those under the earth to be under providence. 488 Ps 46,4.5 He also perceives thus: he has subjected...

He ordained the holy apostles as rulers and teachers of all peoples, both the circumcised and the Gentiles, under their feet, having chosen for himself an inheritance not other than that of Israel; he himself chose the election of Jacob. And he says [of] the whole people of the Hebrews, Jacob. From this the impartiality of God is known, that he loved nothing other than the beauty of Jacob; for in every way the one fearing him and working righteousness is acceptable to him. A voice is made significant by the shout of falling enemies, in which he rejoices (Ps 46:6); and it rises above our understanding when it is found.

The loud voice and the piercing of the dogmas are called the voice of a trumpet; for in the manifest and in the Gospel, a trumpet is taken up, as in the saying, 'When you do alms, do not sound a trumpet before you' (Matt 6:2), which is, do not make it manifest. Sing not only sensually according to the shadow of the law, but also spiritually according to the Gospel (Ps 46:7). Perhaps it commands doing this unceasingly and continuously through doubling. And this same doubling of singing must be raised up to the King Christ; for he is indeed Creator, God, and indeed Providential, King. Therefore, it is necessary to sing unceasingly to the same God and King.

He who sings must also understand the things being brought forth in the song (Ps 46:8b). It is not necessary that the thing happen primarily concerning the rhythm and the tone of the voice, but concerning the understanding of the things being sung. For God spares those who do not sing thus, but only make a noise, saying, 'Turn away from me the noise of your songs, and I will not hear the sound of your instruments.' But he sings intelligently, the one practicing according to the divine teachings and understanding them.

The rulers of the peoples are the apostles or the leaders of the churches, gathered with God Abraham, so that they might bring in the peoples who benefit through him; for their God is the God of children having become of Abraham. But stand firm, if the rulers of the peoples can be angels, concerning whom it has been said, 'He set the bounds of the peoples according to the number of the angels of God' (Ps 46:10a), who also are gathered with God Abraham, since through faith they were made children.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Transformation of Souls and the Shipwreck of Bodies
english: Regarding Abraham, the portions which are found are rulers (Ps 46:10). The mighty ones of the earth are men who have lived rightly, exalting themselves by thinking of the things above and seeking the things above. For they, having been greatly exalted, being suspended by divine knowledge and virtue, have become of God; for the mighty ones of the earth, having become the possession of God, were exalted.

The joy of all the earth is a deep-rooted and good-rooted thing (Ps 47:3); perhaps there is no other one of him who said, 'I am the true vine' (John 15:1). For he himself is the joy of all the earth, being also the provider of joy.

It does not seem that some, having moved from wherever, were heard to have suffered, to signify from the appointed word; for they say that the Savior was crucified on the northern sides of Zion, there being the place of the skull (Ps 47:3).

But we say, following many writings, that the north is not anything other than the devil, according to the 'Exert yourself, O North, and come' (Job 37:7). This side is wicked men, just as they say the retainers of a ruler are his side. The wicked men who serve the devil, having previously been his side, transformed so much in virtue that they did not merely plunder Zion, but became its mountain (Ps 47:3-4). Paul, then, being a traitor, being a side of the north, plundered the body of the church which is Zion as it was transforming. And since the woman is called the side of the man, and the souls that became spouses to the devil, being his side through fellowship with him, became the mountain of Zion through transformation, just as the city of the great King Christ was plundered. For this word intends this, saying Zion [is] the mountain, which was formerly the side of the north or of the great king, we understanding it again as a great king by excellence of power but not of size. And in this city there are certain heavy and great dwellings in which God is known and the care of the city is grasped. These dwellings are of the same kind as the house which he builds upon the rock, he who heard the words of Jesus and did them (Ps 47:5-8). In the city the kings have come and into it...

Having been gathered together, having become the same, prepared by the same mind and the same judgment; but the kings are not those ruling according to God, such as Abraham was to someone, although not perceptibly ruling: 'You are a king from God in our midst' (Gen 26:2).

Not having seen the ancient ones who rose to such height from the north side, they marveled at the sight of Zion, being struck by the change occurring in the rational nature. And if one sees the bad becoming diligent and wise, marveling at the change, if he considers what might happen again—that those able to fall might be the diligent and wise—having thought this, he will cause trouble and shaking even to those who have greatly progressed in virtue, as if they were to seize the terror of dread.

Accompanying this is: 'The righteous groan in the places of the ungodly' (Ps 47:9), for when they fall, they become terrified. There are pains like those of a woman in childbirth. In the city of the great king, it is likely that souls have become pregnant from the bridegroom, and they have a time for delivery to form the offspring cast upon him, as if to labor to bring forth the mother's offspring.

The name of pains may signify those who are troubled and shaken, whom terror has seized. 'A mighty wind shall break the ships of Tarshish' (Job 41:31). The bodies are often called the ships of the souls in the Scripture, as also in 'Those going down into the sea in ships' (Ps 107:23). These bodies are not being crushed by the Divine Spirit striking them violently in essence, that is, being dissolved, so that at the time of the resurrection, incorruptible, strong, and promising spiritual things might come forth from corruptible, weak, and dishonorable, psychic kinds.

But these ships are not simply so, but are 'Tarshish,' changing the voice of Tarshish into the joy of discovery. For then the bodies, being crushed and dying, are praiseworthily broken, so that those nearby may discover the divine joy. While experiencing this in this life, we hear much concerning the heavenly city of God and the spiritual goods in it from prophetic words and other inspired Scripture. If, having been relocated...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Instruction of the Power of Zion
english: Let us become from the earth in the upper Jerusalem, weighing together the things seen in it which we have heard of long ago, saying: Just as we heard, so also we shall see. For it is also the city of our God, since He Himself established it for eternity (Ps 47:9c-d). And the Savior is not spoken of in these things; for the Father shows Him, saying: I will build my city. He is the artisan and creator, while God is the one having the foundations of the city which all the righteous receive.

Just as your name is wonderful in all the land, so is your praise, since the earth is full of His praise (Ps 47:11ab). One must consider the ends and the borders of the earth, those who have passed from the earth into heaven, upon which the name of God and the praise have reached. Of the assembly named Zion, its Lord is the one whom those trusting in the Lord resemble (Ps 47:12a). 'Judah' is interpreted as confession, and the souls participating in the exercise of confession are the daughters of Judah. Perhaps also all the God-breathed Scripture is homonymous with the place in which Judah is given, in which God is known. The daughters, not of the Judah being given on either side, but approaching as much as possible the judgments of the Lord, are true and justified, and they will rejoice in the same way. And since the judgments of the Lord are unsearchable, they do not rejoice at the present, but they will rejoice face to face, approaching the truth then.

Regarding the ecclesiastical opinion, being a scrutiny of the truth and for this reason called Zion, it is fitting to take it up with wisdom, so that having reflected upon the doctrines of the truth, we may describe them in a circle to their own intellect. And since the city of God is surrounded on every side by the approaching enemies, and has towers constructed from which the approaching enemies can be scouted. And since the enemies of the city are now warring, it is necessary also for those in its towers to give guidance. It also agrees: 'Upon your walls I have set guards by day and by night, who will never be silent until the end' (Ps 47:12bc/13-15).

Being islands of the Lord; in this way even Wisdom is proclaimed upon the battlements of walls. Set therefore your heart, that is to say your mind, having scientifically attending to the power of Zion (this is the ecclesiastical teaching), and divide out analytically to each one attending to it.

For just as it is logical to divide things into essence and what has become, and genera into being, so also to divide the power of Zion into its weighty parts as much as possible; and its weighty parts are the individual contemplations in which the doctrines of piety dwell. Do this, so that you may narrate to another generation what our God himself is.

Since the former generation, having received the city and its power, was reproved as evil, adulterous, crooked, and perverted by its own heresy, having attended to the power of the city and dividing its weighty matters, you shall know the things concerning the calling of the Gentiles, which is another generation besides the former, in which you shall also narrate that this is not the God who, having done the aforementioned paradoxical things, cast away the former generation and called another and others. But this God, concerning whom the proposed theology is always the same and likewise has, unto the age and unto the age of ages; and He himself will shepherd us unto the ages according to what has been said: 'And the Lord shall shepherd his flock in strength' (Ps 48:2a).

Prepare your hearing, not the common one toward other animals, but the one of the inner man through which we comprehend what is heard, as the Savior says: 'He who has ears to hear, let him hear' (Ps 48:3a).

Since among the called Gentiles, some are dull of the matter and of the earthly mindset, but having been born sons of men, they rise up through knowledge and instruction, through lessons and examined words; and He calls not only the herd-like and grazing ones, but also the prudent, saying: 'Hear these, you who are born in the Gentiles and are sons of men.' For teachers are debtors not only to the wise but also to the foolish.
I bring forth wisdom from my mouth, having previously meditated understanding in my heart (Ps 48:4). For then one will be able to speak wisely.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Folly of the Unwise and the Eternal Home of the Wicked
english: To bring forward a word, one who has trained the mind according to understanding. He who has learned the divine things and is able to hand them over well (Ps 48:5b). Therefore, even after falling into a parable, he promises to open his own riddle in the Psalter; for he set forth for himself, proclaiming in a rhythmic and patterned way according to theory, he opens his own riddle in the Psalter. And the word is patterned as one who must speak the truths. Perhaps also he who shows the divine words as being riddles, opening each of the riddles in a Psalter composed of sensation and power.

If iniquity should surround me with its wing (Ps 48:6b), no other vision of the ancestral tradition has reached the wing of Adam. All the born are of one kind and brothers, but no one is able to redeem his own brother who is sinning. For that one man alone shall be redeemed, concerning whom it is said, 'I will send a man to them who will save them' (John 11:45), who also says concerning himself, 'Now you seek to kill a man whom I have spoken the truth to you' (John 8:45). But that man, since he did not know sin nor did he do sin, will not give to God an expiation of himself which is given for the sake of those sinning, nor will he even attain the price of his own soul's redemption; but having labored according to virtue, he will live until the end, never to die.

And it can also be said concerning the one being redeemed, 'He will not give to God an expiation of himself.' For not everyone is one who is able to give an expiation, Christ propitiating all in his own blood, nor is anyone able to give a price sufficient for the redemption of his soul, Christ having given his soul as a ransom for all. Even if he gives neither an expiation nor the price of the redemption of his soul, yet after being redeemed he receives commands, so that having labored according to them he may be able to live until the end, having possessed the...

Eternal life. He who has been set free by Christ will not possess salvation so unsteadily as to be unstable and unmovable, even if he sees those considered wise dying (Ps 48:10b), since he is not so scandalized as to see corruption. For the stumbling over seeing is not to be placed upon this one, but upon those considered wise.

He says that they do not know the one who is entirely cut off, but the evil-willed and the bad-minded (Ps 48:11.12ab); and indeed we are accustomed to call the ill-faced one faceless and the ill-skilled one unskilled. Not so, for the evil-willed and bad-minded shall undergo no punishment; for indeed their destruction is such that they will leave the wealth they did not treasure well to strangers. For no one is an heir of the rich man of mind and understanding through these things. Not so, the foolish and mindless, having not known who they are, have glorified what, according to irrational animals, their soul does not abide in. For they say: Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die (Isa 22:13). Therefore, the tombs in which they are buried become their houses for an age, not expecting a resurrection of the dead; but also their tents are in every generation and generation (Ps 48:12c), they shall be tombs, hoping pitifully in this only life. Perhaps also, doing nothing vital but being dead through which they sin, they are casting the tomb down as an eternal house.

And they did not even call upon their names upon the earth. For the names of the apostles through whom they act or think are written in the heavens, but those concerning whom the word speaks called upon their own names upon their own earths, through whom they act, being urbanized upon the earth; for having departed from the earth, they shall be written. Man has become in image and likeness of God (Gen 1:26), and having been shown to be rational, he will have the greatest honor (Ps 48:13). But this not understanding, but acting with irrationality.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Judgment and the Two Presences of Christ
english: He is compared to irrational cattle, like a female horse having become so and having imitated the impulses of all other irrational animals. He was not made like irrational cattle, having hope if he wishes to be made like God. For there shall be five above the cities and ten the upright in the time to come (Ps 48:15b). And Solomon in the Proverbs says the same thing: A wealthy man hastens to be rich, and he does not know that mercy will hold him.

If even the aforementioned things have happened to the majority of men, nevertheless God will take my soul from the hand of the slave holding it and desiring to swallow it (Ps 48:16). And since the sinner is in slavery according to his condition, the one forgiving those holding him in sins thanks God having received his soul from the hand of the slave.

The one lying before us rich, not knowing another life in his life, thinks by this to bless his soul; and only then does he confess that it is good to him through the giving of material desires (Ps 48:19). A father having begotten him through evil works and a clumsy intellect (Ps 48:20). Likewise, acting toward them, he imitated the parents, and as being similar to the generation of the fathers, he will enter into the same deep abyss of ignorance as they. For having accepted only the present life, he did not hasten to see the light; therefore it has been said regarding the age not to approach it; for perhaps, having been condemned in outer darkness, he will not be permitted to behold the eternal light.

He says [the gods are] not the idols and the demons, but the men partaking of the words of God; for those are gods to whom the word of God came. God the Lord is of these gods, just as he is king of kings. And again, from the rising of the sun even unto the settings, he says, to know what... From Zion the splendor of his beauty has come. For the one according to the flesh was shown from the seed of David. The God of the gods himself, having called all the earth to partake of him, will not hide nor be forgotten, but will manifest clearly according to the second presence in glory with his angels; and he will not be silent.

Thus, each one is judged according to his works and his practice. It should be noted that in this present word, both presences of Christ are shown: the first through the 'Out of Zion' glory, and the second through 'God has appeared manifestly' (Ps 49:4).

Since the giving of the law is given upon witnesses, heaven and earth, as it is written in Deuteronomy, it is necessary that the people, being distinguished upon the witnesses through whom they received the law, be examined having stood upon the divine laws. He calls not the heaven above, that is, the divine powers, and the earth, I say, the inhabitants upon it, so that those made his children upon it might be exposed: 'Hear, O heaven, and pay attention, O earth, for the children of God are being proclaimed; for they, having received the law upon you, did not keep it' (Ps 49:4).

Perhaps he commands angels to holy men, so that he might gather his pious ones to prepare and establish his covenant of God upon spiritual sacrifices: namely, the sacrifice of praise and if anyone else similar. He commands the pious ones to be gathered to him, receiving the spiritual covenant upon which they are to offer the sacrifices, so that they might fulfill the things foretold.
'The heavens announce so-called righteousness' (Ps 49:6a), [being] men who are holy, bearing the image of the heavenly.

'God examines not the things themselves offered to those approaching, but the disposition according to which they approach' (Ps 49:8); and indeed, he exposes Cain for not having divided the offering rightly. If someone offers a spiritual sacrifice as whole burnt offerings through his whole body, let him do this with right intention; for one is not praised for the things being done, but one is examined for the intention not being rightly fulfilled.

'Since those in your land, figuratively called bulls, have become hostile to the Savior, concerning whom it is said, "Many bulls have surrounded me, wild oxen have enclosed me"' (Ps 49:9-11a); for this reason, I will not receive them, nor the rams associated with them. For they, offering themselves on behalf of sin, are no better than those who sin. Know then what those who were once beasts of the forest, men awakened from the Gentiles, are to me, being made subject to the divine teaching.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Integrity of the Heart and Speech
english: They have become previously unfruitful, for the grove is a symbol of this. But also the cattle, being like the sheep of Christ, and the oxen who have gone up over your fence—that is, trampling the shadow of the law in the dogmas of the gospel (because of the height they do not reach)—are our own possession. Does Paul say that the care of the oxen matters to God, he who sets forth the law concerning the ox in the books? Or is he speaking certainly about us? But also the souls that have become lofty, being winged by right thoughts and activities, are being called things of the heaven; for I know them, for I know those who are mine.

The good land that has received the seed, that is, a right heart, having cast the seed thrown by Jesus and having borne fruit, a hundred and sixty, thirty, possessing a full and ripe fruit, is the beauty of the field, not far from the sower; for he says, 'The beauty of the field is with me' (Ps 49:11b). The Savior hungers for the salvation of some; as for the lack of concern for the salvation of the Samaritan woman, he says to the disciples, 'I have food to eat which you do not know' (John 6:32), and 'My food is to do the will of him who sent me' (John 4:34). Since those coming from circumcision approach him with the sensible worship of the shadow as one starving, he says, 'If I hunger, it is not for you'; for the glorious church, having become my own possession, is inhabiting the world and its fullness. And the fullness of it is the gospel, not the type, the shadow. Being nourished by the fullness of the Gentiles, I will not demand from you food according to the shadow; but if you wish to have me as your God who heals with the Spirit, sacrifice to me a sacrifice of praise, of thanksgivings and theologizing; for these I receive as offerings; for I desire mercy, not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings (Ps 49:14).

He is the same God who is both Most High and a deliverer from distress (Ps 49:14). Regarding praise, he says [to offer] a sacrifice of the thanksgivings that befit you, and regarding prayers, the promises; for he says both in the first and twentieth [Psalm], 'I will render my thanksgivings in the presence of those who fear him' (Ps 49:12). Since praise is not beautiful in the mouth of a sinner (Ps 49:16), God strikes the one sinning, saying, 'Why do you not recount my righteous decrees, so that you may fulfill them, and why do you take up the...'

Did you receive my covenant in your mouth? For it is necessary that, having received it in your heart and having imprinted the thoughts according to it upon yourself, you would not utter the words of my covenant in this way. To this, the one proclaiming 'do you steal?' agrees, and the following (Ps 49:18–21).

And regarding the mind, 'you will think and not thus'; if ever you were observing someone stealing the will of the truth with heterodox opinion, you were agreeing and running together with him; but also those attempting to commit adultery with the bride of Christ, to draw the ecclesiastical souls toward them, by being of like mind with them or not turning away from those committing adultery, you are placing your part with them. You say this word is fitting for those who are indeed ecclesiastical, but for those coming into fellowship who are not ecclesiastical men.

'Your mouth has increased wickedness.' He who is ignorant of the good but does the evil, he sins; but he who, after knowing the good, sins, is rebuked for wickedness; therefore also the servant who knew the will of his master and does not do it will be beaten much. And it can be 'not thus'; because having taken up the covenant of God through the mouth, if the heart is full of sin, from the abundance of a wicked heart, being in the mouth, it increases in wickedness, just as through his tongue he is wise to entangle with deceits the heretical words that are sophisms.

'Sitting against your brother you have spoken, and against the son of your mother you have set a stumbling block.' Regarding the word 'brother', one can be of like mind and of the same fatherland; but regarding 'son of a mother', one is of the same womb and not from the father. He who is not thus toward brothers, what other can he be able to love?

And regarding the mind: since the word is toward a Jew, perceptibly offering burnt offerings and sacrifices to God, regarding this it must be said to be spoken in the presence of God, 'Sitting'. O you, regarding the letter of the law, you speak against your brother who is according to the spirit of the law and living by it; and you are also against the one who is the son of your mother; for from the same intention the spirit and the letter of the law were issued. And you scandalize the son of the mother, having set a stumbling block and a scandal, the circumcision which is a way of shadow and flesh. Having done these things, and
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: David's Repentance and the Pattern of the Saints
english: I was silent. The silence of God is called the longsuffering toward sinners; for if He were to punish them immediately by those things, He would not be silent, deciding against them, whereas they ought to suffer.
