This is the mindset held by the 'I have been silent from eternity, and I will not always be silent and endure,' says the Lord (Ps 102:2). He does not say this toward the one being reproved: 'These sins have been foretold to you, and I was silent, giving a space from afar through silence and longsuffering for repentance.' It is necessary to be benefited by such silence; from the opposite, you received lawlessness toward the wicked, by which you think me to be like you; for you, having glorified me, rejoice that I do not come forth against you.

Those who, having taken up the forgetfulness of God through sluggishness, take hold of understanding, stand upon the spoken words: 'What I longsuffer toward sins, I do not rejoice in, nor do I do this as an evil man, but as an occasion for repentance through goodness and innate kindness, by setting aside punishment' (Ps 50:1). For if you will not choose to understand, the law or the lawlessness seizes, and there is no one rescuing; for God will rescue those who understand, who are of the evil and who have repented. Let those who confess not care about those who have ceased and are no longer acting, confessing, saying: 'We have sinned, we have done wrong, we have been ungodly' (Ps 50:2). For it is not the one currently doing these things who confesses.

That is, the one praising and theologizing the beauty of God glorifies Him; for the sensory [worship] rather dishonors, bringing God in by making Him manifest and in need of movement. The way is not there in sensory worship, but there in the truth which encounters beauty, which God shows by illuminating His own salvation, the only-begotten Son the Savior, who is the salvation itself; for the salvation of God at times signifies the salvation, and at times the Savior Christ. But let this not become an occasion to rise up against David; for when God has justified, there is no one condemning. But he will be pious toward the man, having understood that the man is long-lived and has spent most of his years in powers and in kingship, introducing only this one sin, having done it, and in addition to this, having counted the people contrary to the will of God, but not even persistently...

For such a great and far-reaching king was rebuked in sin, that when he was rebuked by a private man, he not only did not feel indignation, but even made himself worse, as the rebuking prophet says: 'And the Lord showed your sin' (Ps 51:5). For to say that the Lord showed it is to say that David himself, having led himself to most intense repentance, was led to his sin. We say that what other men fall into when sinning, the saints, running the race of salvation, if ever they should stumble as men inattentive, do not fall but persist in the race, as if the instability of the race had not seemed to them likely to trip them up. And for many other ineffective things the sins of the saints were written down in this regard; for since they are called to imitate an exceeding virtue, being hesitant, they made a pretext for having a divine portion and for the saints being unendurable in sin, but not being such, they were unable to imitate the far-reaching saints. Thus Providence granted a pretext for sin to have occurred concerning them, so that just as they are teachers of virtue, so also they are teachers of repentance for those being instructed then, having done such things. Perhaps also those far-reaching saints, having reached the height of virtue, did not arrive at this by their own power but by the cooperation of God. If they were not to fall, the divine grace would have been little, so that, having slipped, they might seek the helper of their own weakness, having come to be through consciousness (Ps 50:1,2).

And this psalm was not written in vain for Pentecost. For the number has a harmony toward mercy and forgiveness, since, if the writing spirit maintained the sequence of history, it arranged the first Pentecost and the hundredth and those following. For the first Pentecost has an inscription containing the slander of Doeg the Edomite; but that history is before the kingship of David. And the third Pentecost, the slander of the Ziphites against Saul concerning David as being hidden among them, contains this; and this narrative happened before the kingship of David, but the encounter with Bathsheba happened while David was reigning. If not the sequence...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Divine Justice and the Perfection of Truth
english: The history was preserved, not because the fiftieth was arranged with them. But what analogy the number has to a lion, the Savior, teaching about forgiveness, took fifty debtors and with five hundred denarii of forgiveness, and to each side it had happened through the fifty and the related number to owe; but the five hundredth is not. Regardless, the Passover of the slaughter of the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world, having risen from the dead, who has made the forgiveness, the people for fifty days pass through rejoicing the fiftieth day of the outpouring of the Spirit, being worthy.

And called by the Hebrews Jubilee, the year through fifty years is a feast in which the cutting of debts and the restoration of the properties of the Hebrews' freedom are confirmed; therefore it is also following the psalm of David concerning repentance to be placed as fiftieth. And it is composed also of seven weeks and a unit, as if it were a week of weeks in number. It is necessary for there to be in weeks one who casts away the filth and the work of sin.

He who intensely repents and loves the fruits fitting for repentance asks for the great mercy from God to come to him (Ps 50,3a), for repentance is not sufficient without the mercy of God, nor the mercy of God without the recognition from us toward salvation. Just as the hard-to-wash dyes are removed not by one washing but by many, so also the great things of the lawless acts are erased by many mercies of God (Ps 50,3b).

The same energy calls lawlessness and sin, differing by the intention: the one consisting as lawlessness without law, the other consisting as sin according to the transgression of law (Ps 50,4); however, each is worthy to be washed and to be cleansed by God who is able to wash and cleanse it from the aforementioned defilement. But he who the...

Having committed a sin before Him, he would not take up another to do; for forgetting the former ones, we perform another. As for being a king, he was not subject to human law, but to God; nor did any of the lawgivers or a witness testify that he did evil before any of them; but since he wishes to be a king and God-fearing, he was subject to the law of God; therefore he did evil before God alone, and the witness [is] to God alone.

And again: since you are God, and the mind of men leans more toward evil things (Ps 50:6), and there is no man who will not sin, God is justified in His own words, in which He says that all who have strayed ought to sin; by this also He conquers when being judged against men, proving them to be sinners. Accompanying this, if we say 'We have not sinned' (Ps 50:7), we make Him a liar; for if it had been declared that all lean toward sin, he who claims sinlessness proves God to be a liar.

He who has been trained in the skill of sophistry upon the prey of truth, having known its greatness, possessed a perfect love toward it. For those not having been trained in falsehoods, having become more discerning, see the priceless beauty of the truth, namely Moses and Daniel. For after having been tested by the sophistical arguments, having ascended to the true wisdom, they received testimony from God as being perfect wise men, God having made known to them the unmanifest and the hidden things of His wisdom, so that nothing was unclear to them or overshadowed. David, by chance having this skill, spoke the coming verse.

He who has truly approached the typical Passover by the blood of the lamb in us is purified, being led in with hyssop as it is written in Exodus (Ex 12:22); but he who [takes] the lamb of God who takes away the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Repentance and the Davidic Model
english: Having attached himself to the sin of the world, being washed by the blood which is from his slaughter, he is whitened above a pillar. And the things concerning David have happened in a similar way; for he was led astray by a fleece (the blood of the typical sheep) and was washed by Jesus as if to be whitened above a pillar; and here he signifies a spiritual pillar.

Many times the doctrines and the powers of the soul are like bones; these are humbled by sin and by sophistic enchantment. But having heard the joy and gladness of God, the humbled bones will rejoice (Ps 50:10). And sins are erased from the transformation of virtues (Ps 50:11b); for just as knowledge coming into the soul erases and makes the ignorance vanish, so also every sin is erased by the presence of perfect virtue.

If you will erase all my sins, the ones written through the impressions in my heart, you create a pure heart in me, lacking all evil (Ps 50:12), but also kindle a steadfast spirit within my indwellings. And the upright thoughts and earnest perceptions dwelling in the soul are those about which he says: 'And all that is within me, bless his name.' And the steadfast spirit is the Holy Spirit or the conscience, the upright one, which the spirit of a man within him says. It is to be noted that what the voice has created does not signify essential beings, but a certain relationship being established which has been produced.

Of the earnest ones being unceasingly presented before the face of God, only the one sinning is cast out and rejected from him (Ps 50:13). But do not judge me, being contained by your divine comprehension, to be such a one as to be rejected from your face; but also do not take away the Holy Spirit whom you made to dwell in me, lest I be made naked of it (Ps 50:14). Expecting this descent of the Savior, by which it happens that he possesses perfect joy, he entreats the Father, saying: 'Restore to me the joy of your salvation, and with a ruling and perfect spirit support me.' And in these things, the Holy Spirit says 'ruling and leading' is either the man's internal principle or the soul of the man. And this ruling spirit desires support and confirmation according to the former interpretation.

We do not permit ourselves to ever overlook God, those who are diligent to do repentance and to demonstrate the teaching concerning repentance. Behold, indeed, even here what has been said is confirmed: for through the confession toward God, He promises to teach the lawless the ways of God himself, so that having stepped upon these, even if they were once impious, they might return to Him in a little while.

For those who have accomplished righteousness have the imitation and pattern of a good life, so also those who have erred concerning knowledge have to imitate the one coming into repentance, being impious ones returning toward God. 'Since by which I have done toward death, I am full of sins of blood' (Ps 50:16a), 'save me from these, the God who is once and our own.' Perhaps also David, from the sins of Uriah and if any others died with him, is worthy to be saved by God, being the God of his salvation.

'My tongue, called my own, in the always speaking concerning your righteousness, will rejoice in your righteousness' (Ps 50:17). From that, God opens the lips of the one having received the word in the opening of his mouth, so that his mouth shall proclaim the praises of God, always praising and giving thanks to Him.

'He who confesses concerning his own sin, what do you wish to discuss concerning Zion and Jerusalem?' (Ps 50:16b/20). But since we hope that he has not been entirely harmed by having stumbled in the short race, for this reason, possessing a prophetic thing and praying for and prophesying the communion of the Holy Spirit, [he says]: 'Doing good, saying that Zion was brought into being in your good pleasure for your son and approaching the Spirit'; but also the walls of Jerusalem are being built up. And these are guards of angels, a rooting out of incorruptible decrees.

He says righteousness, which is standing together through the faith of Jesus Christ for all those believing. But this righteousness turns out to be a lifting up and spiritual holocausts, and 'sacrifice a sacrifice of righteousness' (Ps 51:19); but also upon the spiritual altar, they bring up oxen like tillers, not other souls, but having been seen as the souls of martyrs, being brought up upon the heavenly altar.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Divine Providence and the Folly of Unbelief
english: Like the calves. For in the Revelation of John, the souls of those having been perfected through the name of Jesus and his testimony have been seen under the heavenly altar (Rev 6:9).

Who then is to provide a pretext for such a tragedy, he who is the shepherd of irrational animals? For we are without a leader. David, having realized his own great wickedness, spoke the words of the psalm (Ps 51) as if to the one moving him through envy, the devil, as if he were present.

Regarding the phrase 'The name of the Day let them reveal here,' it signifies the whole time according to which he errs. The words of 'drowning' are those bringing punishment, the drowning signifying chastisement, just as the lips of the unthinking drown him.

And the Edomite is not truly interpreted as earthly, always shaking because of being uncertain; for he is interpreted as being in a state of instability, he who, having worked slander against the healers of God, loved a deceitful tongue and with it words drowning him. And the Gospel signifies drowning to be the punishment, saying to the one causing scandal among the little ones in the church: 'It is better to be drowned in the depths of the sea' (Matt 18:6), with a millstone hung around his neck.

Because he loved evil to the end, he falls completely, as one not well built but also as one badly planted; 'Every planting which my heavenly Father has not planted shall be uprooted' (Matt 15:13); but he will be made to migrate from the holy tent, casting out and driving you away from that tent, whom you have slandered and into whom you have led to death, even the root of the living. For even if you were an Edomite, if you had attached yourself to Israel through the instruction of the law, you were planted in the tent and in the land of the living; for if you did not have reverence toward the God of Israel, you would not have even begun to disturb the sanctuary. And the things said against this man will apply to all those falling away from piety.
The very pious, those falling away from virtue into wickedness, receive a fear lest they themselves suffer the same. Nor will they dare to mock the fallen, as if saying they would laugh at him.

Thus a man does not set God as his helper; for he has not cast out his servants and attendants. Connect this to the fact that he who rejects you, rejects me. [Ps 51:11] Thanksgiving through confessing to God shows that he has done it, perhaps what he had previously set forth. For he had set forth to flee from Saul.

But also, 'what shall I do?' he says, 'your name is such that I might encounter whatever is good and full of goodness in the presence of your holy things'; [Ps 52:2a] for those having been made steadfast by the holiness of your goodness perceive it.

One is called foolish if he is lacking divine wisdom. For it appears that the word which does not preserve common sense is not about anything. For knowing that a thought of God has been cast upon every soul, embracing ungodliness, he is a god to no one except to his own heart. And thus the foolish devil does not act toward the heart of another (but his own is lying prostrate before God), but toward that which has become from him through sinning, he is a god to no one except to himself. [Ps 52:2b]

For he who has thought badly concerning God enters into wickedness; for casting out the piety of his own soul, he has also cast out with it all virtue following it like a royal garment of piety. Therefore, those saying through foolishness that God does not exist have corrupted their own mind by practicing lawlessness, from which they became loathsome, that is, they have become abominable. If it is chosen hereafter. [Ps 52:2c]
All those sinning, even those who seem to do good, not strictly and truly doing, but so that they might take a pattern of it through a mirror and an enigma, doing it himself. [Ps 52:2c]

The present verse introduces providence, of not only those in heaven but also those on earth; [Ps 52:3] for it has been said to look down providently from heaven upon the sons of men, not looking upon them from without only according to the body, but also according to the hidden part of the heart. He looks upon the sons of men, so that I might know if he is one who understands by doing the good and seeking God by examining the truth. And it has been said in a human way that he stoops from heaven to see if he understands; for great, if not in this way, is the impact.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Prayer of the Righteous and the Judgment of God
english: He has the knowledge of the hiding of all things (Ps 52:4). And from the present word we learn that sin consists in a transgression of the law by one who follows, if he is by nature evil. For all have turned aside; and this turning aside is sin, a failure not of the straight way. And those who turned aside were useless; saying [it is] useless, either according to the dominance of passions or according to the ignorance of one who, not thinking, is swept away into other things, does not have the knowledge of one thing. Of all those turning aside, it is rightly said, 'He does not do good' (Ps 52:5). According to each of the aforementioned, the 'until one' [limit] shows that neither is there one doing good, nor one not doing good.

Since wisdom will not enter a craftless soul, it must be known through divine knowledge. For it is not to be read according to a walk but according to a decision (Ps 52:6). There they will fear a fear that no fear can be brought up to the coming age; in that, fleeing from pain and sighing and grief, one must have courage. In this, not being in a state of fear, those approaching the things by which they will be punished will fear. Therefore, they will fear what God revealed there regarding those who became hypocrites, having the aim of pleasing men, scattering their bones, the doctrines and conveniences of laziness and greed, and the impulses of a vile soul. For if even there they were thought to be pleasing to men, deceiving [them], but being nullified by God as if they were nothing, they were shamed. And perhaps those doing evil will encounter the previously spoken-of punishments. But those hypocritically acting the part of virtue will not be tried by another punishment, their hypocrisy having been exposed; for he who does almsgiving to be glorified by men will not be punished by fire or anything of that kind (for he did not show mercy), but will be shamed, having been shown to have shared in the poverty of existing things not through God but through men (Ps 52:7). For sin is that which takes captive those who do it. But the forgiveness of sins being given as a gift, the [Lord] rejoices.

Israel and Jacob rejoice with those rejoicing in the heavens, similarly with one sinner repenting. Christ is the power of the Father. Since He judges the hidden things of men, He entreats that they be handed over for examination not to other judges, but by the power of the good God; for those, seeking forgiveness for those they passed over, will have vengeance happen against those who do the same thing in vain.

It is necessary that his prayer become well-pleasing and that he receive the things for which he prayed. But also, having become near to God through good works, 'Enlighten [with] the words of my mouth' (Ps 52:9). For no one, uttering a word that is idle, shameful, or some other evil, wants God to enlighten his words, but only everyone speaking the true and pious.

He says that those having an opposing disposition to the earnest ones are strangers, and the wicked demons are strong. And he says: because they did not set God before them, turning away from Him and having given their backs to Him, they rose up against the righteous and sought his soul.

He confesses God as a helper, perhaps the Father and Lord sustaining his soul, so that He might somehow turn the Son; 'He will turn the evils toward my enemies; for they desire to bring evil upon me' (Ps 53:6), these things He turns toward them, this being judged by the Lord in this way. 'Do to him as he has done to his neighbor' (Ps 55:23) agrees with this. And the truth of God, reproving those who are liars, destroys them if they are such; for they are not to be refuted at all, but rather they are such as the holy one prays.

Having these things happened, coming to thanksgiving with a self-willed mind, 'I will offer to You a voluntary sacrifice, not by necessity or force, but by a self-commanded readiness' (Ps 54:6). Lifting up a prayer to God, he entreats Him to draw near to him so that He may receive the prayer which he has brought forward through his trials. For He is near to the one saying, 'to receive the word.' And since I entreat, I do not take courage from another that the things lacking me will be replenished from You; do not despise the plea for which I entreat You. Give to me, [from those] lifting up holy hands without anger and...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Enemy and the Disturbance of the Soul
english: Presenting a meditation to you decorously and priestly, listen to the words which I send from a pure conscience.

The same enemy can be to the sinner, differing only in the lack of distinction. When the sinner is distressed by those through whom he acts wickedly, and when the enemy speaks the truth, 'I was grieved in my iniquity and was troubled' (Ps 54:3b,4a). Here iniquity signifies prayer, as also in the first of the Kingdoms, Anna says, 'Out of the multitude of my iniquity I have stretched out to you until now'; for concerning prayer itself she says this. The saint says: seeing the enemy speaking proudly and seeing the sinner distressed, he was grieved toward God through a prayer of iniquity; seeing those of the same kind and of the same race fallen into the depth of wickedness, he was also troubled by the instability of nature, lest even I should undergo this same turn. Perhaps he is also most caretaking-ly grieved and troubled seeing the wicked going astray, just as a father grieves for a son who remains behind. For some say that this psalm is reported to have been spoken from the face of Christ according to the human [nature], and it is fitting to be grieved concerning those being harmed.

Every serious person understands that to sin in thoughts is neither tolerable nor so, and in deed and word it is both dangerous and heavy. Therefore, if it ever happens in thoughts to cause a stumbling block and harm, guarding these within oneself and not uttering a word, according to the sin committed in secret, and not acting effectively, knowing that the thought is both healing and yet incurable; therefore he says, 'My heart was troubled within me' (Ps 54:5). For I did not interpret the trouble as having done something through it, but also, as the fear of death was falling upon me following the sin, I seized it within myself. For it happens that fear appears from the outside and becomes a stumbling block to others for the one who has been revealed. Fear and trembling came (Ps 54:6,7).
the passive, the irascible, and the desiring
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The distinction between living and dying through the Word
english: Regarding the building of towers, they were assigned one voice and one lip, but through great impiety, having been joined together, they no longer had concord. For those who were making [something] from harmony, intending to be impious, they did not do this, their tongues having been divided. And here, indeed, the one praying desires the tongues of those who have voiced concord against him to be divided, the tongues being submerged, that is, becoming invisible. And before this, if it is said, 'to punish' means 'to submerge.' And Paul, knowing that sometimes it is advantageous to have disagreement against the wicked ones, defending himself on the steps, struck against Pharisees and Sadducees.

This can be referred to the [Psalm] 54:10b, 'Behold, I fled away and was distressed in the wilderness,' through the middle of the two verses from 'I waited for God who saves me,' as the 'He divided their tongues' is such a thing: since in the so-called city of God, Jerusalem, they were committing lawlessness and speaking against the truth, committing lawlessness and speaking against the truth, I fled away from it, so as having become in the wilderness called the Church from the Gentiles, to be distressed in it, resting and spending the night among the believers (Ps 54:11-12).

Since all night and with the day they commit lawlessness and speak against [the truth] in the city, as the city would be surrounded by lawlessness and speaking against [the truth] and by the camp coming upon it because of these, lawlessness and speaking against [the truth] reached and upon its walls, the holy apostles guarding it. For they did not leave it, seeing it committing lawlessness and speaking against [the truth], because lawlessness and toil have come against the praiseworthy pleasure in its midst with injustice, as the birth and deceit of those dwelling in it do not cease from its streets, those acting craftily through whom they think wickedly, toiling by taking upon themselves the burden of evil, with lead being thrown against it.

And its streets were to be considered as the souls widening themselves for the sake of pleasure, to walk a wide and spacious road, this being a glorious and passive life. And for always remaining in these, the toil concerning evils and the deceit concerning frauds, it makes it so that 'It did not fail from its streets'...
Birth and deceit. Ps 54,14b.15a 'You know my reproach instead of being known by me, who has made my bonds sweet to me, but to the rest of the disciples nourishing me with good works.'

Ps 54,16bc Someone of the ancients said that those descending into Hades alone are those having received the instruction of the divine teachings. For the taste of the words of life is dead; those living thus descend into Hades. For those living without the common life do not descend into Hades as becoming a body there, for no one has the common life there. Since neither Judas nor all the people of the Jews had received the instruction of the law and the prophets, they descend into Hades with death coming upon them, living according to sin. Consequently, the one approaching is also said in the verse: 'That wickedness is in their sojournings, in their midst.' For even if they had experience of the life-giving writings, they did not dwell but sojourned in them, having wickedness in their midst, that is, in the ruling principle; for it is said that the wickedness is in the midst of the animal.

Ps 54,17 'I cried to God and had my voice heard by the Lord.' For only he who has cried to God is heard by the Lord. For not everyone crying to God shouts; concerning the Sodomites it is written, 'The voice of Sodom and Gomorrah has been filled up,' not having cried to God.

Ps 54,18 Since the narration of a pious man is wisdom throughout, a pious man and narrating wisdom throughout, the psalmist says: 'The evening sets for me the things of wickedness and the extinguished light of the ungodly, but the sun of righteousness rises for me as to make it in the morning; having become one having reached its noon, I will narrate the things of the aforementioned evening and of the previously foretold morning and of the aforementioned noon; and my announcing, God hears the voice of me, accepting and—if so—rejoicing at my voice which has narrated everything.'

Ps 54,20b He says that God exists before the ages but not having existed. For if he had said 'having existed,' he himself, being the beginning, would have existed previously by some measured interval. Because of this, he is not 'The Existing One,' setting his existence as beginningless and eternal, but because of the 'Before the ages' beginning.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The misuse of the Word and the judgment of the unfaithful
english: Being cast down from the existence of the ages. But it is necessary to hear from the ages how the creatures are being diminished. And the Savior is eternal, being from eternity, before the ages, so that even the ages themselves have come to be through him. And Paul says, 'And he himself is before all things' (2 Cor 5:19). The one existing is the same as the one before all things; for it is not that he has come to be before all things. And regarding the Savior, 'Before Abraham was, I am' (John 8:58), not 'I was' or 'I have been', but 'I am'.

Regarding sins, some are difficult and incurable, others are curable (Ps 54:20). Concerning the curable, there is found an exchange: the sacrifice brought up for sins, but also almsgiving and fasting with prayer (for these things rescue from death). But for the incurable of those who have sinned, there is no exchange to lay down as a ransom and a savior. For if a man sins against a man and they pray for him, there is an exchange for these; but if [he sins] against the Lord God, who will pray for him? For there is no exchange for such things.

He stretched out his hand to repay those who worked what was deserved (Ps 54:21). Since traitors and murderers of Christ have become unchangeable and madmen, they are worthy to fall under punishment as those who failed. They were captured by the Romans so that they might be stripped of their manhood and driven out of the nurtured land which they had never belonged to any other. Nor were they accepted back to their fatherland. For they profaned the covenant of God, not only by not adhering to it but also by rejecting the one prophesied under it. Perhaps also, even though the covenant was destined to be kept according to the sensible until the time came when it had to pass from the one according to the flesh to the one according to the spirit, by remaining in the typical worship, they profaned his covenant. Therefore, also, stretching out his punishing hand, he repaid them so that his wrath might reach them to the end, by which they were divided, no longer gathered together in his land, but scattered in every land. These things the wrath of the face of God brought upon them, since when his face shone and appeared, they did not receive it (Ps 54:22). For they were considered to be smooth and without fault because of their hypocrisy...

To seek out missiles like destructive ones and full of gall. For those interpreting even concerning God do not do so correctly; God has drawn near to their own heart, coming down with men, bringing forth words like oil being poured out and loosening the pains of those who suffer. But for those who despise them, the words concerning oil are found to be missiles, striking those who despise them. Often, regarding the striking, there is the metaphor of the arrow, and arrow and missile are the same according to the subject.

Regarding Psalm 54:24a, God does not give a stable place to the righteous, but those who have profaned his covenant he casts into a pit of destruction, contrary to the wells from which the Word protects life and incorruption from drinking. Perhaps 'pit of destruction' means the abyss into which those having been corrupted in their mind are brought down by his vote and are handed over by his judgment.

Regarding Psalm 54:24b–d, He does not wish that the Jews, who exist from before the ages, should be humbled by God. For they fell against the will of the Only-begotten, not fearing God but also profaning his covenant. And he says 'men of blood' concerning those saying, 'His blood is upon us and upon our children,' being guilty of all the blood of the righteous poured out upon the earth. And they themselves are men of guile, always approaching the Savior and the saints deceitfully. He does not wish that for these, even for half of their days, they should overtake [death]. For after they turned away from the day consisting for themselves from the brightness of the true light, having conceived a day of illumination through mythical traditions, it is evil that in this their days be filled; he intercedes that, in the intervening of their days, lest they should reach even half of their days, the sun of righteousness should set for them, so that they might become in the day of the Lord. And regarding the word 'let him force such things'; since in life the impious, dwelling in unrepentant resolve, do many evils, fearing them, it is worthy that, as human life is in the middle, they snatch away life so that for a few sins and not many they might be punished. Of these, he says, not being divided, 'I lay my expectation and hope upon you, O Lord.'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Partial vs Perfect Knowledge and the Soul's Preparation
english: The scripture arranges the idea of being trampled with contempt, just as it is said of the chaff on the threshing floor, 'They throw it out' (Ps 55:2). To be trampled by men and concerning the one devaluing Christ, it has been written: 'How severe a punishment do you think the one who has trampled the Son of God will deserve?' (Ps 55:2). And the holy one, being devalued by a man through foolishness, according to the [scripture] 'Where is your jealousy and zeal among you, and do you walk according to man?' (1 Cor 16:14), deserves to be shown mercy by God. But this [man] is an unceasing, murderous enemy who crushes the day of life of the righteous by warring, not desiring to be peaceful in any measure. And since in the parable of the weeds (Matt 13:24) the sower of these has been interpreted as the evil man, the devil, stand firm even if the foregoing is said concerning him.

Starting from much of this doing, he says, perhaps having fallen from a higher day and life, they have come upon my enemies (Ps 55:3). God saves those who have fallen into wickedness freely, receiving nothing from them (Ps 55:8). For he says, 'Behold, you were struck by your sins and you shall not be redeemed with silver' (Ps 55:8), being saved not by works but by grace. Indeed, 'above nothing' signifies not being given salvation to them above something.
The voice becoming bold toward God (Ps 55:9). For the living one, not by sin but by God, through these works, makes his life manifest to God, announcing it through disposition and practice.

The word brought forth upon God and through God is praiseworthy, likewise also the discourse. But he argues from a parallel against the same word and the discourse, or sets such comparisons one upon another. Since the word is a part of the discourse, the one being led into godliness, if perhaps unable to participate in the most full discourse, begins from a word, that is, a partial discourse. Care [not]; first the word of the Lord comes upon Jeremiah (Jer 1:9), and after this, the discourse of the Lord comes to him; and in Isaiah, he says, 'Hear, O word of the Lord, you who tremble at his discourse' (Isa 66:2). But the word of the Lord is heard in the one occurring through him in the introduction. If anyone should object, saying that it is given to those being evangelized...

With much power, those who know and prophesy partially now receive a word toward the coming knowledge and teaching, as the perfect word is being given to them and the perfect knowledge is shining upon them as if the partial were being abolished. He who accepts both the introduction and the full bestowal of the word praises God with word and discourse (Ps 55:12).

Regarding the flesh, he says that the man who has the mindset of the flesh is an enemy to God, not being subject to the law of God. For he who becomes [one] in this flesh is not able to please God. He fears lest he who becomes [one] in the spirit should do to him, as having killed the works of the flesh; for he has not truly hoped in God (Ps 55:13).

He who prays does not stand in harmony with those to whom he is promised through prayer, but holds within himself the prayers of praise to render to God. And prayers of praise are those concerning praise; for just as someone prays to do or to render this or that to God, so someone prays to praise God (Ps 55:14ab).

And since mourning and the falling of tears follow the one dying, no one mourns the one dead according to the soul except himself, fittingly after the soul has been snatched from the death of the intellect of ignorance concerning God and his eyes have been freed from tears. He snatched his feet from slipping, having shod them with a shoe that lifts up and makes them above the earth. For God says, 'I have shod you with hyacinth.' And the hyacinth, imitating the body of the heaven, shows the soul being colored with the heavenly, with a shoe not being any other than the preparation of the Gospel. Since the one shod is being lifted up, there follows the being snatched from slipping, concerning the feet being snatched from the matter (Ps 55:14c).

Someone is snatched from the aforementioned harmful things in order to please God, living and having been enlightened. For he who pleases God does this while living in light; and he lives and has been enlightened, everyone partaking of God; for he himself, being life, is the light of men, according to the scripture: 'And the life was the light of men' (John 1:4).
The doubling shows that both in this life and in the future we need the mercy of God (Ps 56:2a–c). And he calls the divine protection the shadow of wings.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Salvation of the Soul and the Unity of the Church
english: The shadow is pre-ordained to distinguish itself from the truth; it means this: in this life, finding myself in the shadow of the wings, I hope to come upon those very wings, being carried on wings by virtue and spiritual intellect. But the wings of God are His sheltering powers, or the lofty thoughts about Him.

The passing away of lawlessness shows that it is temporary (Ps 56:2). And Paul indeed writes in Hebrews that the enjoyment of sin is temporary (Heb 13:5). It is not as if lawlessness were passing away having begun from a certain time; for he says something about it: it shall be neither from the beginning nor unto the age (Ps 56:3).

But the Most High is not in vain (Ps 56:3). For since lawlessness is clinging and low-lying, the one being delivered from it cries out toward the Most High, so that by lifting himself up with the cry, he might become far from the harmful beast.

The Lord, sent from heaven to save, says: 'I have come down from heaven, not to do my own will' (John 6:38). For God sent this word of His and healed those wounded by their corruptions, as David himself says elsewhere. If anyone seeks to ask whether the one sent from heaven signifies a local emission from the physical heaven, it would seem absurd to attribute a local descent to God. For does the voice of heaven not signify the incorporeal and intellectual essence, according to 'Store up in the heavens' (Matt 6:20) and 'God is in the heaven above' (Ps 115:4)? Therefore, the one being in the form of God and being healed as God, having taken the form of a servant, [came] to men (Phil 2:6-7). And this is the sending from heaven, so that the Word of God might become flesh and, having appeared upon the earth, might walk among men (John 1:14). Peter also writes, initiating mysteries concerning the Holy Spirit: 'Now it has been announced to you through those who preached to you by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven' (1 Pet 1:2); for having been sent from the intellect...

That the Spirit may find essence in men, it was granted to those who preached to you (Ps 56:4b). Before this, saying, 'Those who before this, by despising, trampling me into reproach, were given, God having sent from heaven how I might be saved' (Ps 56:4c). For having seen the Son of God caring for my salvation, those acting shamefully and reproaching me, even though they trampled, God saved (Ps 56:4c.5a).

In the preceding verse, having said, 'He sent from heaven' (Ps 56:5a), not having said what was sent from heaven, he now interprets what mercy is and truth, the one rescuing his soul having become among enemies of those who trampled; for these are wild and wrathful dogs. Mercy is not otherwise according to the essence of truth; for both are the Savior (Ps 56:5b).

Sleep often signifies rest, as in, 'In peace I will lie down and sleep.' He does not wish to say this, that is, even if I was troubled being trampled by enemies and terrified by the dogs having taken me in the midst, but the trouble did not remain. For I slept having been troubled, not remaining awake being troubled, but I slept having cast away the trouble (Ps 56:5b).

This is a symbol of the woman continually weakened by the spirit, collapsing and not able to rise up completely, whom Jesus released from the snares of Satan, the daughter of Abraham (Ps 56:7b). Perhaps also everyone who thinks of the things below has a soul having become fallen, not able to contemplate the things above, is such a thing.

And you will perceive the people and those from circumcision, but the mortals from the idols having repented, as to become one church (Ps 56:10). Those having loved the Lord in incorruption, having come to the end of not being corrupted, the pillars through whom they work well, they raise up. For just as those doing the opposite do evil things, they make a forbidden pillar...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Pillar and the Womb
english: They say the law: 'You shall not make for yourself a pillar' (Exodus 20:4), signifying that everyone who practices forbidden things raises up a life like a pillar. Therefore, one may also rightly say that the one doing good things is setting up a pillar, as a symbol of the contests through which he has struggled.

For such is the fruit of righteousness (Psalm 57:3), and in Proverbs: 'To perceive true justice and to direct judgment' (Proverbs 21:15). But injustice entangles, joining sin by acting without distinction in evil. This is equal to the binding of one's own sins in a knot. It is not in vain that you work iniquity in the land (Jeremiah 23:24); for if someone makes iniquity in the heart, he works it in the land, that is, concerning material things.

Those daring to slander the Scriptures and dragging this word into error, saying that those who are led astray from the stomach and speak lies are not [true], say that the fulfillment of the word is sinning. It is not right to say that those who have not perceived the habit of the Scripture have thought these things; the newborn infant is receptive to virtue and to wickedness in power, then receiving by operation whichever of these two it encounters, it will know good and evil. For then also the word is fulfilled, when it begins to act according to virtue. It is said that the good has been made from the mother's womb. Such is what Job says: 'Even if I ate my morsel alone and did not share with the orphan' (Job 31:32); for from the mother's womb they guided them and I nourished them as a father. And those who, failing regarding the word, rushed to the fulfillment of the word from error, began to act. And the expression 'to speak' signifies 'having spoken lies.' Perhaps also, as in the preceding verse, to be a shepherd and to be of another birth: those born from a bad teaching, from the very stomach that bore them, [referring to] the being led astray and the speaking of lies.

They say that the ears of an ox, the so-called 'palms,' are carrying a shield. For if ever a singer, according to his own wisdom, were able to carry a song capable of lulling it to sleep, if it were to hear, the ox would lay its ears upon the non-hearing of the singer's voice, as if a medicine being prepared by a wise man. And they also lay [their ears], not the ears of sensation but the ears of intellect, so that they might not hear the wise songs being proclaimed...
preparing a logical medicine
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Deliverance from Lawless Workers
english: Death of life. He does not rejoice exultantly, but, lest he himself be subject to punishment, he purifies his own deeds, becoming more secure (Ps 57:11a).

When one Saul is pursuing him, he prays to be rescued from many enemies (Ps 58:2-3). He prays not to be [rescued] from the spear-bearers sleeping with Saul, or from the predatory demons acting against him, saying 'many enemies' to be rescued from them. And he prays to be liberated from these rising up against him, wishing perhaps that the ransom of the one being liberated might be to give his own soul instead of many.

But workers of lawlessness are those doing what the law forbids, and since among the forbidden things is murder, men are men of blood, preferring to kill men because of the coming brutishness. But he who is not bothered by those working lawlessness is rescued, being under the protection of God, and also he who is not handed over into the hands of those willing to shed his blood is saved from murderous men.

And in another way: one is rescued from these; for he who does not work lawlessness but is disposed contrary to those doing it is rescued from the disposition of practical lawless acts, just as he who exists outside of murderous intent is saved, not being associated with murderous men.

The verses are to be interpreted thus: since men commit the work of lawlessness while the devil and his angels are working in men, he prays to be rescued from the devil and those with him who precede in the work of lawlessness. The testimony of this thought is: from the beginning the devil sins. For following that, others fall into sin in whom he works. Having cast betrayal into the heart of Judas, he became a traitor, following the thought of betrayal because of the one who incited him to this.

And also to add 'men' to the murderers; for it is not by chance, but the blood of a man is poured out by one strong and perfect in evils. Regarding the intention and brutishness of Saul and those sent by him to take him from his own people and to kill him (Ps 58:4a), he says, 'They have sought my soul, though by the power of God I shall be saved,' by a paradoxical art.
prone to change
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Divine Discipline and Repentance
english: He is Lord, the God of the divine powers, but also the God of Israel, attending to visit the nations so that He might heal them as they are being badly consumed by idolatry and the service of demons. The visitation of the nations occurs because the divine Word has been sent to heal all and to save them from the corruptions that take hold beforehand. Indeed, He is a physician of souls, healing those who are crushed in heart. He is called God of powers and Lord of the rational, holy animals and heavenly hosts. Just as He is God of these powers, so also, by the voice of the discerning men called Hebrews of Israel, He is God (Ps 58:10-11).

While David was being pursued by Saul because of the aforementioned envy, he knew what the successor of the kingdom would be. And having prophetically seen what was to come, and having been anointed for this by Samuel—though he was not yet fully filled with the knowledge of it—he did not repeatedly rush into his hands, wanting to legally receive the kingdom from God, but not to seize it by assault and murder. From this intention he says, 'God is my strength, I will guard myself toward You' (Ps 58:10), not intending to strike, but waiting to receive it from You; and I am confident in this assurance, having known through experience many times that You are both God and my perceiver. For it is not by our power that we are worthy to reign, but rather Your mercy, having foretold me, will show itself to me among my enemies, in which they shall be disciplined by falling under punishment, but I shall receive the kingdom from You.

And regarding the thought of reigning from God according to Abraham: it is written that if some say to the patriarch while he is not perceptibly ruling, 'King, You are with us,' ruling pleasingly to God, he says, 'My God is my strength, I will guard myself toward You' (Ps 58:12); for You will lead into the kingdom those who have spoken, as the Corinthians say, 'And it would be good if you reigned, that we might reign with you.' (Ps 58:13ab). As a matter of history: the enemies lying in wait are worthy to be rebuked by God, but not to die. For it is not right that, if they remained wicked, they should die, for they would bring an end to the divine law; but being scattered by the power of God and being handed over to captivity, they will cry out to...

Having experienced God as a trial of punishment. But He also wills that they be brought low from the height of the pride they possess, which is the one defending the Lord who carries up the prayer. For complete punishment prepares and turns [one] toward recognition. But David, sparing them from this, pleaded that they might be disciplined by a more moderate punishment so that they might be sober; he adds the following: for if they are scattered, they are punished at once, and they will be able to be gathered together again having repented. Likewise, He also wills that they be brought low, that is, humbled: [to stop] the sin of their mouth, the word of their lips, which is beneficial both to those being humbled and to the majority, so that they may not be provoked to zeal against those speaking and saying things in pride and unrighteousness. For those having spoken with pride, having lied against the righteous, receiving the condemnation in the pride of their own words contrary to their works, they receive [it] as if being caught as lawless men being reproved.

It is to be reproved also from the present word those who think with a defensive mindset that the Creator is a heretic (Ps 59:3). God is angry not to destroy, but to have mercy. By this, 'I will bless You, Lord, what You were angry with me for, toward salvation' (Ps 59:3). For if He is angry toward salvation and toward mercy, His anger is not a passion, but is received usefully.

Those striving for material things and thinking of earthly things (Ps 59:4), regarding them as being stable and imperturbable, this such a state brings harm to them; it is better to be shaken and troubled by the mercy of God in a useful way. For having known that to be entangled in material things and to think of them causes trouble and shaking, turning away from the former bad life toward a serious [one], without care and having been crushed, having received the realization of the existing destructions from the demons, she will call upon the Lord who is able to heal these things.

Hard things are shown to someone if he falls into painful [circumstances] (Ps 59:5); but if anyone receives [them] toward the recognition of former sins, he drinks the wine of compunction, taking from the drinking the cause of being moved to repentance. Often the Scripture unreservedly calls the hard circumstances 'hard things'.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Christ in Paul and the distinction of being
english: As in the Cup in the hand of the Lord, the mind is uncontrolled. But the hard things are homonymous with the hard ways spoken of; in the Psalm it says: 'Through the words of your lips I have kept hard ways' (Ps 50:11). For indeed, hard ways are those called according to virtue because they are made straight through much sweat and toil, but here it is when the people, having been tested by hard things, [are afflicted].

What is the sign that God gives, which is the illumination by which it is possible to discern spirits and good and evil? For having this knowledge existing, we flee from the malicious, becoming far from the evil of work and the evil spirit. But the sign is given not to those who happen to be, but to the God-fearing pious.

'That your beloveds, remaining unhurt, may be washed away from the face of the bow, you gave the said sign' (Ps 59:6). It must be said also: then they will be washed away from unseen enemies, whom your only-begotten Son shall save with your right hand. For the right of God has been interpreted many times, especially where it was foretold: 'I have strengthened you with my right, just, and with my right I have established the heavens' (Isa 51:9).

One must supervise how the order of thought precedes the order of utterance. For previously, having heard, God saves, and thus the unharmonious harmony, the word having the sequence 'Save' then 'Hear my' after it, unless it is thought otherwise: 'Having saved by the right, hear my [prayer],' the prayer of the one being saved is not about being saved (for that is what is said) but about asking for divine goods, for the gifts of the divine Spirit are such.

But those who through goodness-and-beauty become gods' beloveds are worthy to be loved by him; men made according to the image of God, even if they have fallen most deeply into sin, yet they are nonetheless, because of the soul's spiritual and rational essence, his beloveds. God speaks to everyone participating in holiness.

Indeed, Christ spoke also in the holy Paul and in every prophet. But if the voice is seized regarding the Father, the holy one in whom the Savior speaks is he who is in agreement with the one: 'The Father who abides in me does the works,' and 'The Father has given me a commandment, what I must say and what I shall speak'; these things fit the economy.

Ps 60:3ab: He who prays here, knowing himself to be far off, sends up his prayer from the ends of the earth and says that he has cried out to God in his distress; for as it is said in Ecclesiastes: 'God is in the heaven above and you are in the earth below.' And it is signified by the word not a local distinction but a difference of uncreated essence and created things, of the existence of God being said to be above in heaven through the superiority of honor, and of the man being below in the earth by having come from non-being into being. Regarding this difference, the Baptist also, having observed the Savior, says that he is in heaven from above, and that the man is from the earth and speaks; for he declares it possible to say by means of a creature.

Ps 60:3c–5: We shall accept 'Rock' to signify the Christ, the flowing spiritual drink. He who becomes in this rock to partake of it (for wisdom and righteousness and holiness exist) is lifted up according to the mind, being raised by God. And those intending to fall toward the Savior, according to his exhortations saying, 'Come after me,' and again to Philip, 'Follow me,' using him as a guide, partake of that same lifting up, not hoping to find any other leader of the way which rushes toward the cause of all. Having obtained this gift, David also says with his mouth to the Lord: 'You have guided me to what became my hope'; and not only a guide but you have become a tower for me from the face of the enemy. For I remained unharmed, having you as a tower of strength and power, even though the enemy was an adversary and wished to fight me.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The fulfillment of eternal things through daily life
english: He who begins to build this tower, as if laying foundations, should complete the building as if placing a crown upon the roof, lest he suffer shame before those passing by, who are accustomed to mocking those who have not completed the citizenship they undertook.

A connection can be made to 'Lead me from the face of the enemy' (Ps 60:6b) and 'You have led me in a straight path thus'; 'You have led me from the face of the enemy' has become my hope, but also a tower of strength in leading me from the face of the enemy. The hope of the saints is the true and unshakeable Savior, as Paul says, 'Jesus Christ of our hope' (1 Tim 1:1), and the prophecy upon him is that they hope in him; for he himself, having been foretold, shall be the expectation of the Nations. Someone, having been perfected in holiness for the ages in that dwelling, signifies 'Who shall dwell in your holy habitation?' (Ps 60:7); for this is the same eternal one in the tabernacle, the Lord, and not man. Although such a tabernacle does not possess the perfection of the Holy of Holies, there is no state with it surpassing the rational ones in which they shall be in Father and Son, but rather in the Trinity. Therefore, it is said to dwell for the ages, but not to reside in the dwelling. He who has become in this [dwelling] shall be covered under the shelter of the wings of God.

For he says, 'You are very rich, and you provide great gifts' (Ps 60:7), rather, by freely giving to perfect men the becoming of your sons, you have given them an inheritance. For although it is expected to be given according to the resurrection in the future age, it is nonetheless being given in a favorable way to those who are being led according to the time what is necessary. And to those who fear his name, God has given an inheritance (Ps 60:8). If there is a difference between those fearing God and his name, and those believing in him and in his name—since it is often said that those made intimate by the approach of God, those united to him, the God, are inferior—it is seen that the inheritance is given also to those fearing God; for if grace has been increased to the inferior, much more to those who have ascended far above. Whoever obtains the interpreted gifts, what kind of king is he, according to what is signified regarding the God-fearing ones as they were a Kingdom...

A beloved, a holy nation. By this signified thing to reign, and the apostles, expecting, say to the Corinthians, 'You reigned without us, let us also reign with you.' To the reigning which has happened, there is added by the Lord, 'day by day occurring.' For it is necessary from a preceding state of light to a transition into another likewise, so that the eternal things, concerning which it is said, 'And I remembered the eternal and meditated upon them' (Ps 103:2), might be fulfilled from that which is named of the days. And the life of the days is extended by taking them day by day, as generations of generations before God.

Who will seek out His mercy and truth? Often, of the divine teachings, His mercy is joined with the truth of God. For since to know clearly and purely the truth of God is not possible for one surrounded by human weakness, from this there is a need of the mercy of God in order to understand the truth. This contributes to the fore-set purpose, that all men should be saved and come to the knowledge of the truth. For first, it is necessary to be saved by the mercy of God, so that subsequently the knowledge of the truth may exist. For the salvation of men is the work of the mercy of God. 'For God sent His mercy and His truth,' and the following.

Since in whom I have found a thankful reception from You, I will sing in Your name, praising through works, thoughts, and good words the prophecy of You called upon me (Ps 60:8); and with this I will repay day by day, just as Jacob says, 'If God gives me bread to eat,' and the following, 'all things to me shall be mine if I tithe them to You' (Gen 28:20-22). For before these words it is brought forward, 'Jacob made a vow,' saying, 'If the Lord be with me,' as 'I will tithe them.' And also to say 'repaying prayers day by day' and 'singing in the name of God unto the age of ages,' for the one singing in the name [is] the one being praised, to extend into the coming age; but the one repaying the prayers, it is as if the time being fulfilled of the days is being completed; it is not that which is delayed by each individual's life. Since we are not in [this] life, we shall repay the prayers, so that we also may sing unto the age of ages in the name of God.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Deception of the Enemy and True Repentance
english: That we may be able. Everyone shifting from virtue into vice is shaken (Ps 61:3), but this does not happen abruptly; a disturbance first occurs in the thoughts through the passions, so that if appropriate action is taken, the shaken thoughts do not become a collapse and a fall.

For when an ugly desire or some other irrational movement begins, the pious thought must intervene, grasping God, to direct the impulse toward action, so that a greater shaking does not occur. The Savior clearly teaches this in the Gospel, uprooting the beginnings of sins so that their remaining does not result in a greater practical shaking.

He who is established and rooted in love is an unshakable wall and has a firmly set hedge (Ps 61:4c); how then could those passing by the way, wicked men and evil powers, not strike it? God surrounds him with such a secure hedge, saying, 'I have plowed and set a hedge.' For this hedge consists of angels guarding, and of truths of dogmas, and of actions being performed according to virtue. While this remains, no one will be able to harm the divine fruits of the spiritual plant. But if the one guarding the vineyard should ever bring forth thorns instead of grapes, God, abandoning him, says, 'I will take away his hedge and it shall be for plunder, and I will pull down his wall and it shall be for trampling.' If this happens because of the production of bad fruit from us, the wall is leaned and the hedge is pushed.

The honor of the wise, which the wicked plot to cast away, is virtue and piety (Ps 61:5), according to 'Glory and honor and peace to everyone working the good' (1 Clem 1:1). Therefore, vice is a dishonor, in which those who have fallen, feeling they have suffered, say, 'Our dishonor has uncovered us unto tribulation' (Ps 61:5). To this, man also takes part, not understanding the value of being in honor. Since the deceivers lying in wait cannot draw one into vice by force, they say, 'They did not drive away my honor, but they plotted to cast it away'; for they are not those who can overcome the one standing strongly against them. Related to these are those about whom Paul writes, 'Deceiving through flattering speech and lying words the hearts of the innocent' (2 Cor 11:14).

It is of the same mind: 'If your enemy entreats you with a great voice, do not be persuaded [Ps 61:7]; for seven evils are in his soul, perhaps coming from the seven spirits, as the unclean spirit receives from more evil spirits than himself.' ...as if he were entreating for the seven evils existing in his soul, the First [God] saying brightly and pleasantly in a punishing way, 'do not be persuaded'; for blessing with the mouth, he curses the heart.

I will not repent, becoming a repentant one by sinning and being distanced from God [Ps 61:8], according to what is written concerning Jacob, who was overwhelmed and turned away from God his savior. Grasping God, I have not become a repentant one, they attain salvation and glory upon God; for I was not saved by my own power or art. And he says 'glory upon God' because it is that which the only God gives to those seeking him, and 'salvation' not of the flesh but of the rational soul, which the one having believed into the Trinity possesses, according to what is said, 'Finishing the faith, the salvation of souls.' Therefore, even if he is violently thrust back into error, I make hope upon him, who has often saved me.

All the assemblies of the peoples of the nations who have believed [Ps 61:9], who no longer have God and hope, hope in him against all craftiness, making your hearts manifest before him; for God will become a helper to you. The same is meant by to pour out before him the heart, to love him from the whole soul and the whole heart. For often to pour out has been arranged instead of a rich abundance and a lavish supply, as in 'the love of God is poured out in the hearts of you through the Holy Spirit' [Rom 5:5].

To such people it was said [Ps 61:10], 'Why do you love vanity and seek falsehood, even though you are commanded not to have a small and a great weight, but a true scale, since a double weight is an abomination to the Lord.' It must be said whether these things are intended, and also toward those who have dealings and fellowship; for in every matter, justice is desired; for those running together toward vanity vainly strive, always having a vain agreement and zeal. Here it must be known: the 'Sons of men' signifies circumspectly those who are...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Twofold Circumcision and the True God
english: They are dying men who are no longer gods and sons of the Most High, as it is signified by what is written: 'For where there is strife and jealousy among you, are you not fleshly and walking according to man?' (James 3:16).

For it is not possible to serve God and mammon, nor indeed to hope for injustice and God (Matthew 6:24). If it seems that the wealth of one who does not seize and does not act unjustly is flowing and diminishing, it is not necessary to add to the heart, so that the heart might not be grieved by the diminishing of the money.

Because the name of injustice signifies, on the one hand, inequality regarding exchanges and sharing, as in 'But you do wrong and deprive even your brothers,' and on the other hand, all practical wickedness, as it is said, 'I hated injustice and detested it' (1 John 3:15), so one must watch according to what the meaning of the word now presents. One says the former, making it clear through the fact that plunder and flowing wealth were accompanying him, while the other says the latter, as it is said, 'But he who loves injustice.' For this is the case, since injustice is not entirely one thing, nor is the seizing regarding money.

God is incorporeal, rather existing beyond all generated being, both material and intellectual, having nothing entangled with himself; thus, when God speaks, He speaks once, that is, monoidly and uncomposedly, not as I hear Him thus anymore. For what is spoken once, you hear as two, according to the manifestation; for this voice is a pointing voice.

He therefore says such a thing: as He speaks with a pure intellect and an uncomposed voice, I hear the things spoken as being two, with my imagination standing by, perceiving someone called a spoken word which turns out to be unspeakable, as He speaks with intellect and an uncomposed voice. And so, if the apostle, writing that he has heard unspeakable words (2 Corinthians 12:4), wishes to present this, the unspeakable ones are such that they are heard not by grasping syllables and sounds, but also by words being present, because the intellect possesses the truth. For where the truth is, there is a proposition. And it is necessary for the proposition to be from a name and a word.

And it must be said otherwise: we use vocal organs, and we are unable to say many things at once. Of God, speaking once and all at once, we hear doubly. Stop, lest it be possible to say a third. Of God, commanding once concerning sacrifice, we hear the command both sensuously and spiritually.

Just as we understand circumcision in two ways, once spoken by God: the bodily and the spiritual. Whether the Father is God, and the Son is Lord, and the Word stands among these, or whether the same God is both God and Lord, saying, 'Visit now' (Ps 62:2a); for what is being viewed is both pious and true in both respects. It is necessary to seek how he gives to each according to his works. For if the sufferings of the present time are not worthy of the glory that is about to be revealed (Rom 8:18), and he who has worked only trifles is not punished worthily. For if one observes iniquities, 'Lord, Lord, who will endure?' (Ps 69:1), how must one take [judgment] by equality? One must oversee lest it becomes not according to quantity but according to quality; and quantity is indicated by the word, the greater things of value being given praiseworthily to the righteous and the punishment being diminished. For equality is not according to corrective justice, but according to distributive justice, the equal and the unequal.

This is accomplished for the one who has come out of ignorance and malice, as 'The night has passed, and the day has approached' (Ps 62:2a). To this, 'Out of the night my spirit watches for you, O God' (Ps 62:2b) is conjoined. But if someone does the works of the night and darkness, how can he say 'I watch at dawn' without the dawn standing before him? And 'I watch toward you' is not to be heard locally. For God is not in a place, but in a disposition, becoming a relationship toward God by having leaped over the sensible things; for to this follows coming toward God. And also the saying, 'God, the God of mine.' For the God of the saints worshipping him is God once and for all, not of all those who have the 'is', but of some who have been set free. Therefore, the belly of those having desire for luxury is not simply called God; nor even the demons are strictly gods of the Gentiles, though called gods. God alone, and every truly wise man will say by nature and truly to God, 'God, the God of mine.'

'From all those present, let my longing depart' (Ps 62:3); I thirst with the soul to be toward God, a spring of water stretching toward me, changing into eternal life (Ps 62:3). And since the soul is being benefited and enlightened, and the flesh also partakes, and of these both as being [one], how also it itself thirsts simply toward God and the power and the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Thirst of the Soul and the Mercy of God
english: His glory. And if the Father is the one who does not thirst, the only-begotten is His power and glory. For Christ is the power of God, He himself being also the glory concerning whom it is said, 'The glory of the Lord shall be seen' (Isa 60:1). And if the Son is His glory and power, the theology concerning Him and the performing of wondrous works exists according to that which is written in the Gospel, 'Power went out from him and healed all' (Mark 16:18), and again, 'And the power of God for the healing of him' (Acts 10:38).

Correspondingly, with this power and also the things concerning His glory were taken from Him, [as in] 'We have seen His glory, a glory as of the only-begotten' (John 1:14), and 'Glorify me, Father, with the glory which I had with you before the world was' (John 17:5). Therefore, on both sides it was taken, [as in] 'Let it be revealed to you in the Holy [One], because my soul thirsted for you' (Ps 42:2), and 'my flesh [thirsted] in a desert land, uninhabitable and waterless' (Ps 63:1).

And indeed the place concerning the earth is not made manifest through the word 'desert' by means of perfection, nor 'waterless' by the not having abundantly the gifts of the Spirit. [As in] 'Rivers of living water were said to flow out of the spring of the one having believed' (John 7:38); therefore also it is uninhabitable, of no one passing over it, of those imitating God as much as possible. For how could the interpreted place not be desert by reason of the lack of knowledge in it, and waterless by the becoming of the pledge of the Spirit in it? For it is not desert and waterless by a complete deprivation of those dwelling and treading, and water is said, but because these things happen in it sparsely and briefly.

And it must also be understood otherwise: the one outside of wickedness and ignorance is a desert of these things, and the one who is also outside the moisture of the passions is waterless, just as being uninhabitable means being manifest to the evil, because a place of the devil or of some other evil spirit is not found in him. Never will the unclean spirit permit itself to approach such waterless places; it passes through them without finding rest among them; [it is]...
For they are fulfilled of all good things, those who drive away and overcome every evil power.

Someone happens to see [the vision] in a desert, interpreted on both sides as an inaccessible and waterless land, while a soul thirsts in holy desire for God, with the flesh also following as much as is possible.

And another scripture is brought forward, 'And my flesh was weakened,' concerning which it must be said thus: not that my soul thirsts for God, but the flesh, enjoying thickness, being composed of shameful desires and other passions. To this, one should take the evangelical saying: 'The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak' (Matt 26:41). For if someone has readiness while thirsting with the soul for God, but the flesh is weak and yielding to [passions].

The apostle has written that piety is useful for everything, possessing the promise of life, both of the present and of the one to come (1 Tim 4:8). Regarding the present, he does not speak of the common life of living creatures, but of that which exists in life, concerning which the Savior says, 'He who believes in me has eternal life, and this is eternal life, that he may know you, the only true God, and whom you have sent, Jesus Christ' (John 17:3).

Of this present life and of the one to come, whoever becomes according to perfection, those who approach the truth face to face, the mercy of God is greater, for through it and by it one becomes in these lives, being lifted up into them. For one does not come to live both lives according to the merit of works and contemplation, but by the goodness and mercy of God.

And it is said that mercy is better than them as the cause of the agent. See then, lest the mercy spoken of here be something other than the Word of God, concerning which it is written, 'God has sent His mercy and His truth' (Ps 145:6).
See if it is possible to fill the soul; wisdom has prepared sacrifices, and the true food is the flesh of the Word, a drink rejoicing the inner man, he who harvests.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Cleaving to the Lord
english: The mind is the true vine and the true drinking of wisdom. For having been called to partake of the table prepared by wisdom, having slaughtered her own victims and having mixed her own wine, the mind, being filled with the desire of the divine banquet and expecting to be filled, says: 'Oh that my soul might be filled with satiety and drinkability' (Ps 63:5). And since, always partaking of this liturgy, it hungers because the desire of the mind is insatiable, it says 'Oh that it might be filled' and yet 'my soul has not been filled,' even though it has abundantly partaken of the food and the drink.

Let those who, after the resurrection, dream of sensible food and drink be put to shame. For it is not the flesh or the body, but the soul that is to be filled with satiety and drinkability, the desire of the soul being filled with God in good things, as it is said in another psalm. And having been filled with gladness, it rejoices gratefully toward the one who has desired the food, saying: 'And lips of gladness shall praise your name' (Ps 63:11), concerning which it is said: 'My lips shall praise you' (Ps 36:13). And virtue is the lips of gladness. For as it is said, 'members of folly,' as in the [psalm of] folly, 'the feet of those who use it bring them down' (Ps 140:12), so let not the lips also be of gladness, unless indeed in this also someone having outward things shows them through the eyes, as it was said concerning the fool, that those using them have feet bringing them down to the mire; and concerning the one rejoicing, as lips of gladness praising the approach of God.

He who avoids idleness is able to say these things, so that caring for the things of the Lord may please Him, and he who keeps his bed undefiled may honorably lie with his bride according to the holy men. Just as for the one running toward virtue and piety to reach the goal, it is said: 'I have finished the race' (2 Tim 4:7), and 'I have run without law and have directed [my course]' (Gal 5:4) (for the one who finished is the one who ran the race), so does the one following God, according to Jeremiah: 'But I have not been weary in following behind you' (Jer 2:12), and according to Hosea: 'I will go after the Lord' (Hos 2:23), and as Moses says: 'You shall go after the Lord your God' (Deut 31:8); let him finish at last the journey after God, having reached the goal of blessedness.

The end is that he will hear towards God, 'And you stand with me.' For a voice is not something of a traveler. Regarding this state, having arrived after traveling behind, as if to be joined behind, he says, 'My soul has cleaved behind you,' (Ps 63:8) signifying the voice of 'It has cleaved' [is] 'It has been united.' For it is not to be heard that those shunning the evil are being joined to the good. He shows [union] towards God, and 'He who is joined to the Lord is in the spirit.' It is not to be sought whether it is the same thing, 'My soul has cleaved behind you,' so as not to corrupt the joining to the Lord and the joining of the soul behind another, desiring the end to be the same joining to the Lord. For the end of traveling behind the Lord is the joining of the soul of the one traveling behind him; however, even if reaching [union] behind is also an end of a journey, there is nothing more perfect than the joining to the Lord in the spirit to become with him.

As he receives the things of the vision, he confesses that his soul has been cleaved behind God, grasping the right hand of God. And this is the only-begotten power of God; grasping and holding securely, the nearby visible and invisible enemies sought in vain the soul of him saying these things, unable to snatch away the one being guarded by the mighty hand of God (Ps 62:10b,11). 'Let the sinners be turned away into Sheol, all the Gentiles who forget God' (Ps 58:5) is in agreement with the entering of the wicked into the lowest parts of the earth. And having entered, they shall be delivered to punishment, the sword being signified by the name. The hands of this sword, or rather, it works pains and bitterness to those serving it, being called vessels of wrath in others. And it calls the evil powers a 'fox-catcher,' because of the cunning, deceitful, and malicious [nature] of those called fox-catchers.

And the present things are to be interpreted otherwise: since it is commanded to become material and fleshly such a one, you will say he has sunk himself down to the earth as if to have entered into its lowest parts by choice.
