Thus, being shown to be peaceful through his works, he who was born according to the flesh from a virgin is from David. Indeed, it is written concerning him, 'The Book of the generation of Jesus Christ, Son of David' (Matt 1:1).

Regarding Psalm 71:2, 'To judge your people in righteousness (clearly those of the circumcision) and your poor in judgment' (Ps 72:2); for those coming to the gospel from the nations are not called poor because of a poverty of unbelief and wickedness. But if the poor of God can be the moderate in mind, according to 'Blessed are the poor in spirit' (Matt 5:3), [then He] visits them. Regarding Psalm 71:3, [He] protects the great-minded through virtue, the high-born and those called princes, to take up peace toward the people. And even if the high-born and princes turn out to be archangels and angels, the whole human race is a people toward whom they are called to bring peace, since Jesus, through the blood of the cross, made peace between those in the heavens and those on the earth, who previously were at odds on the earth because of wickedness toward those in the heavens. Since, therefore, the one crucified...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Church as the Moon
english: The Lamb of God is sacrificed, and by this the sin of the world is released, the sin of those upon the earth; peace is being made between those in the heavens and those upon the earth, joy being made in the heavens before the angels for those repenting from sin. And if Moses and the prophets are signified by mountains and hills, let them take up peace toward the people from the nations who disbelieved, knowing what they themselves had previously spoken concerning this calling. And since even among those possessing virtue, some more so and others having it less, it must be said of those possessing it more as being increased in greater measure by practice and knowledge of the truth, that they are the higher mountains compared to the lower hills. [Ps 71:4] For it is the work of him who received from God judgment and righteousness, to judge the poor of the people.

Not such are those clinging to the letter and the shadow of the law, always named poor, seeing sharply the wealth of not having possessed the spiritual law, having that which the ones from the Jews who believed have, and the apostles also are such. Toward this also he brings salvation to the sons of the penitent. Not such are those who have come from idolatry to the faith of Jesus, those who were born of them according to the superstition of the penitent. Therefore, he will not leave them remaining in many-sided error, but will save their sons having recognized [the truth]. These having been rescued and saved, in order to judge and having come to save, he humbles the one who tyrannizes all in slander, so that he might be crushed as under the feet of the saints. For toward the righteous it is said, 'And you shall tread upon the lion and the dragon,' [Ps 71:5] and toward a man (and toward every slanderer), if he were to say, 'He will turn away slander.'

The same is said to the one remaining with the anointed, what was said to him: 'You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek,' [Ps 110:4] and 'Before the moon, generations of generations, the same one established me before the age.' [Ps 89:2] It is said 'He remains with the anointed' concerning the flesh which he clothed himself with, the soul being breathed into it, being both rational and spiritual; for he remains with the anointed of righteousness because of the indivisible union. But even before the moon, which has the analogy to the sun, there exists a generation of generations, for the church is established through him and in him, composed of all the generations.

They have it from generation to generation in succession. It is presented from the cloud of the waters as the moon is the church; but not thus: Who is she, emerging like the dew, beautiful as the moon, chosen? (Ps 71:6) Just as the rain comes upon the earth bringing fertility, so the visitation of the Savior to men has become the generation of righteousness.

It must be said that the cloud signifies Israel, and the earth signifies the Gentiles. Since previously it descended upon the cloud, and then from there upon the earth. For because Israel disobeyed and did not receive the one who had come, there was a transition to the rain upon the earth, so that all the men upon it might be moistened, rather being watered from the drops to bear spiritual fruits. (Ps 71:7) In the days of the Savior's visitation, the light of practical virtue of righteousness rises, and with it the evangelical standing through the faith of Jesus among the living, and the appropriate peace, possessing a great multitude, so as to extend until the completion of the world. For this is what the reflection of the moon signifies. (Ps 71:7b)

We say that the moon signifies the church. For the moon receives light as a derivative from the sun and does not possess it from itself; so the church, being upon the earth, knows in part and has not been truly illuminated, destined one day to be according to the sun, the perfect one... [gap] ...destined not to have been truly illuminated by appearance, then this happening according to the sun, so that it may receive the perfect [light] and face to face. For by the Word, knowing in part is abolished, and the surpassing knowledge will be established. Thus the lunar condition of the church will be abolished when the sun of righteousness comes, shining like the sun, completing the church of the righteous in the kingdom of their own Father. [gap] ...in the cloud of the waters is the perfection of the bride; and the church itself, after much progress, will be according to the sun. For who is she, he says, emerging like the dew, possessing the beginning of illumination, with which the beginning will be, as the moon, approaching? For she... [gap] ...with which there will be wonder like the sun. (Ps 71:9-11a) Understandings [are] not thus: of those from the nations, the Ethiopians.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Fruitfulness of the Support and the Drying of the Grass
english: Regarding those called through their existence out of impiety, falling down before the king in a manner of recognition, the Jews, who are the king's enemies, will indeed be lacking. And it also seems that the Ethiopians fall down before him; the falling down before the king, who sees the hidden things, demonstrates genuine submission.

It is also possible for the enemies of God to appear to have the sensation of repentance through the fact that they lack; for they are bowing down. Tharsis takes hold of the opportunity to spy out joys, spying out the joy of the friends of virtue and piety, if one might ever be able to hear: 'Come into the joy of your Lord' (Matt 25:21).

Those not having a contemplative gaze toward the joy, the kings who hold [their power] bring their gifts to those who are beginning. And islands are brought forward. But these are souls, possessing themselves firmly and unmovably, even when the sea stirs up a gale and a storm. To these, the Savior says: 'Dedicate yourselves, islands, to me, being renewed by the newness of the Spirit, bearing the new human being created according to God.'

Along with these kings, also the Arabs and Saba will bring gifts, those coming toward the evening of the faulty life, so that the light of the impious might be darkened by them. And it is possible for one to be falsely transformed into an angel of light until he deceives even the elect; for Arabs are interpreted as morning and evening. After these Arabs and many others, repentance is offered by Saba; and the name is taken for the return.

It is possible to take as those worshiping him and offering gifts the teachers of all the nations, the apostles and disciples and the successors of these; for they offer gifts to God from the men who are profited by them. And if even one of the faithful brings gifts of praiseworthy deeds and true mindset, it is as if kings bring their own gifts to the only and one All-King. It is also written that his name is honored, having delivered them from so many evils (Ps 72:14). Having learned, the holy men, that no one of the born [humanity] will deliver men from the prevailing wickedness, all turned away and were made blameless concerning the [unclear]...

Wishing to be saved from the hand of the powerful and becoming a cause of eternal salvation, they were continually and unceasingly sending prayer to the Father, at times saying, 'Show us, Lord, your mercy and grant us your salvation,' and at other times, 'Send out your light and your truth.' Concerning his sending and at the beginning of the present Psalm 71, they prayed saying, 'O God, give your judgment to the king and your righteousness to the son of the king' (Ps 71:15c).

They glorify him through all the days of this present age or of the enlightened life of those blessing (Ps 71:16a). The outcomes of the anticipatory proclamations are more extreme than these mountains, for the one prophesied has become a support in the land (Ps 71:16a).

For Jesus did not bear fruit through the arrival of faithful men, and they possess a multitude and greatness of deeds and theorems; but a witness to this is [the promise] that 'the righteous shall flourish like a palm tree, and like a cedar in Lebanon he shall multiply' (Ps 71:16bc). For when the fruit of the support has been multiplied and exceeded, the Jews who were unfaithful to the Savior shall spring up from the city of Jerusalem like grass from the earth, because of the parched state and the rapid drying up, so named and most justly.

Since they have become flesh in their wisdom, having been unfaithful to the Savior and seeking glory from one another rather than that which is given by God alone, they shall spring up from the earth as grass; for all flesh is grass and all the glory of man is like the flower of the grass. For they shall not merely bloom, but shall spring up [and wither].

And also those of the grass, whether out of the city or not in the city, shall spring up, those of whom the word is. For those who hastened toward life and wisdom outside the spiritual city, Jerusalem, were dried up like the parched and rapidly drying grass; but of the one remaining within the city, nothing of this sort was experienced; for 'he who dwells in Jerusalem shall never be shaken' (Ps 71:17c–19a).

The nations, which are to be blessed in him, make happy the one who blessed them, saying, 'Blessed is the Lord, the God of the discerning race, who alone has done wondrous things, having freed us from idolatry and the treatment of wandering demons; for truly it is a wonder.'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The progression of impiety and the rejection of Providence
english: Regarding what concerns the calling of the Gentiles. The 'Only One' should not be troubled, for the Son cannot do anything contrary to the Father, unless he sees the Father doing it; for whatever the Father does, the Son likewise does. For the 'Only One' and such things taken regarding divinity declare a Father and a Son, as it is presented from the prophet; for it is said to the Father: 'And the Sabaean men shall pass over high upon you and shall worship you and shall pray to you, that what is in you is God and is not God except you; for you are God, and not to be feared, God of Israel, Savior' (Ps 72:1,2). Who is the glory whose name is blessed, who having arrived has made glorious and honorable those from the worthless and gloryless who are the repentant men? It is possible to call his glory and he did not receive an unsung death for the sake of the salvation of the world; for Jesus was not yet glorified, and the Jesus whom we see being humbled through the suffering of death is being crowned with glory and honor.

If indeed his glory is that which his name is blessed for unto the age, concerning which Paul writes: 'Not worthy are the sufferings of the present time compared to the glory that is about to be revealed to us, stand fast' (Rom 8:18). For especially this and the proclamation concerning it we find to be eternally hymned, as Peter said; thus says the witness of his sufferings and of the glory about to be revealed: 'And a companion of that glory' (2 Pet 1:11). And Israel seeing God is interpreted. Therefore also, those not seeing him, they perceive what is good (Ps 72:6b-9). For indeed, although it provides something dark and unpleasant to men, they perceive how it also works advantageously toward salvation, and their steps are not shaken having crossed over and having advanced. Since those about whom the word is, are held not by practical wickedness alone but also by impiety, followingly they are clothed in injustice.

And [there is] the moral wickedness according to the soul, and with this impiety, they think impiously concerning all dogmas. And also to say that their injustice will come forth as from a cloud; then, when it comes forth, the sin is practically fulfilled, no longer remaining only in the thoughts. It has passed into a disposition of the heart.

Having previously disposed themselves according to wickedness, they not only established the evil to themselves but also desired to be harmful to others. Then, after passing into a disposition of wickedness, having thought in malice, they spoke deceitfully as if of good things. They were lifted up, he says, as if to speak even against God, slandering His justice, His creation, and His providence; such as are those who, at the time of the stars, having set their preconceptions, and those who, making the heavens and the creation [themselves] instead of the Creator, lift up their mouth to heaven. They were torn apart, rather they were consumed, as if their tongue had passed through the earth against the Most High, so that all who hear might know what vain and impious things are being philosophized against God and His providence (Ps 72:10).

Of the impious boasting loudly (Ps 72:10), the people of God calls as a starting point for a good return, desiring to enjoy the contemplations of the light of day. And the 'Here' [referring to] the one saying this is God, such as what was said to Moses: 'And you shall stand with me' (Ex 33:33).

Those wanting to cast out providence and injustice, having spoken toward the height (Ps 72:11-13), bring forth such words; how can one know God through human things? For does [the intellect] not have a sensory, organic power? For his understanding does not receive the forms of the seen and the heard, so that, having known, he might also know providential and royal things as he wishes? And having said before, 'How will God be known?', they confess to knowing God, but they are ignorant of the manner of knowing. And after these things they also say they are ignorant of Him, saying, 'If there is knowledge in the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Beastly State and the Proximity of God
english: a disposition according to quality

He turns toward other things. Ps 72:22b, 23a: 'I have become like a beast in your sight.' For just as all creatures are ignorant toward the Father of wisdom and the God of knowledge, according to what was said by Moses, he who does not know the God of the Word—'I am the Word'; for how would one not compare the Word and the most wise Word? In this way it is said again by Moses: 'I am not able to speak from before I began to speak to your servant; heavy of mouth and slow of tongue am I.' For it is not simply being heavy of mouth and slow of tongue and not being able for oneself, but rather after [having begun] to speak to your servant. In this way also Abraham [spoke] to the Creator: 'Since I began to speak to the Lord, I myself am earth and ashes,' he who was ignorant before speaking to God. And he stands forth through the [fact that he] was born, as if he were not being troubled by sin among men, but rather he perceives things not by chance, but as bringing them about by his own wise providence. And it is not by chance to say, 'I am always with you,' but only to the one possessing virtue and piety in an orderly and consistent manner, which is made straight through the intervals.

Ps 72:27, 28: 'Since God is not in a place, locally no one is separated from him, but he is far from the thought of the unrighteous and evil, and near to the righteous and good and the cause of all things; and since the approaching of virtue takes hold of him and saves, the standing away from him having badness and impiety brings destruction.' The same applies to the distancing of God through sin. It is fitting that it is said: 'Behold, those who distance themselves shall perish,' not that those who distance [themselves] should cause those who have sinned to perish by imposing an end to sin through repentance. In this way also, he who does [the sin] but not he who made the sin is a slave to it. Having moved many to long [distances] and many words concerning the essence of the good, the wise man presented his presence to him through brevity, saying that the good is strictly to be joined to God and to place hope upon him. And it is said that the gates of Zion are virtues and introductions into perfection, and all the daughter of Zion becomes she who is born according to her and a soul profiting toward her. Ps 73:1b: One inquires what is the cause of falling to the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Fleshly Food of the Ethiopians and the Lion of the Enemy
english: They stand around, preventing her from approaching and making her stay, and her things are present. God rejects the sinner, after he has first distanced himself. For he says, 'He who comes to me I will by no means cast out' (John 6:37). Do not think the wrath and anger of God is against us; it is far from senselessness. For regarding God, no human passion is indicated, but rather the exceeding turning away through the words spoken, for he says he endures the sheep of his pasture. The pasture of God is the words of the Spirit, the law and the prophets, in which as a shepherd pastures the righteous sheep.

The whole life of man is taken as a sea raised for contemplation. God strengthened this by his power to lead it from more abundant snow and more intense storm into happiness and serenity, as it is said, 'He who turns the sea into dry land' (Ps 74:13). The Savior crushed not the many heads of many dragons, but also the many heads of one upon the water, the water being understood as the wickedness of the unstable and disordered affairs of life. For in such water the dragons work harmfully, and he who excels them is written about as king over all those in the waters and how he dwells in the sea.

For this great and spacious sea shows the turbulence of affairs and the wickedness, saying, 'In this small animals are tossed with large ones, and ships are driven about by playing with the dragon within it' (Ps 74:14). Many heads of dragons are crushed; these are the rulers of this age who promise wisdom, and with them principalities and powers, cosmic rulers of this world, and also spiritual evils and the whole host of demons and opposing powers. And the heads of these dragons are divinations, sorceries, superstitions, and all that contributes to idolatry, but also false doctrines and deceptive practices. The work of the Savior alone is to crush the heads of the said dragons. It did not seem to be possible from any other than him to be strong. Since, however, he did not crush the heads of the dragon alone, al-

And he provided all of it, this food, for the Ethiopian peoples. For he did not need others to be carried away by the flesh and parts of it, nor the Ethiopian peoples, being sons of darkness and night through ignorance. Just as the flesh of Jesus is true food, since all the sons of light are nourished from its use and eating, being enlightened beyond a white snow, so the Ethiopian children of the inner man will be fed with the fleshly [parts] (that is, the things of wickedness and false glory), which will be handed over to the desires of their hearts into uncleanness, and additionally into passions of dishonor and an unproven mind.

He began from the flesh of the numbering to show that the year begins from the flesh, starting from the spring equinox, the beginning of the months and the first in the months of the year, which Moses announced (Ps 73:17b). An enemy mocking the Lord, the devil, but the people is a flock of the other invisible and evil powers (Ps 73:18). The high priest Caiaphas, the enemy, mocked the Savior Christ, and the people, having cried out the Jews, provoked his name: 'Aaron, Aaron, crucify him' (Ps 73:18–21). It is not true the preceding [text] regarding the taking of sensible beasts. For many perfect men, witnesses of the truth, were eaten by beasts. Let it be said, therefore, that a soul confessing [its faith] will not be handed over to those beasts, concerning whom it is written, 'A wandering sheep of Israel; lions drove him out.' The Lord crushed the teeth of these lions. Satan is among these, as the apostle Peter writes, 'Your adversary the devil walks like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour' (1 Peter 5:8). But the poor of God are those who are able, having left his [possessions] having been deprived of wealth, according to those saying, 'Behold, we have left all and have followed you,' whereas others become differently poor, having cast away the wealth of wickedness in false glory. But if those named now the poor of God possess [nothing] even to the poor in spirit, consider this. After these things, he entreats God to look upon the covenant which he established with the fathers around Abraham, so that he may not leave the ones from his seed incomplete.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Pillars of the Ordered Earth
english: It must be said that the clouds of iniquity have filled those who are darkened in the earth; for they do not walk upon the earth [as citizens of heaven], but because of this they have an earthly veil of life, their intellect being darkened by ignorance. (Ps 74:1)

If to corrupt and to be corrupted is often, according to the Divine Scripture, to sin, then incorruption and to possess it signifies virtue; for it is said, 'The grace is with those who love our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruption.' And since it is necessary for Him who began the good work to bring it to completion, that is to say, to lead it to an end, 'Lest you be corrupted' is said, fleeing corruption until the end, so that no one remains in it but remains in incorruption. And this achievement is great, so a Psalm of song is sent up regarding its fulfillment. Having reached the end so as not to be corrupted, with incorruption having been achieved, we shall thankfully confess to you, God, as the cause of the good things that have existed and are being achieved; for with you and from you these are made firm. And we desire to receive even more upon the good things having been achieved; for we are not yet perfect. We shall indeed confess concerning the things that have existed, but we shall call upon your favor in order to receive more. And if those who confess and call upon [you] are perfect, they confess on behalf of those who have received in fullness, calling upon [you] for their protection, so that what was given by the heavenly Father might remain with those asking for it. (Ps 74:4b)
And Didymus similarly explained this. (Ps 74:4,5a)

To dwell in the earth as a resident instead of a speck is taken as being a sojourner upon praise; for it is said, 'Woe to all those who dwell in the earth,' (Ps 74:4) and 'From the face of the north shall the evils be burned upon those who dwell in the earth.' (Isa 15:2) Truly, being one who dwells in the earth, it happens to become fat from thinking of earthly things and doing the works prescribed of the flesh, and to be subject to its intellect happens to become filth toward God because of dwelling in the earth. This thickness coming from evil, through which the heart of the burning people was thickened, the piercing teaching of the Savior stretched out, concerning which it is said, 'What Fire came to be cast upon the earth.' (Luke 12:49) And since it is necessary not only to be consumed from the thing falling away, but the evil...

Because of the predetermination of those being held, the spirit commands the deeds of the body to die and the spirit to walk, so that we do not fulfill the desire of the flesh. Regarding the pillars of this ordered earth, those having a well-tuned and true mindset, the heralds of truth say, the Savior, establishing them in the house of God, does not make them unsteady (Ps 74:4,5a).

Having strengthened the pillars of the church, he grants to the rest not to deviate. He says this regarding the established order and the completed work of Christ, through whom the earth and all who dwell in it were ordered. Furthermore, to the inhabitants of the whole inhabited world, it was testified through the apostles not to deviate nor to speak injustice against God, paying heed to the many errors. But to dwell on the earth is from above as if being received in praise, whereas to reside as a sojourner is as if being received in mockery. For he says, 'Woe to all those dwelling on the earth' (Luke 12:53), and 'From the face of the north shall the evils be burned upon those dwelling on the earth' (Isa 7:4).

For the one thinking of the things on the earth and doing the works of the flesh, his mindset is made fat toward God because of dwelling on the earth, according to [the saying]: 'He was made fat, enlarged, and left [empty].' Such were those whose covering they closed up in the earth, concerning whom it has been said, 'Their iniquity shall come out like the scent of a covering.' The piercing teaching of the Savior, having said, 'Fire has come to be cast upon the earth' (Luke 12:49), has stretched out such a fatness of wickedness.

But since even by predetermination wickedness must be consumed, and not by the one commanding alone, we are commanded to let the deeds of the body die and to walk by the spirit, so that we may not fulfill the desire of the flesh. The Savior strengthens the pillars of this ordered earth, those having a well-tuned life and a true mindset; rather, regarding the heralds of truth, it has been said, 'Pillars of heaven were stretched out,' having been winged with heavenly wings, as it is said concerning them, 'He who is heavenly, such also are the heavenly ones.' It has also been written concerning all of the glorious church, to which Christ presented himself as a 'pillar and foundation of the truth' (1 Tim 3:15). The Savior, establishing all these pillars in the house of God, does not make them unsteady, saying, 'I will lay the foundation of my holy house' (Ps 74:7b).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Breaking of Horns and the Dwelling of God
english: They say [it is a sign] of virtue and piety. But a sign of their wickedness is that they turn away from sacrifices as if they were harmful, unless they receive residue, smoke, and ash; but the pious, knowing God, are free from the thinking of fate and sorcery.

Similarly Didymus says. The faithful, being pious, are such that the works of providence come not from the east or the west, nor from wicked caretakers, but from God. He himself establishes kings and removes them; he raises the poor from the earth and from poverty lifts up the needy (Ps 74:7-8). Regarding the verse about receiving from the Gentiles and from the circumcised people, one must also stand regarding the humbling of the circumcised and the lifting up of the Gentiles (Ps 74:9).

An opposition seems to be signified from the being full of the cup of mixture, with the mind being uncontrolled in it. But the uncontrolled does not oppose the mixture; for the uncontrolled [voice] is homonymous, sometimes signifying that the mind does not differ from the uncontrolled, and at other times presenting the one who is pure as being toward a liquid. It also presents a third meaning: that when a mixture has become, from mind and water, with the mind prevailing, we call the mixture 'the mixture'.

The third thing, therefore, signifies what is about to be said: God mixing into the mixture for those being judged a good intention, so that the one being punished might not be punished unworthily, having done [this] without anyone standing over him, observing the sins that occurred; God brought the judgment according to which the lawless one is punished. This cup in the hand of God is tilted from one to another, many a time for the one being punished, so that through the evils he did, he might be justified by repentance, and the one who was glorifying himself for a little while might fall into being good. However, even if it tilts from this to that, the reaper does not pour out upon men, but upon the sinners of the earth, and upon the devil and the robbers.

...demons. [Ps 74:10-11] When the righteous ones speaking against God are reproved and those following them are finished, I give thanks that I am not found responsible for any of those accused; I rejoice and sing for ever to the God of the patriarch Jacob, who has given me strength, as if to break all the horns of the sinners, which they used against the weaker ones, being like horned bulls. Who are these? It was shown in the assembly of the bulls among the cows of the peoples.

Having said this, he did not bring forth 'And my horns shall be exalted,' but 'of the righteous.' This is customary for the saints through approaching blindness; and they teach that it is for every man to exist in Christ, so that the righteous, having broken the horns of the sinners, may have his horn exalted. And also to say it in a plural way: the horns of the sinners are being broken, but in a singular way: the horn of the righteous is exalted. For every sinner is a multitude, because they are found not to coexist with one another, but evils following virtues like seeds, because of being a middle state. Therefore, let many men have righteousness (which is virtue in general), and they are called righteous in the singular.

[Ps 75:2] It is not the same to be the knowing and the known, so that the known, being known, might be able to be known even of the unknown. For in this way, according to what was said in Judea, that God is known, and following that, in the one inhabiting Judea, Israel, great is His name, I say, of the known.

[Ps 75:3-4] In every way the disturbance of passions and the war of evils must be driven away, so that having the peace which surpasses all understanding, we may become a place of God. For we shall not only be His habitation, but also intending to be observers of truth and virtue; for His habitation is found in the given Zion. The things said will be applied to the holy church, as a place of God established in peace and the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Rider and the Horses of the Soul
english: His dwelling-place. For he says, 'Sing to the Lord who dwells in Zion.' And since these things are established not by our power but by the grace of God, the word attributes to Him the cause of peace, saying: 'There He crushed the powers of bows, the shield and the sword and war' (Ps 75:5-7). For peace prevails in the place of God once the rulers of bows are crushed, from whom the evil one, sending his flaming arrows, was making afflictions and disordered movements, of which he was the cause. Along with the aforementioned bows, the related shield and sword are also crushed, and along with them, those called war are crushed; for the Lord is the one crushing wars (Ps 75:5-7).

And the holy men, looking ahead eternally, namely the unseen and eternal things, from which God illuminates differently the light of the knowledge of Christ—first before the manifestation through prophets and Moses, and after this through apostles and evangelists, so that those being illuminated become light, as Paul says: 'The God who said, Let light shine out of darkness, has shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God' (2 Cor 4:6). And He marvelously added to the illuminating, that which He promises as knowledge to others, and by this God illuminates more paradoxically into knowledge and wisdom for the holy ones through both revelations and visions, seeing marvelously from the things mentioned. And even if it is not in Judea, as the Scripture says, these high contemplations and the doctrines of godliness are seen, and from these God marvelously illuminates those coming into the knowledge of truth. Often in the Scripture, intelligible things and angels are seen, from which God again illuminates, sending them into service for those about to inherit salvation. And to each of the editions it will be fitting [to say]: 'Draw near to the eternal things, protected by God for those who desire godliness, benefiting the prudent through the virtue of the present.' For understanding is a good thing for all who practice it. The senseless are troubled by both afflictions and wickedness; they are also troubled by both sensible and invisible deceivers, according to the [scripture]: 'Their senseless heart was darkened.' For to be darkened and to be troubled are the same; for each denotes ignorance, with the mind being darkened in both cases. And God is called the Jacob of the ascetic and man...

A good and righteous [state] is maintained against the reproach of one falling from these through personal laziness, being established by reproof. For some say that bodies are like vehicles and horses of the souls. In these horses, those riding themingly desire the beginning of sleep, being drawn into a false breath of those who inhale the body and enslave it with skill, those sitting upon the horses.

Indeed, one sees in the Scripture the rider as being mostly falsely named, as also in Zechariah the prophet there is a threat of God: 'And I will strike every horse in ecstasy and the rider in thoughtlessness' (Zechariah 11:7); and according to Moses, a horse and a rider was thrown into the sea—and riders being praised. For instance, toward Elijah, Father Elisha, the army of Israel and his rider; and toward the Savior it is announced: 'Ride upon your horses, and your riding is salvation' (Psalm 75:8).

No one among the wretched is able to stand against God when He is angry, creating fear for those being judged, so that they might not overlook the One who knows the heart (Psalm 75:7). For those having the word toward Him as toward a judge say: 'Lord, Lord, if He observes iniquity, who will stand?' Moreover, even if no one will be able to stand against His wrath, being terrible, yet He Himself, through the coming goodness with mercy, judges. For mercy and judgment are yours, Lord.

Judgment listens from heaven, making everything happen according to the word of providence for the benefit of each. This agrees with what is in the prophecy of Amos: 'The Lord doing judgment, He has set high judgment and righteousness in the earth' (Amos 5:24). For as it is in heaven, He does all judgment in the high place; and as He listens from heaven, sending judgment from it to those on earth, He has set righteousness in the earth as the end of judgments (Psalm 75:11).

The hidden thing of man is in the mind. He who cleanses this will confess to God with gladness. Then he will celebrate in doing what is profitable, and he will be able to think the truths. If, however, 'He will confess' denotes the disclosure of sins, the understanding of the matter will be this: since the one desiring to be perfectly holy must not cleanse himself in solitary acts and words alone, he must confess while rebuking himself regarding a very brief thought. This...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Authenticity of Voice and the Guarding of the Heart
english: He is able to be made manifest from [the prayer], 'Cleanse me from my secret sins.' If one does not even imply something regarding the non-existence [of sin], a confession might not occur; consequently, the remnant of the man's inner mind is celebrated having been found outside of all evil. Or, when the doubt concerning him is taken away by the manifestation of purity, the saint celebrates—not sometimes and sometimes not, but steadily and always knowing the truth and acting according to righteousness. For this is truly the feast according to the apostle who said, 'Let us celebrate, not in leaven of malice and wickedness, but in unleavened bread of sincerity and truth' (1 Cor 5:8).

He is terrible before the kings of the earth, who struck down Pharaoh, and pursued Nebuchadnezzar of men, altering his thinking as if his life were among beasts (Ps 76:13); he deprived Saul of the spirit, who, despising the covenant of God, [was rejected by] Samuel; for it is said, 'The Spirit of the Lord departed from Saul' (1 Sam 16:14), and he was oppressed by an evil spirit from the Lord, sent upon him by judgment and vote. And if even concerning ecclesiastical leaders these things are to be considered, hold fast to the God-breathed Scripture. For Paul, having called the elders of Miletus, says to them, 'Take heed to yourselves and to all the flock in which the Holy Spirit of God has made you overseers, and with Him, and also from among yourselves some will arise speaking twisted things, that is, the divine Spirit of the terrible ones being taken away' (Acts 20:28-30).

When the one speaking has departed far off, with a strained voice (Ps 76:2). Since, therefore, the begotten essence is separated from the One who made [all], a cry according to the intellect is necessary. He is called God because He made all things, and Lord because He rules over those things which come from Him. And it is said, God indeed the Father, and Lord the Son. But to the one speaking, the day is one of affliction, his whole life, indeed, the age which has come upon him, in which he seeks God as one would seek a physician for a disease, calling out. He seeks [Him] through deed and disposition, not being deceived like those who are ignorant of the end regarding circumstances, just as Saul went to a medium and was deceived. But the saint, who is not troubled, seeks God in the night called the ignorance of circumstances, according to the...

According to Isaiah, my soul became attached to a mortal, not being self-sufficient for all the consolation of the memory concerning God. To this, what is in Isaiah also applies: 'In trouble of the Lord I remembered' (Isa 26:3). According to the common habit of many, a wandering voice indicates something superficial, but according to the Scripture and being placed upon one who is praised, it is [authentic].

For Anna, praying genuinely toward God, being called by the priest's child to persist in prayer, answers: 'From a multitude of wanderings I have wasted away until now.' And concerning Isaac, that which says: 'He went out to wander in the field.' But you will receive something superficial if you receive the one who explained to me unlawful wanderings.

If indeed the word were ever said by the divine scholars, having understood the sequence and the speaking person, we would receive the voice either for the better or for the evil. Now, therefore, both the person and the word are praised; the spirit did not faint, which indicates the soul. For even Stephen did not say, 'Lord Jesus, receive my spirit' (Luke 22:43), but, having been faint-souled because of the enemies lying in wait, he gave himself to God.

My eyes preceded the guards (Ps 76:5). Another scripture is brought forward, not saying: 'I have preceded the guards,' but: 'All my enemies preceded the guards.' Concerning many guards happening against me, he was guarding the saying: 'With all vigilance, keep your heart.' They preceded them, those which were about to make me faint-souled, all my enemies; for they were not few, but rather all, and they were filled against me.

Therefore, also, they having become more dominant, I have seen in a certain foreknowledge that I would undergo trouble, but I did not utter anything troubling, nor in any disposition have I become disturbed; for the things of judgment and foreknowledge were not at all heavy upon me, nor had I been made in a passionate fear. For indeed I uttered nothing, whereas those who have shrunk in courage love to speak.

If the guards were to speak in a masculine way, he would say that all the thoughts, that I ought to stand regarding myself to guard me, all my enemies reached me instead of those guarding, casting unlawful and harmful thoughts. Let these things be said concerning invisible enemies. And if the divisions of the night are also called guards (if it should happen, he says, to lose the night being filled according to...)
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Soul, Divine Mercy, and the Way of God
english: Regarding Ephraim, all enemies will lay hold of these strongholds, anticipating them; for they will not sleep unless they have afflicted [him] (Ps 76:6).

Having these things happen to me, he says, I awoke myself to remember the former and many anticipating circumstances (not only me but also my virtuous fathers) from which all the Lord rescued me and them; by which reason I have become more cheerful to endure unto the end, so that I might happen to have salvation from the struggles of such things; for he who endures unto the end, he shall be saved. For having conversed with the ancient days and the eternal ages, having remembered and having meditated, I found many times both myself and the rest of men falling into such a state of helplessness, as to leave behind salvation and all hope; but, having been established in confidence toward God, every helplessness in those who grasp [the truth] is overcome. You shall remember when the Hebrew multitude comes toward the things laid before you by the valleys of the sea; for no good hope remaining there, suddenly God provided abundance in narrowness and in remote helplessness (Ps 76:7).

Throughout all this life, because of the encroaching ignorance of things, being called night, I did not deliver myself to sleep and heart like other men, but toward sobriety and alertness I stirred myself up; for those sleeping at night sleep and at night they get drunk. With my heart, that is, with my mind, I was conversing with myself about the actions and natures of things (for know what the present things are approaching), I learned what the end of the surrounding evils will be. And I was tilling my spirit with the art of farming, desiring to sow into it, so that from it I might reap eternal life; for he who sows into the spirit, from the spirit he will reap eternal life (2 Cor 9:6). And it is not to be thought that to say 'spirit' is to speak synonymously, but rather homonymously regarding the present word and that which was previously set forth; for there the soul was called spirit, but here the spirit of the man is that which is in him. For if even here the spirit is said instead of the soul, who is the one tilling his spirit and idling with his heart? For it is not the body that does these things.

For the soul is not strictly a human being when it is wandering aimlessly apart from the mind and unsettling the spirit joined to the mind. I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray also with the mind; I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing also with the mind. Corruption is the departure from natural goodness, which occurs not while the essence remains, but if something belonging to the natural state is taken away from it. Previously, he was willing to help and was favorable to those asking of him, as I reasoned: 'I remembered the days of old.' Was his goodness not present until those times, and no longer being added to, he was willing to be favorable? No, by no means. For his mercy is not cut off from the former generation, nor does it fail regarding the coming one. For they think that the end of his mercy is this: that he might do good and show mercy to one generation, and not to another. Nor will he fail to have compassion, just as neither fire nor light fails to shine and to warm. For his mercies are held in check by a temporary anger arising from sin, but they are not joined in a way that lasts forever.

Even though many troubles have come upon me, they cast a disturbance into me (Ps 76:8-10). What has been recounted followed in all the appointed words, but also, having understood things, I observed that God is not being thrust away for the ages, nor has He chosen to do other things, as if in some way to cast down a different beginning of a kind of life. For through all those things I have passed through, I have begun the Now, changing all those things that disturbed and frightened me, so that I might become courageous for the rest. This change is not a change of quality (for I have passed from one disposition to another), but an alteration, not caused by another, but by the right hand of the Most High. For He also provided these thoughts and brought them together so that I might be altered.

This aimless wandering is like the one from above is good; for it is a good thing to speak often of the wonders of God. Since God dwells and walks among the saints (Ps 76:14a), He has in each of the saints his own way, traveling according to the intellect of each of them. And since his Word is said to be a Way ('I am the Way,' He says [John 14:6]),
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Redemption of the Two Peoples and the Marks of the Way
english: But His word is in nothing trivial, for it is a way; rather, it is rightly said that the indwelling voice is in the saints alone. Regarding Psalm 76:14b, greatness is said of the intelligible substance by excellence of power, not by quantity. No god is found as great as ours.

He does not say that the gods are the idols or the demons (for these are called gods), but rather those who, having become toward us through the word of God, were made divine. For they are not partakers of divinity, but merely partakers. The present word is said of the Savior, as he will declare the following, being a great God and Father, since he is the Son of the great God.

Regarding Psalm 76:15a, after the article, the Savior is called God, so that he might be shown as different from those to whom it is said, 'You are gods' (Ps 82:6). None of them is as one who excels. After the article, it is said, 'God.' Such is also the Only-begotten God who is in the bosom of the Father, to be God by being alone in essence; for none of the others is only-begotten, but with the only-begotten is God. According to the same divinity, the only-begotten God and the Father God are.

Indeed, it is said of the Savior (of his one divinity and that of the Father), 'God is in you, and there is no god besides you; for you are God, and we shall not fear' (Ps 86:5). For how can it be that if God is in him, there is no god besides him, and he himself is God, unless we understand that the Father and the Son have the same divinity, so as to be one God, Father and Son, and not a Son and a Father? For the Father is the Father of the Son, and the Son is the Son of the Father. Therefore, the 'I and the Father are one' follows the 'I and the Father are one' being said, not the Son saying 'I and the God.' For the Father is not another Son, nor is God another, by the being of the same divinity of the offspring and of the begetter.
Regarding Psalm 76:15b.16, the Savior made his power known among both peoples, to the...

He performed many paradoxical wonders among the nations and the circumcised; for power went out from him and healed everyone. But also by his arm (I mean by his energy and action) he redeemed his people, the two united, having tasted death above all things by the grace of God, giving his soul as a ransom for many; for by his precious blood we were redeemed from our vain, ancestral conduct. The peoples are those in whom he made his power known, whom he also joined together into one people, whom he redeemed: the sons of Jacob and Joseph, the sons of Jacob who are circumcised and believe, and the sons of Joseph who are from the nations. For Joseph is interpreted as 'Addition of the Lord'; for God truly added to those being saved from the circumcised, those from the nations who believe. And 'He made known' does not signify the beginning of knowing, but that which is come to be known and recognized; for saying 'He who works wonders,' he recognizes these things through these words.

When the Savior appeared on earth, the earth endured confusion and trembling (Ps 76:19-21)—that is, the things on earth, which are above all laws and are fearful of all gods, through whose ordinances the demons are overturned; but also the earth endured confusion and trembling because of men, who are bound by passions and are being turned toward the Word of Christ. And the sea, the present life, Jesus God alone bound, so as to leave behind traces and proofs of the way, so that those wishing to follow him might follow; for he says, 'Your paths are in many waters, and your tracks shall not be known' (Ps 77:20), because the word of his journey is incomprehensible. And the sheep of Christ were led by God in practice (symbolically called by the hand) of the spiritual law and the priestly word. And Christ has become for us both, being himself the spiritual law, of the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Spiritual Rock and the Nature of Sin
english: He is the initiator and high priest of the spiritual rite of God, having traversed the heavens. He signifies Moses as the law, and Aaron as the high priest; therefore they are brothers, being sons of the divine providence which brought forth this law and the appropriate high-priestly word for it; for by its will these good things have been raised up to men (Ps 77:1a).

He is able to call all the old scripture 'the law' present here. If the commanding and forbidding word were to signify the voice of the law according to the preceding verse, it commands the law to take heed how those having received the command, choosing the good and fleeing the bad, might act rightly (Ps 77:3).

These things those having the mind of Christ understood and perceived spiritually; for it was not hidden from them, having been explained to them according to knowledge. And they themselves did not reveal to their own children born of them through instruction the matters from the beginning, so that they might be known and not hidden even to their next generation.

For he who becomes with God in spirit, coming from Him, is trusted to understand and is confirmed according to the spirit (Ps 77:8d). It is to be thought that 'spirit' here refers to the intellect, according to what was said concerning the Virgin, how she [conceived] by the Holy Spirit and body; for in these things 'spirit' calls her opinion and her disposition, and from which having been sanctified, the body also comes to be sanctified, being served by sanctifying energies. And if the soul itself is spirit and is called so here, it is to be noted.

Regarding the manna given before the rebellion, the psalm says after the rebellion that both the manna and the meat were given (Ps 77:17–22). But this is not the question. For the psalm joins together things in different times, bringing together one rebellion having occurred in different times under one cause. For if someone should interpret the first rebellion as that before the making of the Tabernacle in the second month of the Exodus, he does not place that history in its proper time in the psalm; for not then did the water from the rock happen to be given, nor did the punishment of fire follow, and indeed the firstlings were not [slain] and they did not unrighteously disbelieve regarding the paradoxical gift of food...

You act with small-spiritedness because you do not immediately find abundance. Therefore, even Moses did not yield to the small-spiritedness of the people. In the second dispute concerning meats, Moses also bears it with difficulty; and it is fitting that the punishment from God was somewhat sent to them, and they were being consumed by fire. It is necessary to believe from those who were previously warned, not believing in the divine power, and it is necessary to hope for salvation from Him, not hoping.

It must also be said by way of upward leading: in the wilderness of the Son, much ignorance of things prevails. Having passed through and having divided his most meager word, a rock called [it], a great watering has become for those being benefited, as if the flowing water were cast alongside an indescribable abyss in depth and breadth. For the water sent forth from this rock flowed like rivers (Ps 77:17–25a). And regarding these rivers, the Savior says: 'He who believes in me, as the Scripture says, from his spiritual belly (that which is according to the inner man) will flow rivers of living water' (John 7:38). And he says, the writer says, that those who believe will not receive this concerning the Spirit. For the water of these rivers is drawn out from a rock, about which Paul says: 'From a spiritual [rock] that follows' (1 Cor 10:4); and the rock is Christ. Christ himself, since he is a rock, says concerning the water of the rivers: 'For from me he will take and will declare to you all things' (John 14:26).

And they added to this: sinning against him—not all who sin against God are sinning against him, but only those who have known his will and are not doing it. Certainly even David, not being ignorant of God's will, says: 'Against you only have I sinned' (Ps 51:4). Perhaps for those sinning in ethical matters, the sin becomes toward men; but for those blaspheming God and providence, the sin, being a certain impiety, rises up against God. For if someone sins against a man, and prays for him; but if he sins against the Lord God, who will pray for him? Certainly, what they overthrew the Most High with, they were lacking in a dry place, being deprived of the spiritual waters; for they turned away from the water from the aforementioned rock. And finding themselves in a dry place, they did not experience the goodness of God which is sweet. But that which is according to virtue and wisdom makes it sweet.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Ascent of Wrath and the Nature of Heavenly Signs
english: Being put into action and being contemplated. They tested Him not in their hearts superficially, but from the depth of their own ruling principle, thinking against God and doubting His power to request food for their souls—not the souls made in the image and likeness of God (for they feed on the bread of life and the fruit of the tree of life), but the souls being transformed into flesh because they have succumbed to material things, desiring not beneficial and healthy foods, but pleasant and disease-causing ones.

The soul that desires food, the desiring and appetitive one, is a rational power in us. For concerning this, it is said, 'And let your soul desire meat' (Psalm 34:8). The irrational animals also participate in this, desiring and being appetitive for food. And they spoke against God, saying, 'Will God not be able to prepare a table in the wilderness?' and the following things; but He has indeed given bread having come down from heaven and prepared a table before His people. Wisdom says, 'She has laid her victims and mixed her wine in the vessel; and none of the unbelieving shall taste them' (Wisdom 18:6). To this, you will receive the 'For I say to you, none of those men shall taste my supper' (Luke 22:27).

Because of this, the Lord was angry and cast down, as if to pay attention to them. This was followed by the fire of desires being kindled upon Jacob; or rather, the [fire] decided and laboring for the sake of virtue, or the fire kindled from God, which is able to consume by their blessing their material choice and their disposition. Consequently, by this fire, wrath ascended upon Israel. For from when they were practicing lower things, the wrath, having perceived, ascended upon Israel. And perhaps wrath descends upon those lying below the strangers of godliness, according to what is said: 'For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven upon all ungodliness and injustice of men' (Romans 1:18). And wrath ascends upon those called to do what God wills, through having been called from above. Therefore, the care for Israel, who ought to look above, has ascended, as it is said: 'the wrath has ascended.' 'Stop, if those serving [God] happen to be vessels of wrath through the punishments from God,' [they] serve similarly as vessels of wrath.

They are called. And the wrath, which is not said to be below, ascends upon the former Israel. This accords with: 'If the spirit of the ruler ascends upon you, let him not leave your place' (1 Sam 2:9). For in these things the unclean spirit is said to be below, which ascends toward. Therefore it is able to ascend upon Israel.

And since they did not believe in God, they did not hope for His salvation. For those who did not hope in Jesus Christ, the salvation of God, did not even believe in God Himself. To the apostles, it was said by Christ: 'Believe in me, and believe in God' (cf. John 14:1). It is possible, then, for wrath to have ascended upon Israel because they did not believe in God nor hope for His salvation, being overtaken by a force, concerning which Paul said: 'And wrath reached them to the end' (Eph 4:30).

And bread of heaven He gave them (Ps 77:38b). The voice of heaven signifies the essence of the intelligible [realms], just as we have also learned in the [previous] passages; and the opening doors of the heavens are the outpourings and manifestations of the patriarchs, through these doors the gifts of God flow. Bread of angels man has eaten, to signify how a man is in the hiddenness of the heart. Therefore, having passed over all the other names, even though he frequently remembered them—of Jacob and of Israel and of Ephraim—he remembers the human appellation here to show the man who is truly made according to the image and likeness of God, having become a fellow-table-guest and a host to angels, receiving the true manna (Ps 77:38b).

To corrupt signifies sometimes to fall into punishment, just as 'If anyone corrupts the temple of God, God will corrupt him' (1 Cor 3:17), instead of punishment. But since to corrupt also signifies being handed over to a condition of dishonor as a recompense for error and other sins being committed, God does not corrupt in this sense; rather, He finds those worthy of being seen by Him, so that they might be propitiated for their sins by much mercy and compassion. He does not say He will produce evil angels such as these, but those who bring harm through their labors. He did not spare their souls from death, bringing them to the dissolution of a weary life (Ps 77:49c–51).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Virtue, Holiness, and the Imitation of Christ
english: Death; having enclosed into this death and their irrational powers, which are tropically named cattle. For it will be for their good to cast away both themselves and their cattle, that is, their base life, namely, the passionate movement.

And understand more deeply: since the psychic man lives according to soul but not according to spirit, he does not spare these so-called souls of theirs, in order to, having destroyed their psychic state, lead them into a spiritual one. And since the name of the soul does not always signify its essence, it is clearly shown by 'the evil soul will destroy the one who has acquired it.' For it does not say the one having acquired a body calls the soul evil, but the essence of the matter has happened to which the word soul now lies. And the habit of calling some soul beautiful or base is consistent with what is being signified here.

And the tenth plague brought upon the Egyptians was death, the death of the firstborn among them from man to cattle. Perhaps it does not literally speak of the firstborn among men first born, but literally speaks of the firstborn voice upon the irrational animals as the firstfruits of pains. For the firstfruits of pains are the firstborn of those who are beast-fed. I agree to this being what is signified: that by the addition of what is said in their dwellings, the firstborn of the irrational ones were taken away, so that those having them might fall into loss, but also the firstborn of men were struck by death because their parents were tested by calamity.

Toward those not being disciplined nor repenting of such god-fearing things, 'I struck your children,' it is said (Exodus 12:12), 'because you did not receive discipline.' And so the firstborn either suffered the penalty of dying because of their own sins or they were not harmed at all, if they fell into death by the winning of others' discipline; for it is no difference to die and it happens by necessity, but toward the truth, the judgments of God are unsearchable. For the purpose of leading upward: since every place concerning the earth is called Egypt spiritually, those dwelling in it are called Egyptians. Therefore, by the grace of God, the firstborn offspring of their souls among these Egyptians is taken away, being ignorance and malice. For before the 157 virtues and sciences of the beneficial children of the intellects, malice and ignorance exist; therefore...

One does not err by calling these things 'firstfruits'. But even regarding those things which appear to be trivial in the exercise of knowledge according to virtue, they are to be rejected. For for everyone acting according to art and knowledge, the doing or acting well does not immediately occur, but it occurs after acting unassailably and acting blamelessly.

And that which lies in their tabernacles reveals what is to be said concerning souls when they are entwined with bodies; for bodies are tabernacles of souls (Ps 77:54). Holiness is the divided and most high virtue, not the intellectual alone but also the practical. And only the one perfect Teacher, Jesus, introduces one genuinely into this. Then those who are in heaven are not sanctified, but they are carried into it by the Lord. This very holiness is not a matter of chance, but it is called the right hand of God's power, not being anything other than the only-begotten Jesus. For every excellence and theoretical vision of the truth is truly a possession of Jesus, and therefore those acquiring these dispositions are called possessions of the Lord (Ps 77:61).

Perhaps they even blessed those having died in such a way, rather than weeping over the evils they had seen (Ps 77:66). He struck them from behind, so that they might not be diminished by a face of coarseness in front, but might be severed from their inhuman and evil state; for God does not desire anyone to progress in evils, but, caring for them, provided them with eternal reproach. And sinners are reproached, not only by others but also by themselves, when they are ashamed of the evils they have committed. For God says to certain ones: 'Be ashamed of your boasting and from reproach, mourn the day.' For those boasting over trivial things are benefited, if they are ashamed and reproached for the things they were vaunting of (Ps 77:72).

The name of 'innocence' does not signify gentleness here, but the absence of evil and simplicity. The sheep do not imitate the innocence of the Teacher, but are shepherded by it. And lest the one practicing evil be thought to be doing so deceptively, but rather from the best state, it is said of him that he is completing the innocence of the heart. And he also guided others by the wisdom of his hands.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Perils of Earthly Desires and the Blood of the Soul
english: For the nature of understanding is twofold: one is of the hands, the other of mind and hand; for understanding, which is called along with wisdom, comes into being through the mind. Concerning this it is said, 'The Lord gives wisdom, and from his face knowledge and understanding' (Ps 78:6). But the one of the hands, being practical and productive, is shown in the understanding of the good in all those who practice it. For the understanding being practiced is an understanding of the hands; and by this the teacher guides certain ones who are not so much benefited by word. Let the understanding of the hands and the discourse of practical things be understood, so that we may logically know for each of those practicing according to virtue.

Toward the intellect: once having become the lot of God, the soul, having enriched the temple, having fallen into the experience of those dwelling within, received it. For they came upon it, not as the inheritance of God, the invisible enemies of old, being unable to approach it even in measure, being mortal because of the foreignness of the indwelling of God. Having not approached these, they entered into the temple of God which is in it, corrupting it through which they entered into sins. Lest this should happen, it is written to some, 'Do you not know that you are the temple of God and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?' (1 Cor 3:16). If anyone corrupts the temple of God, God corrupts him; for the temple of God is holy, and you are some of them. It is also possible to call the unclean and uncircumcised thoughts mortal, having come into the inheritance once inhabited by God as a soul, which also once entered into the holy. But if the things happening at certain times in Christianity, having been worked by the Gentiles in the holy places, signify the things dwelling within, let the one encountering them judge. For the invisible enemies, called mortal, were not so powerful as to lay waste the once-become city of God, as if no fruit of anything remained in it, to place it in a state of desolation. And the desolation...

A small thing, as it is written in Isaiah (Isa 55:1), is a fig-bearing tree; and the fruits of this are figs and gourds. These are Egyptian foods which the people desired when sinning, even though they had the manna and the heavenly food from God, but also the mortal foods of God's servants and food to be eaten by the winged ones of heaven.

For the sinning soul, seeing the peace of God, [is lost]; Jerusalem, which passed well, had certain thoughts, because the diligent and virtuous servants happened to be of God. But they did not entirely remain, instead of seeking the incorruptible life, but they received something mortal in doing something passionately.

This is not the mortal food becoming of the winged ones who snatch what was sown by the roadside, which the Savior interpreted as the evil one (Matt 7:15) and those being sickened by this. For indeed vultures and young vultures, profiting from the beasts of the earth, do not eat the holy ones but their flesh. For whatever is found to be fleshy and passionate is nourished.

If it is possible to raise these things up to the witnesses of Christ, he himself will understand; many in persecutions, having become food for birds and beasts, yet their souls were not able to be devoured by the spiritual winged ones of heaven nor by the beasts themselves, because God did not hand over a soul confessing Him.

But the blood, which becomes the removal of the soul, instead of its life-giving power, which is called 'turning,' is poured out not far from or far from Jerusalem but around it. And this is the boundary of peace. Since the one stumbling goes outside of Jerusalem, of the correctness of the dogmas, the aforementioned blood is poured out about it and around it, not even worthy of a burial because of his exalting his sins; such are the things falling away after the knowledge of the truth (1 Tim 4:2). Since the one being baptized is not buried with Christ (Rom 6:4), and secondly not...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Prayer for Mercy and the Sabbath Symbol
english: If it is a bath, it is fitting that those who have acted impiously after the bath are not buried (Ps 78:4).

By analogy, you call the heretics neighbors; for their dwellings are near us because they hold to the same writings. They do not reproach us, saying we are heretics, but they call us as slaves, well-behaved and foolish. Around us, if there are wise men among the Greeks, they sneer and mock us as believing without examination and foolishly (Ps 78:5–6).
'You have disciplined the Jews sufficiently,' they say; 'surely, at some time, turn your wrath upon the impious mortals and upon the kingdom of your reverence that is alien' (Ps 78:7, 8a).

By analogy: if the word is about invisible enemies, we did not consume the one who once became a wing for the wicked, and their place was laid waste. The place of each is his own station of life; for the prudent man in some way inhabits prudence. We say that the prudent man inhabits the place of the prudent, and others the order of the righteous. If it happens that those possessing these things of yours are devoured by enemies, their order and their place will be laid waste. We say, for example, the place of a bishop and a presbyter. As the saved are food for Jesus, the perishing are not by the eating of the wicked.

'Do not remember our ancient iniquities' (Ps 51:3). And in other places, if no one confesses what he does evilly, but rather what he acted upon of old, 'Do not remember the sin of my youth and my ignorance' (Ps 25:7). And now, those who repent of their ceased iniquities are not worthy that their ancient [sins] not be remembered by God. For indeed, the sensual ones always call upon God not concerning youthful [sins] but concerning past deeds, saying: 'We have sinned, we have done wrong, we have transgressed' (Ps 51:1-3). For it is contrary to the one repenting to be sinning.

'We have become exceedingly impoverished, having fallen from the wealth of virtue and knowledge, Lord; therefore we beseech you to grant us mercy, not in the future, but surely even now and quickly (Ps 51:7). For you are the Father of mercies and the God of all consolation, and your mercies are sufficient to make us rich again.' And this will be easy for us, with your helping and saving; for many times, with your helping...

We experience the salvation of the Lord. Even if we are not worthy to suffer well because of the sins that are among us, but since your name has been called upon us (for we are your inheritance and your people), be propitiated toward our sins, so that your name may be glorified. For we do not bear the reproach of the nations saying, 'Where is their God?' (Ps 78:10). For they hold us in subjection because we have sinned, and they reproach even your name, thinking that you have been defeated by those who are beneath us.

And toward a turning point of discourse: those being squeezed by the chains of their own sins have been brought low, but having become aware of the weight, they are overcome by the plains, through which they are hindered from running toward salvation and from working out those things that contribute to happiness, groaning thus, being utterly exhausted. Therefore they also pray that their groan may be known to God and enter before him. For he will move his own goodness to intervene to break their bonds; for the Lord looses the bound (Ps 78:12). And he will set them apart for blessed life, according to the greatness of the God Word, his arm, so that, even if they appeared as sons of men having been dead, they might be shown to be children becoming living ones. For their fathers, having been killed by the enemies, are living before the Lord, and they are found to be his sons and his servants.

Since the number seven holds a symbol of rest, they desire the retribution to be upon the description of their impiety, through which they reproached God and were roughly brought to his servants, to be led away. For those knowing the good God will not lift up the reproaches of the scourged, but they want the scourgings to be brought upon them, so that the workers of that laziness, to whom punishment follows by necessity, may be idle. But the Sabbath number is a symbol of laziness. Since we are being enriched as your people and sheep grazing your pasture, concerning which it has been said, 'He shall enter and go out and shall find pasture' (Ps 78:13) (clearly meaning the sheep of Christ), we asked for blessings; do according to your greatness, so that, as you are clearly present, we may gratefully acknowledge you throughout life; for this clearly signifies 'unto the age' regarding the present. And if one were to take the usual meaning of 'age', you would say not only in the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Nourishment of Tears and the Allegory of Egypt
english: But also in the coming life, thanks be to God. The phrase 'unto generation and generation' can be said more simply instead of 'and unto the generations and the many successors of men.' Or you may say more mystically, 'in the present and in the coming life,' or 'in both generations, the one of circumcision and the one of the calling of the Gentiles,' so that they may learn to praise God.

The Shepherd of Israel is none other than the one who said, 'I am the good shepherd' (John 10:11), who grazes those who have understanding and see God. He also guides those being added from the Gentiles like sheep, that is, as his own sheep, the Israelites; for Joseph, being interpreted as 'addition of the Lord,' signifies those from the Gentiles being added to those of the circumcision. It is the custom for the shepherd's voice to be placed instead of the approach of kings only in the ancient days. For indeed, even shepherds, as far as possible, set themselves out to rule and to lead among the flocks of the simpler animals, so that having progressed, they might consider themselves to rule over even peoples.

The Lord is seated upon the cherubim, as he is presented in Ezekiel (Ezek. 10). But he breathes upon the animals who have not attained this leadership from the wisdom present to them (for a multitude of knowledge is interpreted by the cherubim), which is established by virtue itself and is found by chance; but there exists in all those who have lit themselves with the light of knowledge which God has shone in the hearts for the illumination of the knowledge of the glory of Christ. This one, being royally established upon the cherubim, the choir of the saints entreats to appear and to shine before those bearing fruit in virtue and the sons of the right hand of God through the right-hand works, thoughts, and words having been performed, and those who have departed from the form of evils by their actions. For they have not truly taken forgetfulness of evils in the remembrance of good things. For Ephraim is fruitfulness, Benjamin is the son of the right hand, and Manasseh is interpreted from forgetfulness. They say therefore: 'Since you are a king, having awakened a greatest power and having roused it, O Lord, so as to save us; for there is no other way to attain salvation than for you, having come to us, to turn us back from sins.'

And of the captivity, the Lord of powers, as follows, bringing it upon us. Ps 79:5-6: 'O Master, All-King, ruling over the heavenly hosts, when will you shine for me, so that I may desire to see your face? For you are angry with me, your servant.' Therefore I beseech you: having been reconciled to your servant, who ruled, that I might not be in need. For I thirst for him exceedingly and without restraint.

And because you are angry at the prayer which we sent up, having turned it into weeping and lamentation, we bear such a multitude of tears at the time of food, as if to eat bread of tears and to drink with tears a little and measured drink. Ps 79:6-8: Since the toil and weeping for the sake of virtue is nourishment, we eat the tears of this very weeping as bread, and also drink them in measure. And the 'in measure' prevents one from always weeping and weeping through trial. For he will receive as rest and a propitiatory state those who undergo labors for the sake of good things. To this end, 'Blessed are those who weep now, they shall laugh' [Matt 5:4], and 'Those who sow in tears shall reap in joy' [Ps 126:5]. For those who sow virtue with sweat and tears, they are able to measure the weeping, reaping in joy; for with it they shall laugh.

Let us be set for contention against our neighbors. It is said, 'Every evil man raises contention'; and the Savior has cast down his hands toward the sinning people who disobey and contradict him. For the neighbors are enemies; they mock them, sneering and dragging away their wise words. The wise man, however, has taken a command for his mind not to say anything, lest the fool should mock the wise man's wise words. But they will also mock those crying out to God. But they themselves, rather, say they are entreating: 'Lord God of powers, turn back now, redeeming our captivity from those who tyrannize.' And we shall desire this good thing: if you show your eternal face to us, you will grant us salvation. Ps 79:6-14
For allegory: the soul is then said to dwell in Egypt, as it spends time with the sensible things and the works of the flesh. But God moves it from Egypt, tearing it away from material things.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Vine and the Wild Beast
english: For all, even he who will transplant it from the former bad planting into a better land. And that land is the state according to virtue.

And he sang before it, having given a saving law and luminous commands before it, in order to travel to the good land; and that land is perfect virtue. If it seems well to you, Egypt, to take the land as a spiritual world in which the soul, struggling with the sensible and temporal things, is planted, you would take a transplantation into the heavenly and intelligible realms of it, with God being the cause of this so great good for it, because he has prepared the way before it by giving the spiritual discourse of the God-breathed Scriptures (2 Tim 3:16). Its shadow covered them. For those called the righteous, who were high and possessed a lasting citizenship, were sheltered by what was well spread out under it. But also those who have become wealthy and well-toned through a more prosperous life, as if to profit from God's gain, were covered by its leafy branches in a certain way, being supported by them. And the vine extends its branches to the greatest extent, as if approaching the seas without suffering harm from the trials and surges of life called seas, to bear fruit metaphorically. And it also extends its shoots, just as the rivers that water it, in order to yield the proper fruit.
