And its branches are those joined to the Jewish worship, who, because of remaining in the law, happen to bear fruit like the shoots of those proselytizing.

If the vine is such a soul cultivated by God, having its beginning and its root in the Word, according to which it is logical for the one saying, 'I am the true vine' (John 15:1), God will transplant its various branches and powers, its roots metaphorically being shoots, into the various thoughts of the Only-begotten. For the vine, being raised up because it is well cultivated, will cover the high doctrines of truth, called shadows, with itself. And this citizenship and knowledge existing here are able to bear a shadow and a type of its true state hereafter.

And its side-shoots, which have branched out from its powers and virtues, are also extended, being called rivers as they are the drinkable waters of the divine words. And in another way, its side-shoots may be called such, as that which branches out from it for the benefit of the other instruction. For just as the side-shoots drink and are transformed into drinkability from the plant upon which they have branched, so also those branching out from the other learning drink from its preceding teaching, with every name being taken captive into the obedience of Christ.

Why would you remove its hedge? For if the vine does not bear fruit, the keeper of the cluster is found in the tent. But when fruitlessness exists, he abandons the tent. And those passing by the road trample it, not those walking [the path]. But these are false teachers and the spirits of error. They trample it, possessing a cluster of gall and a grape of bitterness; for such a settlement has become. And one bears passions instead of moral virtues, having produced thorns instead of grapes; and another errs concerning knowledge, bearing a cluster of gall and a grape of bitterness.

God desolated it from the thicket. Those desolating it are either the irrational [passions] and its wild passions, or the exposed and most evil powers. And perhaps God is able to be the shameful desires and unbridled pleasures, and because of the uncleanness in the thicket—that is, in the fruitless plants—they will be surrounded; for these passions are hidden regarding irrational impulses and fantasies, but the description of the more savage beast may signify even as if they had come to be, the heart and the angers. But the savage beast is the irrational mind, as if someone were to mount its passion (Ps 79:18-19).

A man, who has become like us individually and has not cast away his being, has been foretold by the Divine Scripture: 'Behold, his name is Orient, and a man comes after me' (Ps 79:18-19). If, regarding this man, the creative sign and wonders of God's hand were not to become the right hand (and this is the Divine Word), instead of the logical soul having been united to flesh according to subsistence and through it having blessed the God-marked things, such an improvement would be for us as not...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Musical Allegory and the Tongues of Fire
english: To depart from you. For if we are not partakers of you, we shall not be made alive, and we shall not call upon your name. For from this salvation will also follow us; for everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved (Ps 80:2).

Since the commands of those being improved by Christ are many, and his stages have been spoken of as the true vine, there are various presses—that is, promises—in which the fruit is being pressed out, making the name [of God] and gladdening the heart of man. And since all the God-breathed Scripture speaks of vines (for concerning it, after it was taken away from the Hebrews and given to those believing from the Gentiles, it was said to the Jews, 'The kingdom of heaven shall be taken from you'—'the vine in the parable had grown'—'and it shall be given to a nation producing its fruits'; the fruit and clusters of this vine are the bearing of thoughts; the minds of the believers, having received divine presses, will not receive seeds as fruit, but will press out the Name, from which the one able to say to God, 'Joy has come into my heart' (Ps 80:2), drinks.

Fittingly, the eighty-first psalm is arranged according to its title, this number containing eights and tens as a symbol of the resurrection of the Lord being accomplished on the eighth Lord's day. And it is not the first that is written concerning the presses, but also the eightieth. And it himself, because of the aforementioned thought, is arranged in the order of the number eight.

Since Jesus, helping us through his death, dissolved the one having dominion over death, the devil, we shout aloud, triumphing against the abolished tyrant, rejoicing in the one providing the help (Ps 80:2).

Since the timbrel is made of the skin of a dead animal, he wants us, having killed the members upon the earth and carrying the death of Jesus in the body, to construct a timbrel for ourselves, which we shall give instead of a psalm. We do not take by the present...

The word commands not only to strike a timbrel for the psalm, but also a harp and a lyre. As it is said in other psalms, the harp is [called so] because it is straight and unbending, and because it gives back the sound from above; the spirit is the human spirit within him, the soul being signified by the lyre, with the senses stretched out and the powers of the soul composing the sound through well-ordered and musical activities.

If, then, the harp is the spirit, the lyre the soul, and the body the timbrel, it is being allegorized: we take the divine word [as] a psalm, in order to make the spirit, the soul, and the body active through the contemplation and actions according to virtue. According to an upward leading, it is thus: the command which declares the spiritual will of the shadowy feast is set as a testimony by the Lord to those who were added to the Gentiles by the Gospel. For the name of Joseph and what was said before signify these. For they did not leave behind the passions and the evils and the very place of the earth by wisdom, fleeing out of tropical Egypt, but in leaving it, they previously did not know the language, that is, the dialect they heard. The symbols of this paradox are carried into the Acts of the Apostles, where, having appeared as tongues of fire, they sat upon each of the believers, so that each one might suddenly speak the greatness of God in his own dialect heard in various voices. But those receiving this gift turned away from lifting up the sense of their souls, no longer enduring to lift up the material and muddy things of tropical Egypt. For they served, but they shall not serve with their hands in the basket; their hands in their actions are no longer touching wheat and brick, but are lifting up gracefully and freely some of the baskets, of which Jesus filled, from which he broke.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Divinity of Judges and God's Presence
english: For the fragments left behind have become full baskets since those who feed the disciples carry these spiritual baskets. A storm is often taken for a trial. Since God is not present with those being tempted openly but rather hiddenly, it is necessary for the one being tempted to call upon Him, [so that] how having heard him, God will rescue him from his present distress.

'And my people will not hear my voice' (Ps 80:12). To hear signifies not only the sensing of a voice, but also to be persuaded by the one speaking, according to [the Psalm]: 'You do not heed the voice of my disciplining,' that is, I did not consent to the commands of the discipliner. And hearing the voice signifies also to understand and to think. For he says, 'Whoever has ears, let him hear'; that is, whoever has understanding, let him understand. And he says of his people that he awakens them to goodwill, while weighing down and increasing their transgression; saying only once, 'If he had encountered a nation [that would forgive],' [but] not hearing our voice, being uninitiated, now they shall be punished without forgiveness.

And not only 'my people will not hear my voice,' but also 'they will not pay attention to me,' even though [they are] capable of understanding, seeing me. For even if he despises the voice, it is good to make clear through the one approaching me with my authority, that the timely evangelical word is not understood by the heterodox, who are interrupting these things, as seen in the Savior saying to the Jews concerning the Father, 'Nor have you ever heard his voice, nor have you seen his form' (John 12:49). The heretics, not having understood what was said, say that the Jews, having heard the voice of God and having seen his form, according to the appearances written by them. But the Savior rebukes them, showing that they have never heard the voice of God nor seen his form, and that to pay attention to God involves both hearing the voice and seeing the form. And those of differing opinions were deceived, having ignored the great significance of hearing the voice. For if even the Jews, having heard the voice of God and having received the law from him, did not understand it nor were persuaded by it, they are justly rebuked for not hearing his voice; but they also did not see his form, not having conformed to the character.

Regarding his substance, saying, 'He who has seen me has seen the Father' (John 14:9). Not so; it is said, meaning they have never heard the voice of God, and likewise here they are struck by the spoken word and the word that will be declared hereafter.

In 'the nothing' of Psalm 80:15a, it signifies that they humbled their enemies through lowly things, just as even the greatest tyrant of Egypt was not opposed by great and strong armed men, but by lowly and small creatures. In Psalm 81:2–4, they say that men set over the judging of the people are called gods, as Moses himself demonstrates, saying, 'You shall not do evil to gods, nor shall you speak evil of rulers of your people' (Exodus 22:28). For those being appointed as gods to the people of God are not further from the judges. But since hereafter in this same Psalm God says, 'I said, You are gods, and all of you are sons of the Most High' (Psalm 81:6) (not having been placed there, but because the word of God came to them), it is evident that even now 'God stands in the assembly of gods' (Psalm 82:1) will be brought against them. For all those who are such gods—men and angels—are divine in the same way, for God stands in their midst, unmoving and not abandoning them; such are they. For he stands away from those who fall, leaving them behind. Therefore also Adam, after the transgression, was standing before God who was with him before the sin; and it is said in the prophet, 'And the Lord God will go in the fury of his wrath' (Isaiah 33:19). But God, standing in the assembly of the gods, preserves their divinity, rather nourishing and increasing it through the participation they have in him. But even being in their midst, he distinguishes them in the manner spoken: 'How long will you judge injustice and accept the faces of sinners?' (Psalm 82:2). If the judges of Israel are gods, what is written will fall upon them. For it is a perversion of a judge to judge injustice and to accept the faces of sinners. Just as they corrupt the right through the greed for gifts, so too they judge contrary to the law by accepting faces. It is fitting, then, that the judgment falls upon sinners. For it is not right to give the right to the rich and to another who excels in the sequence of equality. For it is said, 'And you shall not show mercy to the poor in judgment' (Psalm 82:8); and it is also said, 'Not...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Fall of Man and the Judgment of Nations
english: He will show no partiality in judgment; you will judge both the great and the small (Ps 81:5); one will not show partiality, for such is the judgment of God. For it is necessary for the judge to know what he serves in the judgment of God. Therefore it is also well said, that God stands in the assembly of these gods and judges them in their midst (Ps 81:5), as those knowing Him in them and in their midst, according to His own purpose.

If indeed they are gods who change their divinity, since they prove to be turnable, how can one judge injustice? For having an intermediate law by which it is possible to know the good to be chosen and the evil to be avoided, if they come to things in a way that turns away from the good and embraces the evil, you judge injustice; therefore you also take the faces of sinners, hiding your own faces which are according to the image of God. Judge the orphan, who has been left desolate by the father entrusted to guardianship, but also the poor man who does not wish to contend with his own righteous ones; but also bring out the laborer and the poor, being oppressed, rescuing them from the grasping sinners.

But it is also said to those who have been made divine according to virtue, how they judge worthily the one who has cast off the worthless father and the wealth of wickedness, in protection through discipline toward them. And let them also justify the one made lowly and poor through blindness, because he has come to toil for the sake of piety, excluding those who are not truly poor and needy, on account of making them do the work of a sinner by a hand outside of them.

The divine knowledge, being wisdom of God, shines and enlightens the one having it; for the wisdom of man enlightens his face (Prov 1:5), and those called toward divine knowledge have the command to enlighten for themselves the light of knowledge. If then the wise according to God happen to be enlightened, those who are contrary, being filled with ignorance and unreasonableness, wander in darkness, always progressing in evils.

But since, having become accustomed to evils and having embedded the first things of wickedness, they have not only become earthly due to their material existence, but they also wished the foundations of the earth to be, remaining firmly and immovably in the worthless opinion. But if they themselves are of such a kind...

They did not love, but rather the human-loving word causes them to be shaken and moved from the very bad position they hold, and to fall from the position they built with a clumsy hand (Ps 81:6-7). The good God is not all envious of his own, giving to men what he is, just as he accepted the word of the gods. But the God who makes them gods is God, and he will make them sons of the Most High, participating with them, the only-begotten Son of the Most High. But although God granted to them the being to be gods and sons of the Most High, they ran toward the opposite, to become humans and to die the death that follows humans.

For they did not become humans by falling from divinity (for this is how both gods and sons of the Most High happened), but according to how they loved, mortal and human. And they die not as humans do, not the common death, but the death that follows sin, falling similarly to the one who fell among the rulers. For such is the devil; for he himself was a ruler and fell in the heavens. For it is said concerning him, 'How did the Morning Star, rising in the morning, fall from heaven?' (Luke 10:18). In this way also Adam, sinning, did not as a god but as one of God's fell, clearly showing that he became [human]; for God did not say concerning him, 'Behold, Adam has become like us,' but 'As one of us' or 'As one of ours'—as many things are contained in the copies (Ps 81:8).

He said another scripture has, 'Rise, O God, judge the earth; you shall destroy all the nations' (Ps 81:8). God will judge all those on the earth, for the earth was made because of those who think of earthly things. And God will judge the earth, destroying all the nations, but not all the mortals. For the superstitious and the other curiosity, along with those who have worked them, the mortals were destroyed by God, so that the mortals might become pure for the acceptance of the word of salvation. And that disposition in the nations, through which the mortals were diverse, God, by destroying them, will show that they, having cast away what had happened to them, will prove to be in the image of himself, just as mortals have become.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Uniqueness of the Most High and Eternal Dwellings
english: Likeness is understood in two ways. For when there is identity in essence, it is called similarity and even strictly identity; but when it is according to quality, it is called simply similarity. According to the second meaning, those becoming perfect are said to be made like God, just as the heavenly Father is perfect; therefore it is said, 'When he is revealed, we shall be like him' (1 John 3:2), meaning, like God. And the Creator of all, according to the first meaning, which I say is according to essence, fashioned man not according to an image and his own likeness, for no one is becoming like God. For 'Who shall be like [God]?' (Ps 82:2) does not declare something rare but rather something impossible, that no one is able to be like God in essence. But do not err, thinking that yourself and the Son are subject to the things being said. For it is not 'Who is like you?' but 'Who shall be made like you?'; for the Son is not about to undergo being made like God, being of His own essence and therefore being the same as Him, not in number but in the sameness of essence.

He wills them to be placed by God like an unstable and unwatered wheel (Ps 82:14). For it will be a misfortune to them not to be made stable and to remain motionless, having pursued wickedness. Therefore also He wills them to be placed like a reed being scattered and being driven about by a fierce wind before the face of the one pursuing them, a punishing spirit, allegorically a wind (Ps 82:15). And the fire of punishments shall consume them, having cut off the grove which had become fruit. And using another punishment against them, He will pursue them with His own storm, from which there is no escape; therefore they shall be troubled in the wrath of God being brought upon them. Since indeed their sins were diverse, a multi-faceted punishment has necessarily risen over them. It should be noted, however, that He loved them, though they were a good planting, becoming unfruitful. For the reed has its beginning from a good seed, not beforehand, but deviating by accident. For if they had borne fruit beforehand, it was necessary for them to become wheat, if they were to be brought into the granaries of the Word. But not desiring this, they have become a reed and a wasteland, which the tyrant of the spiritual Egypt shall use for the construction of...
They shall burn in the fire of destructive cities, and they shall be consumed by the unquenchable fire (Ps 82:19b).

For even if others are high and have become Most High through virtue, being lifted up, none of them is such from himself or in essence. For God alone is Most High, making [others] Most High but not becoming [so] himself; just as He alone is wise and alone is true, providing wisdom and truth but not participating [in them as a recipient], so the Most High is unique, according to this being the Most High and the Only-begotten Most High. For the power of the Most High overshadowed Mary; and the Holy Spirit, being sent from the Most High, is Most High. The only Most High is fitting to the Trinity. For he who spoke the Most High Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit declares [them]; likewise, he who called the Son also declares the Father and the Holy Spirit. For as there is one deity, so is the Most High in it, so that there might be no difference regarding the Trinity, just as we theologize correctly in other matters.

Regarding the word 'As' (Ps 83:2,3a), it does not signify a likeness or a parable here, but the beloved thing itself, just as in Moses, where he is 'as' a servant, and Christ is 'as' a son. For 'as a son' signifies a true Son and not a likeness; and Moses was not a likeness of a servant of God, but was a servant of Him. Therefore, regarding the word present, the beloved dwellings of God are not according to a parable but according to truth. And if we have meditated on what kind of things they are, we will more certainly understand them as beloved things, rather than finding them to be merely like beloved things. These things are therefore eternal and heavenly, concerning which the Savior says to those present, 'Make friends for yourselves from the mammon of unrighteousness, so that when it fails, they may receive you into the eternal dwellings' (Luke 16:9). My soul longs and faints, to cast off the psychic state and become spiritual, as is appropriate for the dwelling in the heavenly courts, as they have been spoken of in parallel.
The altars are not perceptible. For the altar was not a multitude, according to the history. Unless even the altar is called so, Lord of hosts of the heavens (Ps 83:8).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The progression of power and the superiority of the divine courts
english: The altars upon which [sacrifices] are brought up are better than the sacrifices of shadow and type. The apostle says that the types of those in the heavens are [linked] to these sacrifices, but the heavenly things are better sacrifices than these. For the sacrifices of praise and righteousness are brought up upon these altars, and those offering the living sacrifice, presenting their own bodies pleasing to God, they offer them not upon something else but upon these altars.

For the dwelling of God is perfect virtue and the highest knowledge of the truth (Ps 83:5). It is said that in the presence [of God] the tent is a symbol of progress; for those traveling, it is a home. But the end of blessedness is made manifest by the dwelling of God's voice. And according to the history, the people traveling had a tent of witness (the dwelling of theology) and they had various tents for their own virtues in which all the people dwelt. Having reached the holy land, they had the dwelling in houses, no longer progressing; for they had reached the end of virtue and knowledge. But they were no longer approaching the tent of witness but the dwelling established, completing the things of worship. And there, therefore, after desiring and loving their progresses through the tabernacles, he began, saying, 'How lovely are your tabernacles, O Lord' (Ps 83:7), blessing those who have ascended through the progresses to the summit, as dwelling while bearing the state according to God, when the fullness is fulfilled upon them and the Son is revealed, we shall be like him, seeing him as he is (Ps 83:7-8a).

'The one set' signifies 'to do then,' as 'I set a guard with my mouth' instead of 'I did' (Ps 83:8a); and 'He who sets the inhabited world desolate' is the same as 'He who will make the inhabited world desolate.' And here 'the one set in a place' does not present 'He made a place.' For the surrounding place is not this. For in this God disposed of the [things] before...

He makes covenants for men. Let us not weep, nor let us praise the blameless weeping, learning from the fact that God established covenants for those who are here. For we shall also receive the blessings, living according to the will of the covenant given here. And we shall know the magnitude of the blessings given, understanding who the possessors of them are. And not such is the God who legislated. And they shall proceed from power to power. The virtues and contemplations of the truth are powers. Therefore, those having these are also more able.

Those having proceeded will not hasten according to the progress of the introductory power to become the more perfect, and those living according to the law toward the evangelical way—those knowing Christ according to the flesh to behold his glory, glory as unique from the Father; those knowing in part that he is on earth and that the most sharp knowledge does not fit—upon the coming of the perfect vision of contemplation to know as it is necessary to know, proceeding from a lower power of the intellect to a greater and more perfect power. [Psalm 83:10b] And more pure and more holy of the saints, but rather also of priests and kings, he is able to bring this merit to, Christ, the Son of God. For it is said, 'Do not be afraid of my Christs concerning all the saints,' and priests and kings were approaching as Christs in Hebrew. [Psalm 83:11a] Better it is to be in your courts for one day than a multitude of thousands of days outside your courts. For the perfection among men exceeds that which seems little in the courts of God. Such also is that which was said concerning John by the Savior: 'Among those born of women no one is greater than John, but the least in the kingdom is greater than him.' [Matthew 11:11] Let it also be said thus here: men living are under time, but those in [eternity] are time unto a multitude.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Divine Goodness and the Turning of Wrath
english: The days are divided, one day being an eternal and unceasing one, because of having been created in the divine courts of the Lord. For the Lord has become to him an eternal light, like the sun of righteousness, which is not able to be overcome by it. The unceasing and unceasing day is greater than the life of many days occurring here.

Ps 83:12b–13: God gives grace to those being saved by grace, according to 'By grace you have been saved' (Eph 2:8), a gift of the grace able to be given here. For 'grace' and 'gift' signify the same thing, as one is found to be 'having been graced.' For this reason, it is said that someone has found grace in the sight of God. He gives this grace instead of a former grace, which we hastened to take from ourselves as much as possible. And He also gives glory to those worthy of receiving this, because He has promised the one saying, 'Those who glorify me I will glorify' (John 12:26), clearly through good works and true dogmas. And those moving through all things, unhindered by any hand, go about in innocence. If innocence also signifies simplicity, let Him also establish it.

And since hope is the expectation of good things, and only the rational appetite for truly good things is the proper virtue of man, to hope is especially the substitute for piety; for it is written, 'Hope [is] to the pious one.' For the faithful are reborn into a living and abiding hope because the expectation of good things is pure.

Ps 84:2–4: For contemplation: the Lord is pleased with a good and eager heart becoming His land, because it receives the seed from Him and bears fruit a hundredfold. But He turns away from it also the multitude of captives brought by evil powers, the thoughts of Jacob, because of standing against the passions. These things, having worked them, He grants as a remission of transgressions, removing and loosening their lawlessness. And if even after a remission there is error, He covers these sins, entering into virtue; for virtue covers sins, not hiding them, but utterly destroying and making them vanish. For in this way love covers a multitude of sins. Just as knowledge covers ignorance, utterly destroying it in the soul that it was generated in, so also the love of God, being the same as virtue, covers the sins of those it benefits.

God was pleased with his earth, having sent his Son to appear on the earth and to associate with men; thus it is said, 'Glory in the highest to God, and on earth peace among men of good pleasure' (Luke 2:14). From these things said, we learn that what is called God's wrath is not a passion. For because of sins, wrath is sustained, but it is managed such that they are destroyed and vanished, and it approaches them as a consequence.

If those serving wrath appear to be called vessels of wrath, being homonymous with it—fury and wrath being addressed—it is better that he visits. Since you are God, who gives us the salvations, turn us back, providing us opportunities for repentance and receiving us as we turn toward you (Ps 84:5–7). For it will be possible for your fury to turn away from us. Since we have removed that [wrath] through which we sinned, once we have recognized and turned back, it will no longer act against us, vanishing. Just as fire, when the combustible fuel through which it acts is failing, is no longer, so too, once our sins are vanished, your fury will no longer be sustained against us.

God lives, providing life to those who turn to him, having departed from him and turned away from him; he himself, having turned his face, turned away from them through which they practiced evil. It is possible to understand 'having turned' in both ways, most certainly said. For it is not made clear whether he himself turned toward them or they themselves turned toward him. When life was granted to the living ones, the people of God rejoiced over him, the God who granted life.

Since they require salvation not from works but by the grace and mercy of God, they say, 'O Lord, show us through whom you show mercy and compassion to your people' (Ps 84:8); for so also your salvation, that is, the salvation from you, might be given to us. It is possible to call Jesus the cause of mercy and salvation. For he is the mercy and the salvation of God, according to how he shows mercy and saves.

God does not speak striking the hearing of those listening from the outside, but placing [his will] within that mind, he desires to reveal to the intellect without utterance, which is why it is said, 'I will listen to what he speaks in me' (Hab 2:20). Agree with this also the words of Habakkuk, which say: 'And...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Conjunction of Mercy, Truth, Justice, and Peace
english: I will aim to see what the Lord God will speak in me. According to these things also Paul says: 'If you seek a test of the Christ speaking in me; for in him indeed Christ does not speak simply to him' (2 Cor 13:5). For he speaks through that [person] in whom he speaks; and not everyone who speaks speaks through him, but only the hearing from the outside is struck. But the Lord God will speak in him, interpreting, whether it be peace or whether it be upon his people, the God of all, against all enemies of the people, clearly those subverting [them], or the peace having possessed a mind surpassing all things of the people, by which all disturbance and noise are excluded, bringing tranquility. This peace is given from God and Father and Lord Jesus by grace, as the Savior says concerning it: 'My peace I give to you' (John 14:27). And this peace is given also to those who give back the things of God to God, guarding the righteousness toward him, who are rightly called his own. And he gives it also to those who through repentance turn their heart toward him, making the turning not crooked toward him nor superficial, but from the depth of the mind.

Then indeed he truly dwelt and brought glory in the earth, performing many and great things paradoxically: the Savior's resurrections of the dead, sight to the blind, cleansings of the lepers, and other wondrous things he did (Ps 84:10). And as toward a more mystical word for those fearing God, he did not leave them wanting (For there is no lack to those fearing him), he drew near to the God-participating salvation which they partake in through which they act salvifically. For just as salvation is far from sinners, working the things of destruction, so the salvation of God is near to the opposite, to those fearing him. Therefore also he dwells, glory in the earth, of those saying these things. And you will say their earth: the good heart of theirs which has yielded a hundredfold fruit of the seed cast upon it. But what dwells in the heart as the glory of God, the word establishes, which says: 'The God who said light should shine out of darkness' (2 Cor 4:6); He shone in our hearts for the illumination of the knowledge of the glory of Christ. And it dwells also in the body of those persuaded by the exhortation being said: 'Glorify then God in the body' (1 Cor 6:20).

Regarding those who achieve perfect prudence (Ps 84:11-12). From this, the following of virtues can be shown: that the merciful is true and the true is merciful, and that the just is peaceful and the peaceful is just.

In other words, truth is named along with mercy, as it is said in the Psalm: 'Thy mercy and thy truth have encompassed me' (Ps 84:11), and 'God sent His mercy and His truth' (Ps 84:12). I stand by saying these things because the truth of matters is difficult for men, and even more unreachable unless they happen to be granted it by the grace of God. Perhaps one cannot receive true salvation without the mercy of God, and thus they were named by righteousness. He says that mercy has met with truth. For if mercy and truth come to the same place, we shall know it and be in it.

Moreover, justice loves peace and peace loves justice. For where there is justice, there is certainly peace, without it being a mere sprout. You can also grasp these things regarding the Savior, spoken through His various thoughts, as has been clearly stated before. The truth of the Savior, having become man, has risen from the earth. For there is much deception and much falsehood among men. For there is no truth and mercy nor knowledge of God upon the earth; therefore, falsehood, murder, and adultery are poured out upon the earth, says the prophet (Ps 84:13). This is not the falsehood of the whole earth that prevailed, but the one overcome by Him who said, 'I am the truth' (John 14:6), having caused the truth from the earth (that is, from men) to rise. But also, becoming justice according to the Word of God and Wisdom, He descended from heaven, bowing the heavens and coming down. He brought to us peace according to justice and mercy according to truth; for all these things are thought of in Him, as has been clearly said.

As the manner of rain being given, the soil bears the goodness of the Lord's gift; the intelligent earth gives fruit, having been moistened by the goodness from God. And the fruit of it is the general virtue, whereby the soul, being as a fruit-bearing earth, happens to be presented as described. It is possible to say regarding the people what is set forth, namely that...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Divine Mercy and Human Likeness
english: Something like this is said. Since the Lord spoke peace upon his people, the justice of the people going before him will set his steps upon the way leading to blessedness; and the Lord himself, who is justice, goes before the people and will set his steps into a way. To whom, indeed, is it said, 'Before you I will go and I will make the level places'?

And likewise: the justice operating according to the law in Moses and the prophets, having come forward before the end of John from the Savior, having been placed into the way of his crossings in us, to dwell and walk among us, has cried out: 'Prepare the ways of the Lord straight, make his paths'; for he alone cries: 'Make straight for him who is stepping upon the mountains, the Lord, his name.' Care also regarding John, it is said: 'He will go before the Lord in spirit and in power like Elijah,' and 'Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you.'

If even the Savior is justice going before the Father into the minds of the God-bearers, consider with understanding in what way it was said: 'He who receives you receives me, and he who receives me receives him who sent me' (Matt 10:40). Psalm 85:2b,3: 'All the saints cry out as if upon a great command concerning the servant of God.' Jonah, indeed, when asked from what land he is and from what people, said: 'I am a servant of God, and I fear the God of heaven.'

And the apostles, indeed, are testified by the Savior well through works and words, confessing him as Lord: 'For you call me Lord and Teacher, and you say well: for I am both your Lord and Teacher always, learning from me and serving me sincerely' (Matt 23:36). And concerning their own letters, they set forward this significance, as if being refreshed by a greatest command: 'James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ,' and 'Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ.' Just as the men of the world in the writings of life-transactions wish to be designated by the honors concerning them, so the apostles in the beginnings of their writings are worthy to be designated servants of God and of Christ. David, doing the similar, [and]...

To the King, he says, 'Save, O God, your servant who hopes in you; save me in your abundant mercy, because as I say all the time of my life, I cry out to you' (Ps 85:5a). But leniency is not spoken of as being upon God; for leniency is a human virtue. If it is said about it to be more human, as are the other things, such as rejoicing, being glad, or remembering.

And 'gods' is said not only there to be taken for idols and demons, but also for the saints (Ps 85:8). For in these no one is entirely and unchangeably the equal of the Lord. For He himself alone is likewise God to the Father; but each of these has become a god by participation, having received the Word of God according to 'They shall be gods' (Ps 82:6) and 'The Word of God became' (Jn 1:1). For even if they have become the image and likeness of God, none of them is in essence the equal of the Lord, being those who shall be made like Him but not being Him. 'You shall be holy because I am holy' (Lev 11:44), He who is holy, so that they may become [holy]. To speak the truth concerning those who shall become [holy]: 'Who is holy like you, Lord?' (Ps 86:15). For it has not been written, 'Who shall be equal to you among the gods, Lord?', but 'Who is your equal?'. For they shall be like, according to what was said: 'We shall be like him, what we shall see him to be.' No one is the equal of the Lord among the gods mentioned, nor does anyone among them attain [it] according to His works. Therefore also in the Gospel it is said, 'If I have not done the works which I did in them, no other man has done; he has no sin' (Jn 10:38). For even if the saints once did the same things as the Savior, it differs greatly in the manner: some working by prayer and faith toward God, others by exercising authority; therefore it is said that none of the gods are [gods] according to the works of the Savior. And it is said to us also in the beginning of the Second Book how it was said, 'Lord God, who shall be equal to you?', which we also ought to apply to the one encountering the prescribed word.

To partake blamelessly of the knowledge of the truth is impossible not through moral instruction and active deeds having been passed through (Ps 85:11ab). For one is first led by God through prayer in the way; but this second way is that of practical progress. For the beginning of a good way is doing what is just, and so on.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Son of the Handmaid and the Knowledge of God
english: To be able to walk in the truth of God, one must progress in it and pass through to the end. The end of knowledge and truth is to bestow upon those who have known it completely and as they possess existence.

He who chooses these very good things rejoices in the possession of them (Ps 85:11c–13). It is also to fear the name of God; the one desiring to have it with joy prays to be made glad in heart by God through fearing His name. Having obtained this, he confesses thankfully to the Lord God with his whole heart, which was made glad by the attainment of his requests. He also glorifies the name of God for eternity—that is, all the time of his life—it having become upon him great divine mercy, by which he was also rescued from the pit of slavery. For he named the lowest pit. For those sinning many and great things fall into the lowest pit, and in order that they might be rescued, they beg for great mercy, as one of them can easily say, 'Have mercy on me, O God, according to your great mercy.' It is therefore fitting for one rescued from such great evil to glorify the name of God for eternity and to confess to Him with his whole heart.

One should not receive unthinkingly the saying that these things are spoken by our Lord Jesus Christ, with the kings of the earth and the rulers standing and gathered together against him (Ps 85:14.15). 'Visit me' (Ps 85:16). For you visit, you look, not at another, but to make well and to have mercy. Therefore also in the following things, the king is worthy to be given and to be guarded the kingdom, which God himself has given to him. For with this will follow his salvation as a child of God. If the prophecy is that concerning Christ, the promised things, then in this manner the upcoming things are smoothed out: David says, 'Looking upon [me], as God, have mercy on me.'

And regarding your giving your power to your child in becoming human and taking the form of a servant. And since he follows the one who became man and died, God will save him, the son of your handmaid who said, 'Behold the handmaid of the Lord; let it be to me according to your word' (Luke 1:38). For truly, the handmaid and mother of the Lord is she who bore him. And he thought it to be said in parallel, the Lord as child and the son of the handmaid. And the people from the circumcision can also be a son of the handmaid. For Paul, writing to the Galatians, clearly says concerning these things, 'But he who is born of the handmaid according to the flesh has been born' (Gal 4:31).

'Let a sign be made to me for good of the prophecy being taken up, which forbids among us humans, of a virgin giving birth before the trial of a man and remaining a virgin even after the birth' (Ps 85:17). This is a sign for good, a help to our race. Therefore also we were comforted; for how could we not have been about to have the most complete consolation, having had God as a helper? 'God says he will remember Rahab and Babylon' (Ps 86:4a), for those knowing him. Consenting to this, now having known God, but rather having been known by God. For having taken up the knowledge of him, we shall know him more, and most especially we shall be known by him: 'For if anyone does not know, he is unknown.' And to someone God says, 'Because you cast away knowledge, I will cast you away from ministering to me; you forgot the law of your God, and I will forget you, your children' (Hos 4:6).

Therefore, regarding those who are ignorant of him through faults, God has forgotten them, even though they knew him. Behold, therefore, of Rahab, who takes upon herself the wide way, and of Babylon, being interpreted as confusion, God is said to remember those who have known him. For those turning from the wide and spacious way, they are Rahab, having known God, and those from...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Prayer of the Helpless Man
english: Having come into the tranquility and stability of the mind from poured-out and disordered affections, they have entered Babylon having known God, whom God remembers, deserving of His remembrance when judged. The expansion may signify those coming from the east and west toward the kingdom (Ps 86:6).

Regarding the Church, not only the rulers but also the peoples have been inscribed into the citizenship of the heavenly city of the living God, having a registration upon the church of the firstborn who are written down in heaven, which only God is able to recount. For their registration has not happened from the mere collection of their names, but from that which reveals the quality of their soul, which only He Himself bears. And it is possible to learn from the opposite by the observer: in Jeremiah it has been written, 'Those having departed from the earth shall be written' (Jer 3:3). Just as those having departed and having become far from God are written upon the earth as the image of the worldly, surrounding themselves with earthly and material things and thinking of them, so those bearing the image of the heavenly and having citizenship in the heavens, being enregistered there, have been enrolled in the book of God.

Regarding 'For Ma'elah,' that is, for the dance or the chorale of the sons of Korah, for the understanding and for answering wisely to him who fears God and because of this truly becomes an Israelite. For their fear is interpreted as having all the divine fear and reverence, and to answer with understanding is proper for a wise listener while announcing the song with the dance and the divine chorale of the psalm.

'I have cried to You not only by day but also by night' (Ps 87:2,3), not occurring in solitude among the bright and pleasant things of life (it is impossible to be so by day), but also having been in the gloomy ones, containing a nocturnal state; having cried out in the day, so that the participation in the good things might remain for me, and in the night, so that when its end is coming out of the night, I might be able to rouse my spirit toward You. And it is possible to say more simply, similarly to what was said by the Savior: 'The Father will avenge His children who cry to Him day and night' (Luke 18:7). For he who meditates on the law of the Lord day and night and through it...

With works and disposition, he cries out to the God of his salvation day and night, at times asking for salvation, at others entreating that it might be preserved, which already exists. And the voice saying, 'Let my prayer enter before you' (Ps 88:4), speaks with much boldness toward God. For I ask such things as are profitable for me and appropriate for you and good to give (for I ask for the truly good things); let our prayer become in your hearing; for in this way you will also grant the responses I have requested, descending and inclining toward my cry; for in this way I have believed to be heard; therefore, O Lord, I cry out to you.

For many are the enemies lying in wait to tear my life into the pit (Ps 88:4), by whom my soul has been filled with despondency and evil struggles, that is, the indulgence of evil circumstances. The Holy Scripture calls the same place both the pit and the grave (Ps 88:5). The Savior himself, having become not [a sinner], came for the salvation of those being slain to give a ransom, by the grace of God, having tasted death above all. For he alone died on behalf of all, and in this way he was counted among those descending into the pit.

For as each one rightly descends into the pit because of what he has done or thought, I was counted and numbered with them; not being led to this by the works of following, but by the Father's good pleasure and our will to be counted among those descending into the pit and being judged; not that I became arbitrarily and voluntarily as a helpless man, the likeness of which is not being raised to the man. 'Depart'; for he has become a man according to truth, and he says that to be like a man is not simply to be a man, but a helpless man. For being able not to suffer, not to be seized, and not to be bound, he gave himself, becoming obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.

But even if he has become a helpless man voluntarily, as also to be cast into death, yet he is free among the dead. For among all those departing to the place of the dead, being led by some, not only the wicked but also the distinguished, Jesus alone has been emboldened to say, 'No one takes my soul from me; I lay it down from myself, so that I may take it again' (John 10:18). But what [is] the soul of all [those] by some into...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Victory of the Savior over Death and Sin
english: It will be clear to one who has studied the Gospels. For concerning Lazarus, a distinguished man, it is said: 'And it came to pass that the poor man died and was carried to the bosom of Abraham' (Luke 16:22); and toward something trivial he says, 'In this night they demand your soul from you'; and toward another face he says, 'Until you are brought down.' For the one being brought down by others is brought down there.

Therefore, no one among the dead is free, whether they are those being pulled toward others or those being led to the place of the dead; but Jesus alone, having placed his soul by himself, receiving it from no one, has become free among the dead. And why? Because although all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God (Romans 3:23), being delivered from life with bonds, having difference in what is more and what is less having occurred in Hades, he alone, not having committed sin and not having known sin, has become free among the dead, as also to loose the bonds of death of the other dead in order to raise and vivify them.

For just as he alone on earth is the liberator of sins being given as a gift, he says, 'If the Son sets you free, you will be truly free' (John 8:36); so also, having become in Hades with freedom, he liberated the held souls, making fear work in those holding them; for even the gatekeepers of those places flew away, having seen his authority and his freedom. It follows then that you should interpret the following verses as having been spoken by Christ.

The Savior therefore says to his own Father: 'Even if I have come to be a Savior of the world, having come to seek and to save the lost, being made worthy of eternal salvation for all, but rather, O Father, you are the God of this salvation which I provide for the being saved; for I grant it by your will; therefore, becoming a Paraclete toward you on behalf of those who have sinned, I will save them, interceding for them.' Following this, you will understand the following, as previously foretold.
The Savior says: 'For no one will be able to snatch him who is guarded by the mighty hand of God' (Ps 87:6bc); for he is contained by God, invincible to those desiring to attack and snatch him.
He remains. But someone having become worthless through whom sin occurs, is unworthy to be made a part of the hand, and is cast away, no longer worthy to be held and remembered by God.

Since he says, 'Because I did not come into Hades and death according to my own work, but having tasted death on behalf of others, I bring the cause of falling into the lowest pit and into the very heart of the earth' (Ps 87:7) instead of 'You made me to go into the lowest parts of the pit,' just as having resurrected those in the depth of this, he leads them away from there to bring them into the paradise of God. 'You laid me in the dark and in the shadows of death' (Ps 87:7). For if he says he has become victorious even in death, it is not in death strictly speaking, but in its shadow (for he reached [the third day] having risen), and in the same way, having placed them in the darkness under them, he turned them away, so that they might no longer live in darkness but in me, the light.

The wrath of God is like fire, which takes sin as food (Ps 87:8). Because of these things he underwent, and he himself acts; and as they are being consumed, he also approaches (Ps 87:10a). When many human abominations were occurring, the wrath of God was being carried against them, but the benefactor Savior submitted himself to the wrath of God, so that he might be fixed upon it, no longer moving or acting to find fuel, and so that God might be extinguished, not having been fed by him; because he was not known to sin, having been tested in all things without sin.

And he brought upon himself all those wavering temptations and tribulations, so that having struggled and having been tested in all things, he might be shown proven, so that we are no longer subject to wavering. For he dispelled them; and it is said of God, 'They are not for you,' because they are brought upon them for His judgment. Those of the circumcision who knew him and were known by him were fortunate, but those who responded to the law and the prophets had become far from him, having turned away and having been shown to be traitors, having been cast out from the Father and having been made far from His own Son, whose hand exists from which...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Darkness of Perishing vs. the Light of Truth
english: He drove them away according to the [psalm]: 'They drove You from my hand' (Ps 52:11). And he says that the pretext for them being distanced from Him is that they made an abomination for themselves. For the Jews, having become sinners, considered piety to be an abomination; for piety is an abomination to a sinner. Therefore, they also made the mystery-initiating abomination of this [piety] an abomination to themselves, not being of such a kind.

'I was handed over and was not delivered away.' For the Savior was not immediately handed over by them unto death and departed, leaving them nothing remaining to them in the providing of a way for repentance. For it was necessary for them to be perceptive, just as His eyes are said to be, and they grew weak as if to see Him no longer. Because of this he says, 'My eyes have grown weak from poverty' (Ps 102:3). For the cause of the weakness is that spiritual poverty has come upon them, for they desired the flesh and, taking everything written according to the letter, they grasp it.

How then can His eyes, the perceptive ones of Israel, be able? It will be clear to you once you have understood: 'You are the body of Christ and members in part' (1 Cor 12:27). For just as those who believed according to the Gospel fulfill the body of Christ—just as the perceptive ones are the eyes, and the understanding ones are the hearers, while the practical ones are called the hands—so also, before the manifestation, those holding to the Scriptures were the body of the Word of God according to the stated analogy.

[Psalm 87:11-13] 'Can a voice be read thus: Will you not do wonders for the unfeeling ones, and will you not perform wonders for the dead who have lost the power to grasp?' For these things happen similarly to those who perceive and are able to marvel, not to those who fight against God, the impious, and because of this they remain unrepentant. For no one will pray for them.

'There shall be a resurrection upon your confession.' For those who happen to be God-fighters are not of a nature to confess. And regarding 'resurrection' here, he is not speaking of the most common sense (for all shall partake of this), but of the one occurring through repentance, as it is said: 'Does not he who falls not rise again?' (Luke 15:18). It is possible to decide: 'Will you not do wonders for the dead?' Only, he is not saying, 'Will you not do wonders for those who have been deadened by other gods,' since even those who become gods by fighting against God will not rise upon the...

To confess. For no one says that to those who have despaired and to those hidden in tombs, the announced mercy of you will be recounted to the living who desire to be shown mercy, but nor will your truth be [recounted] to those who are making a work of perishing and because of this are named perishing. For the Word recounts the mercy to those whose nature is to be shown mercy (for they are not those who show mercy to neighbors; for they say, 'Blessed are the merciful, for they shall be shown mercy'), but also the truth is not recounted in perishing, but to those who have passed over it and have reached salvation. The wonderful things are not to be known in darkness. Those held by superfluous wickedness and ignorance are darkness. For darkness is said of some, but also a land forgotten and a heart unremembered, being filled with thorns of pleasures and worldly cares. The wonderful things of the truth are not to be known in this, nor is practical justice and moral virtue in the land forgotten because of the thorns.

It is fitting for Jesus to speak with boldness, 'Why, Lord, have you rejected my prayer?' (Ps 87:15), for it is not that you have rejected my prayer and turned your face away from me because I have sinned at all; therefore, having received my petition, lead all into salvation, for whom I intercede, shining upon them with your face. When the rich one, who labored for us, became poor for our sake, toiling for our salvation, the text says, not saying at all that he is poor, but from youth. For being rich and existing in the form of God, having emptied himself in this present age, he became poor, from the time he was born and had age; and having been lifted up to the cross and having been humbled, and his body having been laid into the tomb, it seemed to be vanishing, causing many who believed in him to stumble, but having risen from the dead, he was lifted up again into the heavens, having been taken up so as to draw to himself those who are able no longer to see him as poor and toiling because of the humanization, but as rich and the icon of the invisible God (Ps 87:16-17). Since the Lord who became human bears the face of the many sinning of all humanity (for he took up the...)
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Preparation of Truth and the Oath to David
english: Regarding all sin into his own body, all impulses according to various sins and his terrors passed over him as to disturb him, but they are not able to work against him, since he has not known or experienced sin. And it is said that the impulses and terrors of God, which are powers serving through punishments, turn out to be vessels of wrath.

These, having passed over the Savior, disturbed him, saying, 'Now my soul is troubled' (Ps 69:1). For even if he possesses a most perfect soul, yet seeing such a multitude of enemies, he experiences a fore-passion, especially since the water of the day surrounded him all at once, rushing against him and drowning him, if he had not been an excellent diver. For just as perceptible water surrounding someone drowns him, especially if he does not know how to swim, so the evil powers kill the one crushed by them.

But if they have become as water around Jesus, surrounding him all at once during the day, they are not even able to harm him; for much water will not quench the love (Song 8:7). For the perfection which is placed toward God through love is unquenchable. And this existed according to the human nature of Jesus, so that the shield of the hands cannot harm him.

And thus Eusebius of Caesarea, Didymus, and Apollinaris explained. It is said many times that the generation is carried in two ways. It signifies the people from the circumcision and the Gentiles. And it gives the reason for which the mercies of the Lord are for ever, having brought [them] in, that if all, mercy will be built up for ever. For the age which has come has not arrived, God clearly shows mercy and does good; and by this he says mercy is built up for ever. For just as a building is composed of many and various things being fitted together, so a building of many being benefited by the mercy of God takes place. Perhaps mercy is being built up, the building of wisdom...
Having built for itself these things. For its humanization is the foundation and the end of the building of mercy, the removal of the pre-occupying sin of all those being shown mercy.

From these things follows: 'In the heavens your truth shall be prepared' (Ps 88:5). For since we, those on earth, are imagined to be able to perceive divine things not yet with a clear face, but through a mirror and in a riddle (1 Cor 13:12), in the heavens the truth of God is being prepared for those having been prepared from there as if they are about to face it. For then they face face to face the beauty of the truth, having seized the end of knowledge and understanding, the partial reaching of things having been abolished for them. And the truth of God is being prepared in those not thinking of earthly things but having their citizenship in the heavens, by wearing the image of the heavenly through which the heavens are used.

By this God gives to David his father the throne to reign over these people forever, Jacob, into the ages (Ps 88:4), as if there is no end to his kingdom. And so that no one might think that David attained this blessing by chance according to favoritism, God says, 'I have sworn to David my servant'; for since David has been proven a genuine servant and worshiper, I give to him a sign, that a virgin, chaste and untouched by man, shall give birth to the God who is with you among men. For this the voice of Emmanuel signifies; it is not the seed of David being prepared. And the 'I have sworn' spoken by God establishes the stability of the promise toward David. For just as an oath-taker keeps an inviolable intention, being pressed by the word of a binding agreement with God, so also God, regarding whom it is said He eternally and certainly grants by oath, does not act according to another. For He says, 'As for myself, I have sworn, says the Lord, not as to the unfaithful...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Circumference of Truth and Divine Light
english: He does not use mere words, but promises an unchangeable and unalterable will. Since his will regarding the man from David becoming his son is unalterable, it is fitting that the Lord said to my servant, 'You are my son' (Ps 88:7). No one of those born from God, having received the spirit of adoption, will be able to become like the Lord. For he alone, according to truth, is the offspring of God, while the others are called sons of God to partake in him.

For the sake of a perfect understanding of what is set forth, we shall use the apostolic voice, which sounds thus: 'Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ' (2 Cor 13:14). For having called God Father of himself and of those near him, he was reverent, not assigning to himself an equality with any glory to the only-begotten Son; therefore he added, 'And the Lord Jesus Christ,' having cried out only once: 'if indeed we have become sons by the grace of God, and he himself becomes our Father, yet also we are slaves of Jesus Christ according to the nature of our Lord who is' (Rom 8:17).

This very thought is confirmed by the set-forth word: 'For who shall be like the Lord among the sons of God?' (Exod 35:19). No one is, according to essence, a son of God, except the Savior alone, who is the only one consubstantial with the Father; but those who are not according to essence, but according to quality, shall be made like him, just as they become merciful like the Father and perfect as the Father becomes: 'You shall be holy, because I am holy' (Lev 11:44). For the Lord comes upon the clouds of heaven with much power and glory, and the saints shall be caught up in clouds to meet the Lord in the air, to be with him forever (1 Thess 4:17).

Therefore, of the Lord and the saints being in the clouds, no one of those caught up in clouds shall be equal to the one coming upon the clouds of heaven with much power and glory. For each one was caught up with power, but not with much glory. For that power and glory he possessed, but the Savior will come with much power and glory; and each of those was in a cloud, but not upon the clouds. The expression 'upon the clouds' establishes the authoritative and kingly, whence no one in clouds shall be equal to the Lord; for truly, the cloud of each of the saints, being spiritual, is the intelligible moisture (the clouds...

For he says, 'justice has overwhelmed' (Ps 88:8), no such clouds can be found equal to the Lord, who is also a cloud, since each of them only waters a little, but He waters not only all men but also all rational things.

He is also fearful to those who are opposed, threatening punishments and bringing them down against those who fall away from His divine commands. For you, being near Him in receiving His divine teaching, while sinning, are near the fire, as the words of the Savior say: 'He who is near me is near the fire, and he who is far from me is far from the kingdom.' Thus, in the present word, He is fearful to those around Him who, through having believed in Him, disobey His commandments; how great [is He] to those held by His virtue.

The truth about God is none other than the one saying, 'I am the truth' (John 14:6). If it is around God, it can never not be, lest God should descend from not being once surrounded by truth to this. But it is surrounded by this, generating it, and He alone is the true God. For just as He alone is wise, not participating in wisdom but generating wisdom, so He alone is true and has truth around Him, not taking part in it but being with others and giving it to them.

For the Father exists with the Son in every thought and energy; for the Word, being with God, is God the Word, since the Father is in the Son and the Son is in the Father; for it is fitting for a God-Word to be with God the Father. But also as light, God has light with Him, the Son, as it is said in Daniel: 'And the light is with Him.' For it is not 'was' or 'will be' but 'is,' for this shows eternity, and thus it is said to be an emanation of eternal light. And the truth is said not to have 'become' or 'be going to be' around, but to 'be' of the almighty God. And the eternal power will be present to the almighty God, which exists the same as the wisdom, truth, light, and Word of God, but also 'your truth is around you.'

Understand this (Ps 88:10): faith in Him ruling all creation and the sea, regarding what is written about Jonah; for there it is said that waves were stirred up in the sea, and again, the sea will be to Him from the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Creative Power and the Arm of God
english: of its violence. And Jesus, demonstrating by word what kind of son he is of the master of the dominion of the sea, rebukes it while it is being agitated and stirring up a storm, and immediately calms it.

But if the sea's allegory signifies the life of men, its dominion may be the evil one in whom the whole world lies, that is, the mortal and perilous state. By this, the master of the sea, providing weakness to its dominion, grants authority to the travelers to suffer against all his power, calming the unstable and irregular surges of its waves, which are called upon it, making it also a firm footing for those receiving authority to walk upon it with Jesus, of whom Peter bears the image.

For no one, apart from Jesus, is able to suffer the sea of life, becoming subject to anxieties and pleasant passions, unless he walks along with Jesus. For he is the one walking as if on dry land upon the sea, as it was said to him: 'Your ways, O God, are in the sea, and your paths in many waters' (Ps 88:12-13). For Jesus has trodden paths in the strong waters; the passions are also life-related anxieties that those following his tracks are able to mount.

Regarding the thought, all those interpreting confess his wonders, and the earth receiving Jesus, being a seed and bearing fruit, becomes his property, reaching one hundred and sixty and thirty. And he established the inhabited world upon its fullness, being no other than the church, in which souls dwell having adhered to the right reason and the truth. But sacred powers also dwell in it, intervening around those fearing him.

And the foundation upon which it was established is not other than that about which Paul writes, for no one else is able to lay a foundation other than the one laid, which is Jesus Christ. And the fullness of this spiritual inhabited world, being founded upon the same foundation, is the fullness of virtues and of the dogmas of piety, along with the divine gifts of the Spirit.
And the Lord created the north and the seas, so that they are no longer as they were before. For just as having created the two into one, a new man from the two, he has...

It has been struck, and the being-created heart is pure, from which it has become pure; and he creates also those outside of faith, so that in Christ they might become a new creation—not by creating the north wind and the seas. But everyone who obtains divine election and is suspended by light, having been enlightened, rejoices in the name of God with a light of knowledge.

Just as Tabor is indeed outside, but Hermonius is a suspension of light; for the Hebrew names of the mountains are taken toward these things. And if Tabor is also interpreted as a pit (for it does not carry the sense), you will understand how it is said 'a praiseworthy pit', having understood how God gives to some in a manner of blessing pits that have been dug; those who have dug them did not dig them out. And if the pit were spoken of in mockery, having changed the voice, it would not be named thus, as one should not enrich wells; the spring will rejoice upon the name of the Lord (Ps 88:14-15).

The poetic power of God (but this is His creative power, His only-begotten Son) is signified to all those who are within by name. For 'arms' is said in the [Psalms]: 'And the arm of the Lord, to whom was it revealed? And your arm, O Most High, and you shall not be afraid.' But also the 'hand of the Lord' is confessed in: 'My high hand has done all these things'; and 'right hand' in: 'Exalt me with the right hand of the Lord.' For the holy one says to God: 'Yours is the arm with might, reigning and holding all things.' And it also says: 'Let your hand be strengthened, performing wonders and accomplishing great powers.'

For Peter says to God: 'Grant to your servants to speak your word with boldness, stretching out your hand for signs and wonders' (Acts 4:29). In thought, the power of the Father is not different; Christ is called these things. For if He is the Son of God and Wisdom and the Word of God and Truth, He is the right hand being lifted up by God, suspending and lifting up all, and He goes forth before your presence as mercy and truth; for no one who is to approach your face has been previously pitied and has conversed with the truth. It is possible, then, as in other places and here, that mercy and truth are not other than the Only-begotten, as in 'God sent forth His mercy and His truth.' It is not other than the Only-begotten Son of God, who is the same.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Perception of the Lord and the Vision of the Prophet
english: pre-applying... to the intellects

If we effect power, then our horn shall be exalted in your good pleasure. For our horn was exalted by the good pleasure of God, who says, 'This is my beloved Son in whom I have been well pleased' (Matt 3:17). For He was well pleased to effect our salvation through His own Son. And because of this, he says, our horn was exalted in the good pleasure of God, since the perception of the Lord is that by which He perceives, fighting and defending those who receive this grace from Him.

And this perception belongs to the holy Israel, our king. For the king of the true Israel, seeing God, is a son; the same perception is not of the Lord. The same perception of the Lord can be as being worked by Him, and of the holy Israel as enduring it. And a holy Israel in these things is one who is sanctified in the mind to see Him. And our King, being restored by the Lord who transcends, what is the perception of our Lord the King and of the holy Israel? (Ps 88:20–23).

He who perceives a spoken word, if he only senses it, it is through hearing, if he hears the one speaking; but if he understands the things being announced, he does not perceive by hearing, but by vision of the mind he perceives the speech of the one offering it. Since God was showing things rather than merely announcing them, He speaks to His sons who are being enriched through progress and perfection, not in hearing but in vision. So also it has been written concerning Israel: 'And the people saw the voice of the Lord' (Exod 15:2). It is necessary to say, 'Heard the voice of the Lord,' but if it is said instead 'Saw the voice,' that is to say, he perceived it with the mind.

The prophets were seers of visions; for they did not say they were perceiving by sensing some things or by grasping them with the eyes, but they were striking with the mind at the beauty of intelligible things. 'You spoke in vision to your sons': 'I made help as far as possible,' saying this regarding the Savior who has come from the root of Jesse. For truly in this He set help to help all creation that is able. And the one on whom He set help is the chosen one from the people, exalted not according to divinity but according to the flesh. For concerning him it is also, 'Israel is my chosen one,' and the [people] received him...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Anointing and Calling of the Son
english: My soul. For he was chosen from myriads, as in the selection of the elect. And because of this the Father exalted him, granting to him the name which is above every name. 'I have found David my servant' (Ps 89:20); and since the one according to the flesh is of the seed of David, it is possible and sufficient for him to be held by the hand over all the rational creation so that he might teach me in this way; therefore he anointed him with holy oil, proving him priest and king in all things (In holy oil, by the Holy Spirit, clearly meaning anointed, as it is said: 'God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness among your companions' [Ps 45:7]), because my hand shall take hold of him, his arm being strong.

And the arm and hand of God, the divinity of the Only-begotten; and it takes hold of him, performing strange and great works through him. An enemy will not benefit in him; instead of the devil (for he does not know sin, nor is there deceit in his mouth), thinking he can benefit, while he is able to instill deception and other wickedness. But no son of lawlessness, having come to break the law, will be able to harm him by surrounding him with sin. But the benefiting against the enemy lies strictly in overcoming. And in the Gospel, indeed, the deliberating chief priests and Pharisees against Jesus, not overcoming in his gathering, said to one another, 'See, you benefit nothing'; and the whole world went after him (Matt 22:37)—so that they would not overcome at all.

These things, Didymus says, clearly dividing the one Christ, even if in some way he turned away his manifest slanders. For he clearly presents two persons and two sons, and leads toward this kind of life a doctrine; therefore it seems to me that the interpretation of the one before him is more preferable to those wishing to think devoutly. And Eusebius, through similar things to Didymus, almost brings forward recollections in which he selects: 'The one of the prophets etc.'

He says of David, because the one according to the flesh is of the seed of David, it is possible and sufficient for him to be of hand; for this reason the voice of David is taken up. He found and with holy oil anointed him, since my hand shall take hold of him, strengthening him by my arm (Ps 88:27). And the arm and hand of God, the Son of God, has been said. For he overcomes the man, taking hold of him, the one born from the virgin. And the hand overcomes him and takes hold, performing extraordinary works through him. And the enemy will not profit; the devil is in the man who is the Lord's; for he did not know sin, nor was there deceit in his mouth.

He himself (clearly the one anointed with holy oil) will call upon me; 'You are my Father, God,' he says (Ps 88:28). For since having been born from the virgin he has been called the Son of God, he will call upon me, saying 'You are my Father,' the only-begotten Son of God (for he is Son according to essence), but not only calling but confessing God as Father. And he took upon himself man, and was called the Son of God, and calls God his Father and the supporter of his salvation; for he raised him and into the heavens he took him up. And he has become a supporter also of his own salvation, not that he himself is saved, but that he saves those fleeing to him. And having thus called upon the Father, the cause of all, the Father himself sets him as firstborn, bearing the first things of all those who have been called sons of God, not in the same way as he was raised up with the only-begotten; for he alone is the genuine instrument and temple of the God Word.

But do not let him fail you, thinking until then that the throne of Christ will be extended until the fullness of this; for heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away (Ps 88:30). For he reigns again, his words not passing away after the passing of heaven and earth. For it has not been said 'I will throw down the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Defilement of the Sanctuary and the Scattering of the Apostles
english: His throne lasts until the passing of the heavens, but like the days of heaven; for after the passing, heaven is. It is not possible for its passing to be perishable. And the bright and combatable things can be days of the earth, but the bright and light-like mysteries of truth are days of heaven; likewise, the throne of the Savior, having been placed unshakable, remains forever.

In this, God steadfastly promises by swearing, upon which He has spoken and enters into (Ps 88:36–38). Since He does not change His mind after swearing, giving an unpassable priesthood according to the order of Melchizedek, He remains constant; and having promised to Abraham with an oath that in his seed all the nations of the earth would be blessed, He shows the immovability of the blessing. If indeed He gives something by chance, He does not swear upon it; for indeed, having handed the kingdom to Saul without an oath, He did not change His mind. Since He also willed that the Savior be born from David according to the flesh, and that his seed, having come from David, be unpassable and steadfast, He was faithful to Him regarding the making of the unshakable promises. Therefore, O Moses, David [says]: 'In my holiness, not lying, upon which I promised, his seed remains for ever, sharing the throne of his beginning with the Sun of Righteousness.' And the moon remains most fully illuminated as the gathering of those being enlightened by Christ for ever, when the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the righteous shall shine forth like the sun in the kingdom of their Father (Ps 88:39–46). And a faithful witness concerning this being so in the heavens exists; concerning Job he says, 'Behold, in the heavens is my witness and my supporter in the highest' (Job 16:19).

But Didymus did not give the intellect in the same way as the interpretation of Eusebius: 'You, O Lord, having said the seed of Christ remains for ever, have cast away his seed.'
