'He will deliver,' he says, meaning to have let go of desires toward uncleanness and toward passions of dishonor, and to stop making an unproven mind do what is not fitting. And he says also in the Psalms...
according to the inclinations of their hearts
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Fruit of the Womb and the Arrows of the Soul
english: Those striving for the care of life give to those with them the bread of pain, eating it constantly. Therefore they are deprived of the beloved of God, those who advise moderately that reaching the Lord is the end and providence.

If the beloved of God, those raising themselves toward piety, do not despise this, but instead a spirit becomes for them a private rest, having been turned and having changed from this life, with watchfulness being maintained according to the common way of living, then those previously mentioned eat the bread of pain. All their striving is done in vain, rising and standing up after sitting, and having sleep, sitting, standing, and rising up become to them useless. For they were not able to do these things not in vain, nor to eat the bread of pain, if they had given attention to the beloved of God before receiving the spirit from God.

And those who seem to go toward godliness, if they thought they were being enlightened by themselves, rise in vain; for it is not fitting that it be said of those who do not say, 'My spirit rises to you, O God, through the night.' But they also rise in vain for the energy of good things, sitting and resting again, thinking they are doing this not from God but from themselves. But the one who confesses this is from God says to the Lord, 'You have known my seat and my rising.' And it is necessary to have joy and gladness, eating the bread that supports the heart of man; they eat it with pain from grief and necessity, but not approaching its use cheerfully. Therefore, they are altogether incomplete and do all things in vain.

And the former inheritance of Israel was made; for a portion of his inheritance is Israel; he was the firstborn son of God, saying, 'Israel is my firstborn son' (Ps 126:3). And all were sons by chance through a concordant and united will according to one law of life. But second after them are the sons concerning whom it was said by the Father to the Savior, 'I will make you heirs in my place, and I will give you an inheritance.' And from both of the two inheritances, one has become, which the Spirit says, showing it in the Son, 'Behold, the inheritance of the Lord is the Son.'
Indeed, all possess the spirit of adoption and are born from God to practice righteousness. And a reward is this, being the fruit of the womb of the Lord who has come to visit.

For it is said to her by Elizabeth, 'Blessed is the fruit of your womb' (Luke 1:42). And 'fruit of the womb' is the name for that which is not from a man, but from Mary alone, through the Holy Spirit having come upon her and the power of the Most High having overshadowed her. For those who have received seed from the fathers are those fruits; for it is said to David, 'From the fruit of your loins I will set [someone] upon your throne' (2 Sam 7:12), teaching him that his kingdom shall not fail like that of Saul, but that this shall be directed from his succession. And if the Son can also be the fruit of the father's womb, it follows, as [it is said], 'From the womb before the morning star you were born, visit [them].'

Who is the powerful one, the Savior, who is able to send the arrows of wisdom and truth sufficiently to wound for love? For it has been written, 'Your arrows are unavailing' (Ps 126:4). Similarly, those who are born of the sons of the stretched-out ones, those born of the holy men, are archers. And those who are stretched-out do not consist of all the dust of material things and soil, having sent forth by a rational movement a discerning soul capable of following the sequence of the dogmas.

And because of this, the Word, seeing peace and exhorting toward it, entreats, saying, 'Shake off your dust, Jerusalem.' Since the young ones, being stretched-out in the ancestral tradition of the Hebrews, are called and are capable for war, as we learn from Ezra, it is fitting that those who have put on the new man should stretch out the old man from themselves through his deeds, becoming imitators of the Powerful through their deeds, and through their hands being called to the word, they possess the arrows to strike the unavailing words. And the sayings of Ezra concerning the stretched-out ones are thus: 'And it came to pass from that day that half of those who were stretched-out were doing the work, and half of them were resisting, with spears and shields and bows and breastplates, and the leaders behind all the men of Judah who were building on the wall, and the...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Spiritual Meaning of the Blessed Man
english: Next, through the spoken words, we understand that the sons of those stretching themselves out to build the house of the Lord hold stones and swords and other weapons, as with one hand doing the work of the building, and with the other throwing stones to hinder those wishing to stop the construction of the divine house.

For the divine teachers strive in each soul being educated to build for God and to fight against thoughts and evil powers attempting to obstruct the growth of the building. He blesses the man who, because he has preserved that which remains according to the image of God, has had his desire fulfilled from the arrows of the Mighty (Ps 126:5). For having been directed toward the desire of good things by them, he has been shown blessed. And possessing unashamed and undaunted boldness in the gate of the beneficial entrance, he speaks without being shamed by the enemies, who were striving to be obstacles to the fulfillment of desire and to the building.

And it is no wonder that he has blessed a man singularly; he has blessed in the plural, that those speaking in the gate shall not be shamed; for the word is not about one, but about everyone who has fulfilled his desire from the arrows (Ps 127:2). And in another way, if they nourish their own soul with virtue, so as to be according to God, desirable foods and joyful for the soul. He who does not fear the Lord eats the labors of his fruit, but he who loves him as perfect will eat the bread, the heavenly one, according to 'Blessed is he who eats bread in the kingdom of heaven' (Ps 127:3). And he says 'fruits' here, so that it might be in some way 'He shall eat the labors of your hands,' that is, of the practical powers.

The word is indeed somewhat shorthand, smoothing these promises to be given to the one fearing the Lord, as if they were complete, but not to the one loving him with all heart and all soul and strength; for 'Eye has not seen and ear has not heard, nor has it come up upon the heart of man, what God has prepared for those who love him' (1 Cor 2:9). To the one fearing the Lord, a gift of God is given, a partner and a companion, not a woman by chance, but one grafted into the true vine.

Who can find a woman of worth, a good wife, and a woman of manly strength? Such a thing is more precious than costly stones. Just as the opposite of evil is good, and the wrath of God is a spouse in a harsh manner, so also sons from God are given to the one fearing the Lord; they are not like many sons, but like young olive shoots surrounding and crowning his table. You will also understand these from the perfection of the one saying, 'But I am like a fruitful olive tree in the house of God' (Ps 52:8). For the offspring of such an olive tree are called like young olive shoots. If anyone says that those not fearing the Lord often possess much in the property of children and in the prosperity of a wife, we will say that the present beatitude does not simply promise a wife and children, but all of this is depicted as a woman in a vineyard and children as young olive shoots; such things are not the lot of the ungodly.

From there: Blessed is the man who fears the Lord, since the wife accompanying you is fertile, finding herself like a vine rejoicing with fruits (Ps 127:4). But also your offspring are not weak or female, but strong sons being around your table, bearing the food of light like young olive shoots. And your spiritual table exists, full of all those who nourish mind and soul. Be having in these things a blessing from the Lord; no one else, but the God-fearing shall receive from the Lord. This is shown through 'the Man' and 'every man.' Therefore, regarding the present things, one ought not to take them as being about a sensible woman and bodily children, since many having obtained the fear of God have possessed neither wife nor children. If, then, the things of the word are not entirely literal, the spiritual sense of the things expressed must be sought by every one existing in piety.

By ascent you will understand thus: those being captured by the enemy in a single blow would not say this, but the one alone, driving the enemies into flight anew until old age, becoming always a victor and a triumphalist over them (Ps 128:1-4). And he brought forward the proof of having fought them many times: 'For even I was not able; for He was strengthening me, the Lord, who crushes the enemies.' Regarding those being announced with boldness, not the one happening by chance, but the one seeing God...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Harvest of Iniquity and the Sifting of the Wicked
english: He calls [him] a witness of the mind. And they show what is 'from my youth' (Psalm 71:5), and that having dared to speak from the womb and being drawn up for godliness, he opposes the devil and his allies and bodyguards, who are arrayed against him and fighting against him, and by no measure was he defeated by them.

The 'from my youth' is able to show that [he] is strong and being strengthened by Christ, from whom I have cast off old age, having cast away the old man with his deeds; having clothed himself with the new man, fighting against the aforementioned enemies, he was never overturned by them, but conquering unceasingly and steadily, and turning them to witness for Israel.

And the boast is not small, to be fought against by the devil and those around him, who do not possess this [strength]; for they are his friends and obedient ones. And everyone alone says, 'For indeed you were not able to trample upon me, having received authority from the Word of God, upon the lion and the scorpion, and to trample the lion and the dragon' (Luke 10:19). For having escaped all such things, the God crushing Satan under his feet, he says, 'Many times they have fought against me from my youth, and indeed they were not able; but I was able against them, being strengthened by the Lord. The sinners have stretched out their necks upon my back, they have lengthened their lawlessness' (Psalm 74:18).

It is a stain and very dangerous to have the enemies before [one's] face, having them sufficiently according to thought, and to harm and destroy them merely through seeing and through the senses, those whom we have perceived of them; it is proper to always turn away from them, casting them upon the back. For he who hastens toward God and virtue turns away from wickedness.

For if the sinners have stretched out [their necks] upon the face and before [one], they have harmed the heart, timely casting it into evil thoughts, and the sight through destructive spectacles, and the other senses harming through those things belonging to them. But he has the sinners behind, the one forgetting those behind, and stretching out [himself] toward those before, and going behind the Lord God; but he who follows the interpreted sinners turns away from the Lord, as to say God, 'They turned their backs upon me and not their faces' (Psalm 74:18). Mis—

For they have cast your instruction behind them, following the demons who are lovers of their heart. The lengthening of their lawlessness reveals the persistent wickedness of sinners who weave a series of sins like a rope, and by adding to those who have already received, they lengthen their lawlessness. The word weighs such people down: 'Woe to those who pile up sins,' as with a long rope and as with a heavy yoke, subduing their lawlessness. For their hands weave injustice, and as adding sin upon sin, they lengthen their own lawlessness. The Lord is righteous and has cut off the necks of sinners. The righteous Lord cuts off the neck of those who do not submit to his good yoke. But he makes this addition good for those who, having cast off their inclination and strength toward worthless things, submit to the Lord, who is all naked and bowed down.

And the wise of this world are themselves like stubble, having only their promise until this present life; and they are a heap of roofs for those who through them act and think that they have surpassed all. Therefore, it is a dried-up stubble, not casting its roots into the soil (that is, the sensible things), nor hastening toward a spiritual planting instead of stubble. Before they are even cut, they dry up, not filling the hands of the one harvesting this stubble, because they have unbelief. For the ungodly shall not rise in judgment, and 'he who does not believe is condemned' (John 3:18). Not only hands, but even the bosom of himself the harvester of this stubble will not fill, by not receiving them first into the bosom of Abraham, and then thereafter into the bosoms of the harvesting angel; for the Savior interpreted the harvesting angels as the harvester wielding a sickle in the prophet: 'Therefore I have cast away your prophets' (Matt 23:37). He himself also cleanses his threshing floor, having the winnowing fan in his hand to gather the wheat into the granary, but the chaff to burn with unquenchable fire. And who are those who hate Zion? They become not stubble, but like stubble, the weeds sown among the good seed by the evil one and being burned in the future.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Cry from the Depths
english: the grass of the roofs are those who have leaped over

Not as one ascending, but finding no one able to help, he cries to God. Along with confessing where he has fallen, he says, 'Out of the depths I have cried to you, Lord; Lord, hear my voice; for having heard, you will raise me up from the depth of wickedness and the deepest pit' (Ps 130:1-4). This expression agrees with what is said by him later: 'If iniquity be observed, Lord, Lord, who shall stand?' (Ps 130:4).

It is possible even for one dwelling in the earthly place, through human life, to send up this prayer, feeling himself far below both heaven and God; for heaven is high and earth is deep. It is also possible for the one praying to be holy according to what was previously stated. For he does not send up the prayer concerning small and earthly things, but large and heavenly things. He does not send up the prayer from a psychic discourse concerning them, asking for them, but being enlightened by the Spirit, searching all things, and knowing and contemplating the depths of God. Following the one searching these things by the Spirit, it is necessary from these depths to cry to God, deeming himself worthy of having his voice heard. And from these depths he cries, seeking not the non-sensible but all intelligible things and the Holy Spirit itself.

It is equal to 'Let your words be done' (Luke 1:38) for those attending to 'Incline your ear to my voice' (Ps 40:5). Since our voice does not reach the heights, and because there is a great difference in the nature of your words. And from here we learn, having understood, that they are not always the same, but 'Let it be done' also signifies a certain relation. For the words of God do not simply become, but become worthy of attending to Him. Following this, one must also understand what was said concerning Christ: that He became to us wisdom from God (1 Cor 1:30), and that God made Him both Lord and Christ, and such things. Since from you is the propitiation (Rom 3:25), the one being propitiated and, having forgiven sins, [is] Savior, not—
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Spiritual Zion and the Davidic Promise
english: Observe, examining iniquities; for if he were to do this, no one would stand. For all have strayed, all have sinned. Therefore, since no one stands before the judgment from you, there is need of the propitiation from you, being propitiated for the salvation of all.

And what is the propitiation, the Savior? John writes: 'And if anyone sins, we have an advocate with the Father, a righteous Lord Jesus Christ' (1 John 2:1); and he himself is the propitiation for our sins, not only concerning ours but also concerning the sins of the world. But also Paul: 'For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, whom God put forward as a propitiation through faith in his blood' (Romans 3:23-25), and the following. A symbol of this propitiation was constructed in the law, concerning which also now the one praying to God says: 'That from you is the propitiation'; from you, as a generation from the only good Father, is the propitiation. Not every rational creature needs, not with a god to be upheld, observing the iniquities of each of the created ones.

Always and at all times it is necessary to hope in the Lord, not only the one standing openly but also the one standing in gloom. From the morning watch, the one with the bright things present, and until night, the one with the dreary and darker things surrounding; and what is from the morning watch, the rising of the true light and making the beginning of a mental day, the discerning mind, Israel, called by the Hebrew voice, let him hope in the Lord (Ps 129:6-8), expecting from him an addition of the bright things and a deliverance from the gloomy things, what is from him as in a fountain and from him the mercy which those hoping in him need; but also much redemption from him, the propitiation from him is not another; for he himself from all iniquities will redeem him. For even if the iniquities of Israel are many, from all he will redeem him.

David, having perfected gentleness, says the following: 'Remembering me,' he says, 'upon these things you will give me an inheritance, the land of the gentle' (Ps 131:1). And those with these priests, not by chance, but they shall rejoice, they shall rejoice, of the only perfect and from the beginning rejoicing, from the most perfect rejoicing of this thing. And it is possible that the...

The person and the saint are the same, though distinguished by relations, for one is priest and the other is a saint of God, being the same in substance as the subject. Who is the cause of them putting on righteousness and rejoicing? It is David, the holy one, who is capable by hand. For the Lord brought forth for David his servant. He who became God's servant according to the flesh from the seed of David, having taken the form of the servant, emptied himself.

Understand thus [Ps 131:10b]: intending by your grace to shine upon men the face of your Christ, O Lord, do not turn it away, so that they may remain unhidden from his appearance, having been benefited. The cause of the certain fulfillment is the one having brought forth, saying, 'The Lord swore truth to David and will not deny it' [Ps 131:11].

The 'certainly shall be' regarding what was sworn in truth to David, concerning the coming of the Lord, is that the fruit of the womb of David shall sit upon his throne [Ps 131:11]. He will fulfill it as he swore; for the oath of God is truth, according to what was said by Gabriel to Mary concerning him being genealogically from David: 'And God will give him the throne of David his father, and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever' [Luke 1:32; Ps 131:12-13].

If someone takes the earthly Zion, how could he understand 'that my resting place for ever and ever' [Ps 131:14], since passing to the end of this age, the heaven and the earth pass away? For if the whole earth passes away, then the Zion which is upon the earth will also pass by. Regarding the spiritual Zion, concerning which it is written, 'Sing to the Lord who dwells in Zion' [Ps 87:1], that is the most holy Church, which he desired for a dwelling place for himself, he who said, 'I will dwell, what I have desired' [Ps 131:14].

Another [text] instead of 'the widow' says 'the huntress' and says: 'The unprotected and the brave guardian they do not have, I will bless all the poor to whom he provides an abundance of bread,' he says, 'I will fill her poor with bread' [Ps 131:15], since each of such poor people, being the seed of the righteous, is not diminished by bread. It is carried in copies as 'Blessing her huntress, I will bless.' And being blessed with the blessing of the Lord, she was a huntress hunting on every high mountain and...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Anointing and the Spiritual Dew
english: The sent-out fishermen and hunters in the crevices of the rocks are a symbol of those dwelling in the village of the hunters, for all dwell in Bethsaida, which is taken to be the village of hunters (Ps 149:9). 'I will clothe the priests of this Zion with salvation' (Ps 149:4). Christ has come as salvation for all, to seek and to save the lost (Lk 19:10). Regarding the presence of salvation and the clothing of it, it is written: 'Let my soul rejoice, for you have clothed me with a garment of salvation; they shall rejoice, and those who are holy of him shall rejoice in divine joy' (Ps 18:10).

There, in Zion, I will cause a horn to rise up for David (Ps 132:17). This horn of the kingdom is raised up by God in the house of David, according to what was said by the righteous: 'Raise up a horn of salvation for us in the house of David' (Ps 132:17). Prepare for this horn, Christ, who is found as a lamp, the Father running forward with his divine law for his visitation, for it is written: 'Your law is a lamp to my feet and a light to my paths' (Ps 119:105). And John, until the law and the prophets, is a lamp being prepared for his own Christ, concerning that Savior. There is that lamp which is kindled and shines: 'Did you not desire to rejoice at the right hour in his light?'

These things being theologized concerning the one who came from the seed of David according to the flesh, his enemies shall clothe themselves in shame, desiring, if they were consumed by fire, to say 'that a child was born, a son was given to us' (Isa 9:6), not recognizing the beginning of his time, mocking shame more, saying 'what he embraces with other men does not have a life that has ascended far above.' Therefore also upon him his holiness shall blossom, as it is said in Isaiah: 'And a flower shall ascend from the root' (Isa 11:1), following which the flowers of the earth shall appear in our land; such flowers being present toward the blossoming of the holiness by the Lord. For this blossoming sanctifies those passing by it, which is the very holiness of God, a flower, or rather to say, 'I am a flower of the field, a judge of the valleys' (Isa 35:1). If the flower and the judge of the field and of the valleys do not do these things, it is not fitting that flowers should appear in our land, once God has caused his holiness to rise up upon the enlightened and those approaching the...

A blessed and spiritual feast. The beard is a symbol of manhood. The oil descends from the beard of Aaron onto the shoulder of his garment (Ps 132:2). Aaron represents the shadow of priesthood. His head, the original, is filled with the divine oil of the name of Christ, regarding which it is said, 'Myrrh, your name.' This oil descends upon the beard of each who is able to say, after surpassing the shadow, 'I have become a man,' opposing the infant. Such a man becomes an imitator having become like Him, regarding which it is written, 'Behold, a man, whose name is Dawn, and a man comes after me' (Ps 133:1).

However, even if the oil descends upon Aaron's head, it does not descend upon a random beard but upon the high-priestly one, and from there onto the shoulder of the high-priestly garment. Aaron's tunic does not merely bear a type, for it is the Lord's body, born of the Holy Spirit, according to what was said concerning the Virgin: 'For that which was born in her is of the Holy Spirit' (Matt 1:18). Regarding the mountains of Zion, you shall perceive the divine and universal Church, which is the high doctrines of truth, the ornaments of the soul, having seized the being of Mount Zion (Ps 132:3).

Upon these mountains descends a spiritual dew, regarding which Moses said, 'And I will come down as dew' (Ex 16:4), and in the prophet, 'For the dew from you is its essence' (Hos 14:5). From this heavenly dew, the habitation of the blessed shall be from heaven. This spiritual dew does not descend from random clouds, but from the celestial light of the one saying, 'I have come as light into the world' (John 8:12). For this light both dews and shines from above, and makes [things] to become in most piercing brightness.

All the servants of the Lord bless the Lord (Ps 133:1), not having stepped far from Him but approaching Him through wisdom. Therefore they have stood in the court of the Lord, firmly established in Him. And they have stood in the courts of our God. The courts of God are where those who fear Him stand, the God-breathed writings and the doctrines of truth.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Nature of God and Divine Participation
english: It is not a temple for those ascending into it to follow the songs of the ascents and praise God joyfully. Therefore also 'Alleluia' is written upon the psalm, the superscription signifying that the living God must be hymned (Ps 134:1-3).

How will it not be that all those having ascended the ascents with songs and hymns will stand in the house of the Lord with right thought and unassailable practice, being His servants in the house of the Lord, and hymning Him in the courts of our God? But the courts of God are the old and new Scriptures, the theologies according to their parts, or the many dwellings in the promises in the house of the Father. And to praise first according to the introductions His name, so that they might serve the Lord and serve Him sincerely.

And toward allegory, if there are certain spiritual clouds, they signify a mental and invisible rain flowing. And these rise from the end of the earth, since the Gospel does not call those from great, rich, philosophical, oratory rulers, but from men thought to be the lowest, the unlettered and the laypeople. But He has also made the bright flashes of theories and the justices into a rain, to enlighten and to water those asking for these things in harmony with what is set forth. And He brings forth winds from their treasuries, which some signify better breaths and intellectual, transcendent natures.

This memorial is from the former generation of the Hebrews as a generation of the calling of the Gentiles, concerning which it is written, 'The coming generation shall declare to the Lord' (Ps 134:13b-14). And these things shall remain, as God has mercy on His people and calls upon His servants. For having responded to the intercession and the appeal of His servants on behalf of the people and themselves, being sent up, He was comforted, that is, He granted the appeal. Therefore also He has mercy on His people.

According to an upward leading, if in Israel there are those perceptive and seeing God with a pure heart, and in Aaron those who serve Him perfectly and priestly-wise continually, not day by day (Ps 134:19-21); and with these, the Levites are inferior to the sacred things, those being in the temple and the services being imposed in the...

Those who perform the service of the 251st God [Psalm 135] will not be newcomers to God, being brought into justice; and all those from foreign nations are added by the fear of the Lord. However, even if all bless, not each one will do this according to the proportion of power.

But those previously mentioned do not merely bless, but he is also blessed, not from a chance place but from the heavenly Zion, dwelling in the city of God, who gives the heavenly Jerusalem and the church which has no house or wrinkle, unlike Jerusalem, to see the peace which Jesus gives, saying, 'My peace I give to you' (John 14:27). But even if he is blessed in Zion by another thought, God is not thus in it and from it. Let these things also be said concerning the soul through knowledge and perfect virtue, being called Zion and Jerusalem.

The present psalm, being called forth for thanksgiving, commands to confess to the Lord, who does much in kindness and goodness (Ps 135:1-3). Therefore, in every verse, a hymn-like phrase is selected: 'For his mercy is unto the ages.' For since he neither ever has mercy nor ever does not, but always has mercy, it is fitting that those who hymn say, 'For his mercy is unto the ages.'

Of what gods is he, concerning whom it is said? If he is not God to them, then the Word of God did not become toward them according to the scripture saying, 'I am God' (John 8:58). For this one truly it is fitting to be called God; so do not worry even about those who are called gods around Abraham (Exodus 3:6; 'God of Abraham, and God of Isaac, and God of Jacob'; for this one truly it is fitting to be called God). According to this, the meaning of divinity and angels and divine powers is said to be 'gods,' as the apostle says, 'As there are many gods and many lords in heaven and on earth' (1 Cor 8:6), so all those called gods with the Trinity are such by participation of divinity.

But the Savior is not thus, but is God by essence; therefore he makes gods of those who partake of him. He has been said to be the only-begotten God; for he himself alone is the true God from the true God, being God according to the same nature as the Father, being consubstantial with the one who begets him.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Allegorical Exodus and the Sea of Passions
english: If he is God of gods and Lord of lords, he is of those in heaven and on earth having a relationship to the holy principalities and powers and lordships (Ps 135:4–6). For it was written that he alone does wonderful things; for the Father, remaining in the Son, does the works. But also, while making the heavens in understanding and strengthening the earth upon the water, it must be confessed again. And what is set forth agrees: God in wisdom founded the earth, and prepared the heavens in prudence. Understanding and prudence are through which the heavens are prepared and strengthened; who is like the wisdom through which all things came to be, concerning which the theologian says Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God. For also those bearing the image of the heavenly become intelligibles, being heavens. Such things are prepared in the revealed understanding and prudence of God. And the earth is strengthened upon the water, receiving the seed cast under Jesus in order to bear fruit. For in the flowing and temporary things of life, they allegorically strengthen and provide firmness upon the water to bear fruit most fully (Ps 135:7–9).

Having made great lights alone, by saying: 'Let there be lights in the expanse of the heaven'; he arranged the sun for the dominion of the day and the moon and the stars for the dominion of the night, just as it is said in the creation to have become the sun for the beginnings of the day and the moon for the beginnings of the night and the stars. And these things contribute not a little to us for the order of life and for life itself: the elements nourishing fruits, without which one cannot live; showing us seasons, marking hours, representing the courses of day and night, guiding the travelers of earth and sea, providing ten thousand other uses. If you see how unto the age is his mercy (Ps 135:10–12). And towards diani-

Regarding what belongs to the tropical Egypt while the world exists around the earth, these things, appearing to be firstborn, are struck down by God for the benefit of Israel. For when these are struck down, the mind seeing God is led out from it by God. And God leads Israel out from the middle of the allegorically called Egypt through His word and His wisdom, which is named His arm and His mighty hand. And these things are said concerning Christ, since according to the Epistle of Jude, Jesus is the one who saved the people out of Egypt. A mighty hand and a high arm should be said to express His paradoxical energy and power.

God divided the Red Sea into not one division but into many, so that it might be driven out from the middle of it by God, while Israel walked as on dry land (Ps 135:13–15). It is given into twelve divisions according to the twelve ways, so that each tribe of Israel might have its own passage to pass through.

And these things are indeed according to the literal sense; but for the intellect, the life of man is often like a sea placed before us, filled with waves and much saltiness and turbulence, yet the word of God provides us a way through, rising up and piercing the storms laid upon us from passions, so that we might have a way through once the moisture of all those passions has been dried up by God, while the intelligible Pharaoh and all that from demons and unclean spirits are being sunk in it, his power being fulfilled as if he were scattering them like the most worthless dust into the [sea] of God.

Happening to be deceived by those prepared in a sophistical manner, since the Amorites are interpreted as those who provoke and the king of them, Sihon, as a temptation or an incitement (Ps 135:17–22), and since it was necessary to provoke others and to act as those who speak through sophistry...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Prayer of the Just and the Glory of God
english: Are they undermining the words, those enemies of the truth, intending to speak and to shout in order to deceive, to test and to provoke, having such a purpose?

But also, since Babylon is interpreted as a symbol of that which brings shame upon those doing evil, accordingly the king of this [Babylon] will be struck and killed along with the king of Zion among the Amorites, so that the land may be given to Israel. They ruled it badly through sophistry and through a wearying life, meddling in the nature of things and appearing to rule it; but their interpreted land being taken away, it is given as a possession to Israel to inherit it, becoming a true servant of the cause of all things. (Ps 135:23-24: And when we were brought low through misfortune, he remembers us and redeems us.)

Let my confession be upon your mercy and your truth, since, having been often shown mercy and having seen the truth which was enlightened in me by you, I was rescued from all evil and from its related deception, you providing remission of sins through your mercy and keeping me from all wandering through your truth. (Ps 137:2: Let my confession be upon your mercy and your truth...)

But since you have magnified the word given to me by you, depending on it through your presence as if it were your own wealth, I will worship toward your holy temple and I will confess your name, giving thanks that your word is being magnified in me; for then it is magnified in me, and since I am progressing by it, I hasten toward its perfection. (Ps 137:2d: Another scripture is brought forth saying, 'That you have magnified your holy name above all.')

When is this fulfilled? When every knee shall bow in the name of Jesus, both heavenly and earthly and under the earth, every tongue confessing what the Lord Jesus Christ is, to the glory of God the Father, announcing to his brothers who have come to be the Son's likeness the greatness of the Father's presence; for he has not come alone in the name of the Father, so that the holy name of God might be magnified above all. We learn to say in prayer, 'Hallowed be your name.' But just as the hallowed name of God does not become holy from something profane, but is shown to be such, it is not magnified by increase as...

To become great from something small, but with his greatness being made manifest. The one who prays unceasingly and performs this by spirit and mind: 'I will pray, saying, by spirit, and I will pray also by the mind,' having God as a listener on each day, concerning whom it has been written, 'and the ears of the Lord are toward the righteous, and to their supplication' (Ps 137:3). For one possesses God as a guardian who does not delay nor despise him, but watches over him in his provident power.

Because of setting the mind on earthly things and seeking the lower and temporal things, making a profit, the peoples of the earth—about which the prophecy says here—the reason for wanting all the words of your mouth that you spoke in the law and in the prophets concerning their calling is this: for even if they are not hearers of your oracles, it is not by their power that their faith was foreknown. Therefore also I desire to reach them with diligent and musical recitation in your ways, namely, the Scriptures, so that one traveling through them by continuous study and reading might diligently proclaim the meanings from them. And if someone speaks of the virtuous ways of the Lord, and someone traveling diligently through these [ways] sings triumphal hymns against the wickedness that of old was working in them; if someone diligently speaks the word of virtuous activity concerning each of the ways of the Lord, having sent forth a diligent voice through the actions according to them.

All these things shall be made perfect, since also the glory of the Lord which performs these things is great, concerning which it is said toward Jerusalem: 'And the glory of the Lord has risen upon you, and all flesh shall see the salvation of our God' (Ps 137:4-5), since the glory of the Lord shall be seen. And who then is this, the savior, being a radiance of the glory of God and a character of his substance? It is brought here instead of 'Peoples' as 'Kings': 'Let all the kings of the earth confess to you, O Lord' (Ps 137:6). And both expressions have harmony with the concept of being called to reign, the peoples confessing to the Lord being set as a royal priesthood and a holy nation (Ex 19:6); and toward some of them it is written, 'And you have reigned, so that we also may reign with you' (2 Sam 5:11).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Inaccessibility of Divine Wisdom
english: Not only concerning the Father, but also concerning the Son, these things are to be spoken, since He holds all things that were made through Him and in Him they consist, and above all things He is. Thus also the almighty rule is ordered upon Him, as in the prophet Zechariah (Zech 4:6). Even if the High Lord sees someone among the lowly, He is high to the heavenly and is of a nature that has ascended far above, but He does not only know these things from a distance as being far from Him by a change of existence.

In this way, the apostolic word is like it: 'Beloved, do not avenge yourselves, but give place to the wrath; for it is written, Vengeance is mine, I will repay, says the Lord' (Rom 12:19; Deut 32:35).' That is, do not hand us men over to invisible enemies intent on killing us. By which I press forward toward the front, until I reach the prize of the high calling (Ps 138:7).

And it is nothing wonderful if He knew all things concerning me, He says (Ps 138:5); for knowing all things, He does not merely observe them, but also the beginnings and the ends of them, and the causes by which they came to be, and what will be about them after the cosmic variety. Having formed me possessing the knowledge of all things, You placed Your hand upon me, which is said first. Having placed Your hand upon me, and having formed me from dust and clay as a man, it is as if one of the wise said this: 'Your hands made me and formed me,' and likewise, 'Remember what clay You formed me from.'

And it is also not so; having formed me, You were not satisfied with having made me, but You also placed Your hand upon me in order to improve and guard me and to lift me up by it. Therefore, let him who understands this gift and advises others be careful, saying, 'Humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, so that He may lift you up in due time' (1 Pet 5:6), so that, being secured by it, you may not have any insolence or scheme occur. For no one snatches from the hand of the Father; for the invisible enemies only tear apart those who have been cast away from it. Having understood how You have knowledge of all things, I have come to a marvel. But even if, having understood, I marveled at Your knowledge, it is not that my will understands it on my behalf, having been made [by You].

It has been strengthened so that I might not be able to reach it. This is consistent with what is in Ecclesiastes: 'I said, I will be wise, but wisdom has departed from me, and it was made far from me, beyond my reach; who can find it?' (Eccl 8:17). And also Paul left the same voices, saying: 'O the depth of the riches and the wisdom and the knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments and untraceable are his ways!' (Rom 11:33). And he himself says this, since he is not able to reach the knowledge of God having been strengthened beyond him.

It is also possible for that which is near me to show that your wisdom, which is wonderful, was not revealed to me, because once it is strengthened, I will no longer be able to oppose or strike at it. And if even concerning the knowledge of God, the saint himself has words about it as one who is grasping it, discussing the things set forth, having visited it. Having theologized about the things concerning the foreknowledge of God, that He is, and has the knowledge and understanding of all things, he moves on to say that He is everywhere.

He indeed says toward the one being theologized about: 'If your spirit has filled the inhabited world, where shall I go from it? But since your face also observes and looks upon all things, where shall I flee from it? For ascending into heaven, with you present, I receive a vision; if I become in Hades, I see you present' (Ps 138:7-12). And if in heaven and in Hades your presence is known, and in the intermediate places it is evident that you are there; 'Do I not fill the heaven and the earth?' says the Lord, as the prophet says (Jer 23:24). But also in the sea itself, he manifests himself to those seeking him, as the following word presents.

Therefore also, one of the theologians says to one of those listening: 'And he shall know by intellect what God is in the heaven above and on the earth below, and there is nothing besides Him.' But He presents Himself everywhere, not locally dwelling, but creatively and providentially entering into all things. For he says concerning the only-begotten Word that all things consist in him; and if all things have been established in him, nothing of those established in him is left out from him. And we learn also from the things set forth the theologized Trinity. For the Holy Spirit, the Spirit of God, has often been demonstrated to be a person, his only-begotten Son being an image of him.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Illumination of the Night
english: It is said to be the being of the invisible God, and also the character of his own subsistence. From this we learn that the Spirit of God is not a creature, but is joined to the God himself and to his person. For it has often been demonstrated that he is never with the creation, but always is joined to the Father and the Son. Only this is presented as a contrast: that it becomes my case to pass locally and ascend, while it is your case to be present and to be established there, in having made him and turning him, and also to descend into the sea similarly passing, by your presence of providence there.

Therefore, God is not in a place; for if he is everywhere, not passing from one place to another, nor being limited by each one, nor being circumscribed by all the places, it is evident that by a creative and providential presence he moves through all, upon all, through all, and exists in all, according to apostolic philosophy (Ps 138:9-10). 'I searched,' he says, 'whether by using the wings of thought I might have become far beyond the sea and the ocean itself at the ends, whether I would be able to go from your spirit and flee from your face, and there also to have seen your active and providential hand, and that very right hand of yours surpassing, working; as this very thing, that to have dwelt with me, would be established for me in a predicted sequence at the ends of the sea, your hand guiding me and holding me with your right hand.' For even if the ocean is boundless, yet even the worlds with it are driven through by the commands of the Lord; for all things having been made toward him, whatever they ever are, are straightened for me by the commands of his own providence (Ps 138:11-14a).

Since, having been enlightened by the knowledge of the Lord, to have become in the morning at the beginning of the day, I meditated on glories with the intellectual wings through which every rational nature is lifted up to be far off and beyond the ocean, he also knew this very thing: not to be able to go from the spirit of God and the following, to seek another way, by which to go from the spirit and flee from the face of God who is, lest perhaps by darkness...

I will be able to speak this having happened. Therefore I say, 'Alas, darkness will tread upon me,' that is, it will cover me. For just as the floor that is being trodden upon is hidden, not being hidden underneath, if the darkness happens to tread much around me and upon me.

If indeed the glory is a luxury regarding the attainment of what is labored for, immediately even the night and the gloomy darkness is illumination, nothing of that darkness being darkened by God illuminating it just as also all other things. For among us, those using the distinction see the difference between night and day, and those seeing in the day, but in the night they neither see nor are seen; but with God, the night is illuminated as the day, seizing for himself those in darkness and night as those in light and day, since the night is illuminated as the day by God himself.

The righteous man applies all these things to himself, having intended to teach those having wrong opinion about God that it is not possible to flee from God. For are those thinking these things about God, to say even the God himself, 'Will someone not be hidden in secret places, and I will not find him?' (Ps 139:12), for God is approaching all, and I am not God from a distance. Cain has become a father of this ill-reputation, having said to God, 'If you cast me out from the face of the earth today, and from your face I will be hidden' (Gen 4:14).

And another, through surpassing foolishness, sinning in a dim and gloomy place and night, says, 'Darkness covers me from every side, and the walls cover me; who sees me?' (Eccl 10:3); 'The Most High will not remember my sins' (Ps 139:12), saying only once, 'Since in darkness and in the midst of the gloom I sin, with no one present, I elude everyone, and even the Most High would not know my sins.'

But stop, for if someone becomes further than the word concerning darkness, he will be able to behold mysteries, if the division of the things being said is such: 'Will I indeed be able to flee from God, having become evil and trivial, as to become under the darkness and to be trodden upon by it?' But having thought this, he immediately knew that even the night is illuminated in the day, that is, in the luxury of the rational animal; for illumination from virtue and knowledge is truly and appropriately a luxury for the rational animal.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Divine Knowledge and the Unworked Creation
english: Lest I become a son of night and darkness, having striven to be a son of darkness through whom I act and think wickedly; rather, since the darkness is not darkened by it, God who illuminates all things says: The God who said, 'Let light shine out of darkness,' who shone in the hearts of men for the illumination of the knowledge of Christ, [says] night shall be as day, of the one passing from ignorance and wickedness saying, 'I am not a son of darkness and night but of light and day.'

For this reason night shall be as day, since its darkness is not so, nor its light. For since darkness is held by choice and not by nature (for no one is evil by creation), so also it holds virtue; and finding no place of flight, having turned to himself, he says: It is no wonder that, having become evil, I cannot be far from you, since I have even possessed my own kidneys, God who examines kidneys and heart; for if you are a knower of my hidden things, having possessed even my kidneys, in whatever part of the world I may be, you have knowledge of my presence; for if you even took hold of me from my mother's womb, having formed me in the belly and laying your hand upon me. Since, because of all the aforementioned things, you were fearfully wondered at (for with fear I have marveled at all things concerning you), I say, turning toward thanksgiving: I will confess to you what I fearfully wondered at (Ps 138:14b,15).

God has possessed the kidneys of the one who has accomplished purity in temperance. He, therefore, being idle in celibacy, having inscribed his own kidneys to God, says: You have possessed my kidneys, Lord; with the achievement of knowing all his wonderful works of creation, providence, and paradox, he says: 'Wonderful are your works,' and my soul knows it intensely. The 'intensely' refers to the knowledge of the soul or to the wonders. And the [text ends abruptly]...

He says: 'You have done in secret so that no one knows the combination of this; nothing of it is hidden from you' (Ps 138:16). For how can those who are your handiwork not be like the soul of the body? And it is said also to those discussing the nature and generation of animals that the transformation of blood into bone is invisible and incomprehensible, even though I say that others observing the generation of flesh and nerves see how they are.

And the scripture of Ecclesiastes establishes this, not saying 'as a bone in the belly of the pregnant' (Eccl 11:5), but 'you shall not know the works of God.' And my substance was not hidden from you, having reached the lowest parts of the earth; for neither the soul having been created in water, nor even the body having been decomposed and dissolved into the earth, escapes your vision.

Through these things extended, having theologized with prophetic eyes, he says he has seen the Lord's visitation, that it has come from the virgin. For having been born from the virgin Mary, the birth is unworked, not composed from a studied combination of labor, but existing from the Holy Spirit. Some understand this as what was said in Daniel concerning the stone being cut out without hands (Dan 2:45).

This being made manifest unworked, subsequently salvation for all shall come to be, as if it were written of them in the book of God to become worthy. But since that also can be unworked—being of a nature to receive labor yet not having had it—it is possible to speak concerning all those who are about to exist, the Maker of God, and especially concerning the resurrection of the dead, of which the said thing is the anchor. Since my substance is in the lowest parts of the earth, and not to always have such a thing, I say I have pre-conceived this with faith and hope, that the resurrection of the dead will be: 'Your unworked [thing] my eyes have seen, and upon your book all [are written]' (Ps 94:4).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Nature of God's Enemies and the Deception of the Tongue
english: They shall be written: all things happening to them in all things, and all darkness, and all grief, and pain, and the sighing happening from the feet, but in a bright day they shall shine forth like the sun in the kingdom of their own Father. For it is said, 'They shall be made as the Day' (Ps 139:16), so that they are no longer in the darkness of their creation, being sown in corruption and in dishonor, but in light and in a day standing together, being raised in incorruption and glory.

But since they are not made such as the day, and since all things happening in all things are written in the book of God, God will be in them, and there is no one among them of the evil ones or worthy of being despised. Perhaps the multitude and the 'who' and the 'no one' will vanish; for because of a great perfection and for the sake of oneness and identity, having restored the number, there shall no longer exist a 'who' or a 'no one' among them, having understood all things into the unity of the Spirit. The 'who' and the 'no one' shall no longer be among them.

A scripture is brought forward: 'My unformed eyes saw you' (Ps 139:16). And let this itself be understood likewise: 'You understood my thoughts from afar,' instead of 'the unformed of my thoughts'; before anything is accomplished, your eyes, seeing all hidden things, are full. And the Gospels are full of such things. They are friends of God, having come to be from faith and virtue. For it is said concerning Abraham: 'Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness, and he was called a friend of God' (Gen 15:6); and concerning Moses it says: 'God spoke to him mouth to mouth, face to face, as if one were speaking to his own friend' (Exod 33:11). But even the greatest of the prophets has not become such a friend of God. And toward the apostles, indeed (they possess this friendship), Jesus says: 'I say to you, my friends' (John 15:15).

And these rulers, receiving authority from the King Christ over more than ten cities or more than five cities, are very strong as they co-reign with Christ. And it is said also by another meaning: their rule is strong because the reasons for it are friends of God. For those who are highly honored, friends of God, through a multitude of contemplations and good activities which they have, shall be multiplied beyond the immaterial, that is, beyond the sensible and the bodily. For since the companions of the material [things] regarding the immaterial [are] under this as the foundation of the house...

Their path, having fallen easily upon this, is established or fortified under this; which carries a symbol: the Egyptian, having been struck down by Moses after being seized by error, is necessarily taking a super-cosmic disposition, being worthy to be numbered by God despite the error (Ps 138:21-22). Regarding the same, it is to accept and honor the friends of God and to hate those who hate him, and to count as enemies the impious and those who think foolishly concerning God. For how are those who turn the deceived away from the truth not enemies of God, since God wills all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth (1 Tim 2:4)? And perfect hatred exists against such people, not for the sake of another, but because one hates them as enemies of God. And just as someone has perfect love toward the good, not for the sake of another but desiring it for its own sake, so the one hating those diverse from God does so not for the sake of another but because they are enemies of God, raging against them according to the one saying the prophet, 'I have envied with zeal for the Lord Pantokrator, whom the sons of Israel have forsaken' (1 Kings 19:10).

An evil man is a treacherous and deceiving man; but an unjust man is one who has ascended above this in wickedness, as if through craftiness and mischief, hastening the rational nature from virtue into wickedness, attempting to transfer it by some craft. Desiring to be saved from both, the one declaring the things set before him prays to God, since they reckoned iniquity against him, hiding it in their own heart, so that through remaining hidden, what such people are, they might be able to ensnare him, standing hostilely and against him for the sake of the duration of his life. Therefore, if it is said, 'All the day they prepared wars,' having no time of peace and rest, instead of a sword they have sharpened the tongue of themselves upon the deceiver, and being able to wound, they utter a word imitating the serpent who corrupts in his craftiness. And under their own lips, that is, their speech, they have thoughts made to be cast into them by evil powers because of the harmful and venomous nature of what are called 'darts.' And it is possible also concerning the devil and the other invisible enemies to grasp these things.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Power of Salvation and the Battle of the Mind
english: For a man is often called an evil one and an enemy, the devil. But also one serving his purpose may be called an antichrist. Ps 139:5,6: The hand of a sinner, the sinful practice, prays to be guarded from by God acting as a watchman. And besides this, it is worthy that he also be rescued from men who intend to do wrong by their choice, since they have reasoned through deceptive words and thoughts to trip up the steps of those walking toward progress in greater things.

It is possible in these things to catch the sinner, the devil, and unjust men, or rather his evil angels, or those who work men toward iniquity of soul. For they possess a deceptive wisdom, which they do not bring forth openly but hide like a snare under their sophistical words. But also their complex ropes of wickedness, which are composed and entwined by their sophistical words, stretch out to catch the feet of those walking rightly, calculating through these ropes to trip the steps of those who unthinkingly follow a path that someone has worn down.

Obstacles and stumbling blocks are, if they are thoughts, being cast against those intending to walk well and according to virtue. But he who has known himself, that he is not self-sufficient to remain harmless before so many [dangers], flees to God and requires power; therefore he also announces those surrounding him. Ps 139:7,8: He who is mastered by practice and thought will say practically to Him, 'My God, are you?' and it is worthy that he asks how his voice of petition might be heard, receiving it unto his own. For he truly says, 'O Lord of all, and You are my Lord, and I am your servant; therefore You are the power of my salvation.' For of the truly and attainable salvation of yours, man's power exists to have an impossible salvation if he has not become in you. And my salvation is the likeness according to the image and the likeness that has become yours, to partake of your holiness through which also salvation exists. And that very gospel is the power of God unto salvation, as it is written by the apostle regarding the one becoming in the gospel...

One possesses the power of salvation by living and acting according to the Gospel. The power of my salvation, O Lord, has overshadowed my head on a day of war, specifically my mental head. I am convinced, therefore, that nothing is difficult against the invisible enemies during the day, that is, during the temporal extension of this life. The testimony that the head is mental is found in 'The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of the righteous' (Ps 112:3) and 'The eyes of the wise are in his head' (Ps 111:10).

The sinful devil takes those who perform sin, making them his instruments. It is not clear, however, if one is mastered by a certain shameful desire. For if someone is drawn from desire into practical sin, he immediately becomes the devil's instrument; but if, having looked at a woman with desire, one stops in thought to prevent the fulfillment of the desires, he will not become the intended sinner. Therefore, one prays to the Lord that from desire alone, without being drawn into the action of the desire, he may not be handed over to the sinner, nor proceed further being conquered by it, but rather always be prevented by the better thought from You. It is also said: since all good desire is present to me as a righteous man, let me not be such as to fall from such desire and be handed over to the sinner having acted sinfully.

‘Lest through many of my thoughts I may be able to [sin], do not leave me, guarding me in the shelter of your wings and under your strong hand’ (Ps 139:23-24), so that no one may seize or lift himself up arrogantly against me as one caught by him. A fighter and a slanderer is one who is accustomed to speaking with a wagging tongue. For no one of such a kind is able to be directed in a good disposition, always turning away from the fighter; for they are lovers of sinning through rejoicing in battles, insults, and slanders. Therefore, it is not possible for such a person to be directed by virtue. And he who is always trivial in everything is called unrighteous. Perhaps he speaks of the hand that operates the corruption in those who frequently perform many evil deeds.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Sacrifice of Praise and the Discipline of Silence
english: Punishment is corruption, appearing from the corruption. 'With your corruption, O Jerusalem, who will help?' (Ps 79:9). And also the hand-operated disposition will be corrupted because of uncleanness; it will be corrupted by decay, as it is shown by 'Evil conversations corrupt good habits' (Ps 139:13-14).

He says 'judgment' is the examination of deeds and intentions, and 'justice' is the repayment according to merit. And even if the same subject is signified by both words in a parallel way, examine it yourself. The same must be said concerning the poor and the needy; for indeed, both names applied to the same thing must be taken according to different matters, such as being 'poor' if one has fallen greatly from wealth (for the rich have become poor and hungry), but 'needy' being one who has the necessary things for living through toil rather than through property.

The righteous confess either that they have not fallen into such things themselves, or that those who disregarded them and caused them much harm were subjected to such burdens by the judgment and justice of God. Regarding the confession of the righteous, the upright—others of the righteous—will dwell in the face of the Lord; those who confessed by the name, the righteous, confessed. Others of the righteous, the upright, if not entirely in substance, but in thought only, being righteous in one who performs moral virtues, and upright in one who has possessed the contemplation of truth.

Perhaps one who sometimes performs praiseworthy things may be called righteous, but while the practical man of the righteous confesses by the name of God, the upright one has acquired a city and a house through contemplation, dwelling in the face of God. For the character of the substance has been shown to be the face of God, Him dwelling in this face, concerning which it is said everywhere, 'If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation' (2 Cor 5:17).

And if the 'upright who will dwell with your face' is to be explained, not thus: 'that your face they will dwell in, the upright, not going out from the face of the Lord God like Cain (Gen 4:16), or fleeing from it according to those things said concerning him, "And Adam and his wife fled from the face of the Lord God" (Gen 3:8).' But not thus: 'You are found upright, saving the image and likeness of you, having become conformed...'

They dwell in the likeness of the image of your Son, so that your Son may be found [in them], the fulfillment of what the Savior said concerning such things: 'I am that I am, and they shall be with me, to behold my glory.' And this is to be heard not locally but in a God-befitting manner.

[Ps 140:2b] This sacrifice is offered by one who, having hurried to complete it, reaches the evening, while the one sacrificing in the morning offers according to the law the sacrifices that present the sensible things. But at noon, after this, he who has learned what is said by the Lord, 'You desire sacrifice, not burnt offerings, but the knowledge of God' [Ps 140:3]. And above all, an evening sacrifice is to be heard, the offering of the hands previously mentioned.

[Ps 140:3-4] If the lips of the prophet approach with crushing, and a smooth-tongued man will not be directed upon the earth. May I also not fall into these things, O Lord; a guard to my mouth and a door of restraint around my lips. For I have set all things upon myself, having obeyed the exhortation of the one saying, 'With your words make a weight and a balance' [Prov 16:11]. For it is not advantageous for all to speak, nor even to be silent; for to the one able to open the mouth with the word of God, silence is not fitting, but to the one who brings forth a word that is idle and to those condemning words, silence will be for good. But those who practice silence differ from the one saying, 'He who keeps silence is found wise,' and 'He is keeping silence, for he has no answer,' and 'He is keeping silence, knowing the time.' For the one possessing the knowledge of the time to speak and the time when it is not necessary to speak, would ask that a guard and a door be present to his mouth and his lips from God, so that he might not bring forth anything unseasonably; and let the one who is not called to answer the questions being put forward be requested [to remain silent], so that, having been shown to be unbridled toward God, he might not answer rashly instead of others; for indeed, let the one found wise through silence seek confirmation from God by that silence through which he is found wise. And since men who work iniquity make excuses, defending themselves ostensibly on behalf of those on whose behalf they work wickedly, I, having entreated you much, O Lord, deserve [to be heard], that I might also [entreat] on behalf of not coming into such a disposition, or of having a heart flowing into words of wickedness upon the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Pretexts for Sin and the Victory of the Word
english: Men make excuses in sins along with those practicing lawlessness. For if my heart were kept by your guarding, I would not be joined with the chosen ones among men who practice lawlessness. And these chosen ones are those who use pretexts upon which they act wickedly, being worse than those without pretexts who lawlessly act without covering. For these are not like those who sin while knowing, who seem to hold ignorance or weakness as a pretext, but like those who lawlessly act while knowing. If, through the things set forth, the one praying says, 'No cause, O Lord, should exist, as if through ignorance, or force, or weakness, that my heart should be turned toward words of wickedness through any pretext upon which one sins,' how might he not also avoid being joined with the chosen ones among men who practice lawlessness? (Ps 140:5b). In this, the ruling principle, as if the head of the soul, must be considered to signify the head.

Understand also this: what else are the chosen ones who practice lawlessness but those in good will, or false doctrines and evil dispositions, whom you would deem worthy of having your own prayer become a means to be exposed and cast out? (Ps 140:5c–8a). For in these things his prayer becomes nothing other than a request to God for their overthrow and destruction. Therefore, regarding his worthiness, manage the matter. For the strong ones among the men practicing lawlessness, being the same as their chosen ones, were crushed, as the divine Scripture has often interpreted the Word of God approaching them as a rock. And a symbol of having conquered is to swallow up; for it is said, 'Death was crushed into victory,' and 'That the mortal might be swallowed up by life,' but also 'Aaron's rod swallowed up theirs'; it says the rods of the sophists and the vainglorious, by the victory of the scepter of divine truth.
the scepters of the phalanx
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Deception of the Enemy and the Flight from God
english: It is said. If these things are accomplished well while praising God, he says, 'Lord, Lord, who is like you?'; but if they should sin and turn away through which [sin] works according to malice, casting away all harmony and unity, they are scattered not just anywhere, but in the place of the dead souls.

But this has not arisen from inattention alone, but it is also possible for the eyes of the soul to be lifted toward the Lord, who is able to gather together into himself the things scattered by the adversary, interpreted as 'bones to each one,' and as the Scripture says, 'to each one' [giving] back to its own harmony. And also, to speak in the plural regarding the dispersion (for 'our bones were scattered'), while the saving [thing] is spoken of in the singular; for it is not said, 'O Lord, Lord, our eyes are toward you,' but 'my eyes.' For when the spirit of unity is toward the Lord for those seeing toward him, but malice and the dispersion of the bones is a multitude, those experiencing these things say.

Compare this also to the first commandment of God toward Adam, which had the singular regarding the command and the plural regarding the prohibition: 'For the Lord God commanded Adam, saying, From every tree of the garden you may eat, but from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat; for in the day that you eat of it you shall surely die' (Gen 2:16-17). And if in the Decalogue both the commands and prohibitions were expressed in the singular, the things spoken of are not invalidated; for these things will find their own proper interpretation in due time.

Toward you, O Lord, are my eyes, hoping in you; therefore do not let my soul fall, lest it fall down to the pit (Ps 140:8). For even if the bones of each of us were scattered by the adversary, yet I do not hope that you will gather and restore them to their own concord and harmony; if it does not happen by your goodness, not only will my soul not be destroyed, but it will be saved, you guarding me from the snare in which he established it for me. And not from this alone, but also from the stumbling blocks of those working lawlessness, guard me. And perhaps one snare being set for me is the deception of the wicked according to pseudo-orthodoxy, and the other is the stumbling block of those working lawlessness.

And moral wickedness, for the one stumbling in uncertainty, sees many more acting lawlessly; the testimony of this is 'For when iniquity has increased, love will flee' (Ps 140:10), and the proof is also that the trap set deceitfully, the pseudonymous one, is known from the fact that they 'strengthened themselves with a word of evil' and narrated how to hide traps.

If it is spoken concerning the devil, the explanation will be this: the enemy of our race holds a two-edged sword, woven from his various thoughts, all of which are terrible for the purpose of deceiving, which surrounds men and brings them into a fall through sin, so that they are immediately proven sinners, except for those alone who escape him. For we do not ignore his thoughts; indeed, he has caught many and is making them god-makers with nets, which he used as a snare and incense for the two-edged sword for the hunting of the deceived, as it is written in the prophet. But even if sinners fall into his two-edged sword, I, having withdrawn from all material things, am alone, so that when I pass through this timely life, I may escape the multitude of evils and be joined to the Lord, to be with Him in spirit.

No one recognizes the wise of material things and the foolish, since concerning the wise and wisdom they do not even have a concept, but only the wise recognize themselves and their neighbors. 'Since,' he says, 'no one recognizes me,' I have perceived into the right things which I previously looked upon, having had a perception of them, that since something more wise than I has come to be, my heart would come into the right side, perceiving nothing sensible but all things intelligible.

And since everyone who sins flees from God, as it is presented that one who is after transgression is said to 'flee from the face of God,' both Adam and his wife (Gen 3:8); but he who no longer sins but having been made upright speaks 'Flight has perished from me,' that is, wickedness has perished from me, in which those fleeing from God hide. Therefore also there is no one seeking my soul, having been revealed to God and having stood before Him. And 'searching out' indicates an intensification of the search: 'the one searching out'—the lost is sought and is being sought. The same thing is to have perished and to have fled. And he who has come to be in wickedness does not even repent.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Justification through Faith and the Nature of the Soul
english: having joined my prayer

By the grace through the faith of Jesus Christ, having the righteousness that was revealed apart from law, being testified to by the law and the prophets. Perhaps, since the one believing in him is not judged, he receives from him perfect faith so that he might happen not to be judged. For judgment comes to those who loved the darkness more than the light or to those who do evil works. Surely, if God listens to someone in his own righteousness, he does not enter into judgment with him; for he happens to be his servant, doing all these things commanded to him (Ps 142:3b–4a).

To be brought low to the earth is to have the life of someone observing the things below and thinking the things upon the earth. Just as the life of those having their heart in heaven is tossed about and lifted up, so the one hoarding on the earth and having his mind about sensible things is brought low, having his life toward the earth.

He says, 'In the dark ages' (the rulers of this darkness rule there), 'as the fallen one, to be made like the dead of the age.' But those called sons of this age are not, except the one having stripped himself of these things, not a dead of the age, but having become as a dead of the age. Therefore also the spirit called the spirit of man, being with him, despaired for the sake of help. For since he has encountered the man helping him among those things, it is fitting that he despaired and was angry only upon knowing the things of the man.

This parched earth and the adjacent souls, parched places, the unclean spirit does not pass through, finding no rest or repose with them. But even if they happen to be parched by the drying up of foul waters, they do not pursue the Lord to find him on the straight path, who will also rain upon them as a preceding rain and as a dry rain. Therefore they shall be in waters, having springs in them of living water changing into eternal life.

And since the Holy Spirit does not remain where sin is, having said, 'The enemy pursued my soul' (Ps 142:6b), and the following, let him be careful not because of these things to abandon him then as a spirit present with him, as it is the same as the one proposed: 'Turn not your face away,' and the Holy Spirit.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Learning the Divine Will
english: Do not drive me away from you. For no one who is in God and possesses the Spirit is immediately cast out for sinning, but he who persists in sinning is like a craftsman preparing a tool; for then such a person will be cast out from the divine face and be deprived of the Holy Spirit. However, he who does not possess the Spirit is not stripped [of it], but he does not grieve it [while it is] present through sinning.

In the beginning of the day being illuminated by you, and having begun to shine like the rising of the sun, let me hear of your righteousness [Ps 142:8a]; I am not speaking about it as my own state or hearing. For then, having been benefited by the hearing about it, I will be able to progress as to seeing it with longing. I shall also obtain the vision of it, as he who calls to all the zealous ones, saying, 'Show us, Lord, your mercy'; for then it becomes visible, so that if someone receives what is heard, it is not in ignorance but in the beginning of knowledge, which he revealed through the First.

Perhaps also the former ways, Moses and the prophets, having been walked by someone according to 'Stand in the ways and ask for the paths of the Lord eternal' [Ps 119:58], after the journey in them, seeking the good way, he will say to the father of this [way] alone to the one knowing the way, 'Like a son, make known to me the way in which I shall walk.' Therefore also, having been acknowledged by the father, making itself manifest, he says to the worthy, 'I am the way; for no one comes to the Father except through me' [John 14:6].

Being pursued by a single enemy, as if being finished, he prays now to be rescued from a multitude of enemies [Ps 142:9]. But they do not fight with different words; for he called the leader of evil, the enemy, singular, but his army he called enemies in the plural. And it is most just to be rescued from the enemies, since he fled to no one but to him alone.

'Teach me,' he says, 'not only to know but also to do your will' [Ps 142:10]; for it is not the knowing of it that is sanctifying and making blessed, but it being worked and being done. Therefore also the Savior says, 'Not everyone saying to me, Lord, Lord, will enter the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of my Father' [Matt 7:21].

Regarding the one in the heavens. It is evident what one does the will of God and understands it, not necessarily being one who knows it and does not do it; for this reason, the 'Learn to do good' agrees. And what is this learning of the divine will, the following word signifies: what is the guidance of the Holy Spirit into the straight land. For the one having learned the will of God in moral virtues will be guided by the gift of God by the Holy Spirit who works upon all truth. And the straight land is the good and pure heart in which Jesus will bear fruit, the seed of the gentle ones. And it can also be thus: 'Teach me to do your will,' not merely formally but spiritually, fulfilling your law, which happens to be not other than your will; and having progressed to this and having been guided by the Holy Spirit into the straight land, one articulates the remaining truth face to face.
