In some [texts] it is carried instead of 'Your Holy Spirit' as 'Your Good Spirit'; from which it is presented that the holy is good and the good is holy, and 'good' is not by participation in goodness but is good by essence, such as also the holy is. And such is the Father; for indeed it is said concerning him, 'Holy Father,' and 'No one is good except God.' And the Son, being from the good and the holy, is said to be good and holy. Ps 142:11: 'For the sake of your called name, I will do your justice. You will make me live in your righteousness, for you justify me; for it will not happen that I live in it.' It is fitting, therefore, that 'You will make me live' inclines toward future time, since here, just as we possess other good things only partially, we shall live perfectly when Christ, our life, is revealed; for he is the righteousness of God, in whom the one who approaches him will live. Ps 143:1: Since everything that is good and useful comes from God to men, what do the saints possess concerning such things? They give thanks to God, knowing him to be the cause of the good things. Behold, even David, having experienced fighting his enemies in military matters, those invisible diverse ones who are overturned and cast down, bless God, becoming a teacher to himself of that knowledge.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Nature of Man and the Revelation of the Father
english: Regarding such wars, it is as if the fingers and hands of a man were skillfully touching the defenses, through which one might strike and wound the evil men and demons who are protectors of wickedness and false knowledge. Ps 143:4.

The composition of men from a corruptible body and an immortal soul, joined together, possesses according to the immortal and spiritual soul a thought and knowledge of the cause of all things; but according to the body, it is nothing, being compared to the moving and bright shadow of the day of a man's life. Ps 143:4.

Yet although the power of the soul is spiritual, it is not reckoned as a god by chance, but by providing good things to God itself. For it is not said, 'What is man, that he should know you and think about you,' but, 'That you were known and you think about him.' For the Savior makes himself manifest to those prepared for this, and by this it is said that they know him. Having been known also according to spiritual contemplation, having been seen, he shows also the Father to be seen by the same. For 'He who has seen me has seen the Father,' and 'No one knows the Father except the Son and whomsoever the Son wills to reveal.' Since, therefore, the Son, possessing the Father within himself, shows Him to be seen by the same, so also the Father, possessing the Son within himself, reveals Him to him who wishes to have knowledge not through flesh and blood but from God. Ps 143:5,6.

And the following things are able to signify the coming of the Savior from Mary, who, having bent the heavens which are His handiwork, descended because He was to come forth from her. Since, therefore, having descended, He overturned the invisible demons who are harmful and filthy to men with all their host, through which they are called 'decaying' because they see themselves as arrogant and lofty. Since, therefore, the things being purified and made bright are not gold and silver by the striking of fire upon them, but...
by the fire that has come to be cast upon the earth
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The True Theology of Abraham
english: Many waters are brought forth in vain, through which the impious and godless contend. For they wish to imitate through them the one who said, 'If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink, and whoever drinks of the water I will give him shall become a spring of water welling up to eternal life' (John 4:14). And indeed, in these things Jesus gives as if it were one water; this is the Spirit which those believing in him are to receive.

The waters of the heterodox, through which they imitate the quenching given by the Lord, are many, because they are diverse and discordant and do not lead to a single end; for both the ends and the beginnings of their mindsets are different. 'Send therefore,' says the Psalmist, 'your poetic and protective hand, to bring me out and to rescue me from many waters and from the hand of strange sons' (Ps 143:7). For the strange is commonly to be taken both in terms of sons and of waters. And it is possible to say that to be rescued from many waters means from the evil powers and from the devil, the king of all those in such waters; and to be rescued from the hand of strange sons means those working through men.

The ten-stringed psaltery is composed and joined by the energy of the ten commandments; for each of the ten commandments is a string musically composed in the whole instrument. 'And kings, he says, you shall perceive, and those who rule perceptibly the nations and the inhabited world' (Ps 143:10). For if a king is not saved by much power, the kings being saved by God possess the kingdom. And also it is said of giving salvation to kings. Since they always have it from the one being saved, he did not cease to give salvation, but always has given, and will give, and gives. And the same applies concerning the one redeeming and not having redeemed and the one about to redeem.

Be useful to those destined for the turning away of the world (Ps 143:12). For concerning the women of the church, Paul writes how they, praying with modesty and self-control, adorn themselves with the works of godliness, but not with the laying down of gold and pearls and elaborate hairstyles (1 Tim 2:9). Consider these things said and apply them to the heterodox. For their word is struck like swords.

Regarding the devouring and the stripping away of those who have not put on the armor of God. Those previously mentioned as speaking vanity, who are alien sons, use this evil sword. The divine thoughts may be their sons, having strength in youth but not in perfection, being like their daughters, whose words are beautified and trimmed with a smooth composition and the elegance of phrasing.

Therefore, they are a likeness of a temple but not a temple; for they do not have within themselves a divine mind like the words of the divine Scriptures; for a temple is where God is found in them who encounter them rightly. He exalts God, the one theologizing rightly and truly, uttering great and high things concerning God (Ps 144:1). He says regarding the faith set forth of him who became a child of Abraham through works and faith, that the God of all causes is not [his God], but he confesses toward him, 'I am your God.' But he, having become a man of God by serving his God, fleeing every evil kingdom, is ruled by this God himself, and so he will be able to say, 'You are my king and my God.' Having the soul say immortal, he says, 'I will bless your name for ever and unto the age of ages.' And he blesses the name of God and his king, the one doing to wear it and saying and thinking the things belonging to the divine calling upon him, beginning to bless from the present age unto the doing of it as of the age; for if now, knowing in part and participating partially in the good, he blesses the name of the benefactor, much more he will bless when he approaches the perfect good and the face-to-face knowledge of God.

And it shall be said also concerning those from the circumcision and from the Gentiles who have believed: 'Generation and generation shall praise your works' (Ps 144:4), being rightly worthy of praise by his own word, just as he has seen the divine Creator with a divine gaze to be very beautiful. The holiness of God is not another of the Savior; for he himself is the sanctification who sanctifies those approaching God, to whom it is said, 'You shall be holy, as I am holy' (Lev 11:44). The glory of this holiness is majestic.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Kingship of God and the Justice of His Son
english: It is. Therefore, those who have been instructed in the holiness of God and also in his glory, they are transformed and they hymn him magnificently, not by bare speech, but before this by works and right disposition, thinking, acting, and speaking holily, gloriously, and magnificently.

The glory of the holiness of God is able to be: 'He will glorify' (that is, the Paraclete), what he will take from me and declare to you. Therefore, also those who hear him declaring, in giving the word of wisdom and the word of knowledge, they speak of this holiness. And toward this they will recount his wonders, not merely what the holiness is, but penetrating the mystical word of his wonders, which occur at various times and are occurring, with precision and keen contemplation.

It is fearful to fall into the hands of the living God (Hebrews 10:31), and 'Shout to God with a voice of joy' (Ps 144:6), what the Lord is most high and awesome; they will say this in practice and through right understanding (for through this fear of God and exceeding reverence, they will say to him the power of his awesome things). And if they have been benefited, they will fear his greatness with virtue and sinlessness, and they will not say 'the power of your awesome things' but they will recount it after having known what is without experience and without limit; for they do not recount it as having described and limited it to the intellect, but as surpassing every human apprehension.

For only the Son knows who the Father is, and the Father who the Son is; but even if the Son reveals the Father as he wills, not as it is possible for humans to see according to analogy, anyone who has it before preparation will make him manifest. Since a perceptible trembling becomes a fullness (for having been filled with food, he sends out spirits bringing breath, according to the quality of the things eaten), it follows that one must say that he who has eaten the words concerning the goodness of God, having been filled from these spiritual foods, intensely stirs up the memory of the goodness of God, of the goodness capable of being good. But since it is advantageous toward knowing God for the good, also his justice...

And the mind judges them, so that the memory of your goodness shall be searched out, and they shall rejoice in your justice. The justice of God can be the only-begotten offspring of Him, upon which those having obtained the Wisdom born to us from God—justice and sanctification and redemption—rejoice.

For what was sent to proclaim to the captives the goodness of God has become redemption for those being set free from captivity, who, remembering the goodness of God that happened to them, search out its memory; but also having perceived how they were justified, it having become for them the work of the one redeeming and of the justice from God, they rejoice in this justice of God. And those who are to receive both all practical virtue and the justice having come through the faith of Jesus into all those believing are made manifest in the present word. [Ps 144:13] All those whom God has made through his word and his wisdom, God holds and reigns; therefore God is almighty.

Since, therefore, even the ages, being part of all things, have come to be through God by means of the Savior according to the Scripture saying, 'Through whom also he made the ages, and over all of them he reigns,' and since the thing theologized by Paul agrees with these things: 'To the King of the ages, the incorruptible, invisible, only wise God' [1 Tim 1:17]. For to reign over all the ages and to be the King of the ages is the same thing.

Consider if it is said of the Son, 'Your kingdom is the kingdom of all the ages,' reigning over Jacob, that his kingdom has no end; for reigning over all those having come through him, he holds and reigns for the ages. Therefore, just as the others who belong to the Father, so also the Almighty shares in the approachability. If not the Father is the King of the ages and the Son's kingdom is the kingdom of all the ages, it is fitting that his kingdom is also without beginning and without end, both before the ages and while reigning with them; for 'the Lord reigns for an age and for ever and ever' [Ps 10:16], and 'our God is King before an age,' that is, before every age. Accordingly, his lordship also extends to the kingship...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: True Calling and the Divine Will
english: He rules over all generations, being Lord of those within time and generation, but reigning over those who have ascended beyond the temporal by looking at the unseen and eternal things. 'But God is faithful in all his words' (Ps 144:13a). It is said not that they offer [something] from faith or by faith, but that it is worthy to be to the one believing.

Indeed, everything he says becomes according to what is written: 'He said, and he will not do or speak, and he will not remain' [text is garbled/corrupt here]. For it is said, 'Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away' (Matt 24:35). Regarding being faithful in his words and holy in all his works, imparting to them the holiness from himself: just as one is holy among those participating in his holiness, and the Savior is wise among the wise according to him, so the Lord is holy in all his works becoming holy through communion with him.

Perhaps those who are in desires and bad thoughts without practice fall; but those who sin actively are shattered. However, he helps both sides, supporting some and restoring others. How does he support? By commanding each one, 'You shall not covet your neighbor's wife' (Ex 20:17), and the following, and 'Do not let beauty's desire overcome you' (Prov 21:9) by advising through a wise man. Those falling are those sinning in morals while being encompassed by Christianity, but those shattered are those turning away from it; those falling are those sinning in practice, but those shattered are those entering into the impious heresies of the ungodly.

In all his ways he causes to walk, providing and governing, judging, benefiting, granting, punishing; righteous he is found (Ps 144:17a); 'for God is faithful, and there is no injustice' (Ps 144:17). If someone says his ways are the virtues (for those traveling practically and intellectually bring them to him), and in these he appears righteous. No one living earnestly and according to virtue blames providence, but if someone has stood foolishly outside his ways: 'A man's folly ruins his paths' (Prov 14:12), yet he blames God in his heart. Regarding the saying of 'ways' and those given from him in...

If one dares, the righteous man will be known, having matched them in power to those who have received [grace]. But he who says that nature is an unproven virtue in men, or that fate is forcing them into sin, does not rightly say that God is in the ways He has legislated (Ps 144,18).

It is said that He is near to those who call upon His name. Therefore, those making progress pass on to calling upon Him in truth; for calling upon the name of the Lord is more introductory for those who are perfecting themselves in calling Him. For Moses says, and Aaron among His priests, and Samuel among those calling His name, they called upon the Lord, and He himself heard them—those doing this sincerely and not by chance.

It is possible to say that those living according to the letter of the law call upon the name of the Lord, whereas those following the novelty of the Spirit call upon Him in truth, appropriately worshiping Him in spirit and truth. Each of those having a pious disposition, having denied human will, wishes to have the will of God, saying, 'Teach me to do your will, O my God, for You are God' (Ps 51:17). Therefore, he who does the will of those fearing Him transforms his own will into action, he who wishes to have God as his will, revering Him.

And there is no difference, in the plural or the singular, between 'wills' and 'the will'; for His wills are the virtues according to each kind, but His will in general is the universal and common virtue. He who wishes to be guarded by Him, so that by no means the evil one may deceive him, let him love God with all his heart and soul and strength. To those thus guarded by Him because they love Him, the things promised without falsehood are made favorable, concerning which it has been said, 'An eye has not seen and an ear has not heard, nor has there risen upon the heart of man [what] God has prepared for those who love Him' (Ps 144,19a).

He says 'mouth,' not the sensible but the intelligible, as also in another psalm toward God: 'I will open my lips, and my mouth shall declare your praises.' Yet, when His praises are being spoken, all flesh having heard Him shall bless His holy name.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The God of Jacob as Helper and the Truth of His Promises
english: That which is called upon her, the disciples of Jesus do not understand, praying to others saying, 'Hallowed be thy name.' And all that flesh blesses his holy name; concerning this it is said, 'Hear my prayer; unto thee all flesh shall come' (Ps 145:1,2). And all flesh shall see his salvation. These things are not said concerning sensible flesh, but concerning the existing analogy to the fleshy hearts, concerning which God says, 'I will take away from them the stony hearts and I will put in them fleshy hearts,' in which the spiritual law has been inscribed, Paul saying about this, as it is not written on stone tablets but on fleshy heart tablets (2 Cor 3:3).

The hymn is not being sent up to God by those happening to be [celebrating], but by the one celebrating God in doing the necessary things and remembering him according to right and pious discourse. For 'Angaios' is a feast, and 'the memory of God' are the interpretations of Zechariah. Everyone who does not work the practical virtues unceasingly, not even one but many feasts, is named Angaios in the Hebrew tongue; but also everyone who has suffered well through all things and has been benefited by the goodness of God, remembering [him], is called Zechariah according to the Hebrew voice, interpreted as the memory, that is, of God.

Praise, O my soul, the Lord. But when will this happen and how will you always do it? How does the release from sins approach through virtue and the rectitude of the knowledge of truth? For praise is due to the upright, not to the beautiful word in the mouth of a sinner. I will praise the Lord in my life; for as long as I live (and I live always the eternal life), I will praise. It is shown through the things set forth that no one possessing death, every soul sinning, is able to praise the Lord. I will sing to God my God, as long as I exist. And it is often interpreted that to sing according to virtue means to act. Therefore, a harmonious practice is promised to the Praise. And the 'as long as I exist' [means] to submit the mind...

Such a thing is not possible: for as I possess a share in the one who says, 'I am the Being,' I sing with the one who has the desire for me, for no one can sing being separated from the existing God and not becoming a being.

It is also not possible to divide [trust] thus: 'Do not trust in rulers who are of this age, nor in other evil powers (for they are falling and do not have the beginning), nor even in the sons of men; for salvation is not for them, they do not become salvation for mortals; for they are not able to provide it, nor do they have salvation from where they are, but they receive it from God' [Ps 145:3].' For the Savior alone is the cause of eternal salvation, saying, 'Salvation is not from me.'

But he is blessed not simply as God is a helper, but as 'God of Jacob is a helper' [Ps 145:5-7b], being helped by the God who shakes the rulers and the authorities and the cosmic rulers of this darkness. For he who has the struggle against these, having shaken them regarding what has happened to them, is helped by the God of Jacob, the son of Jacob who is [so called] according to practice in his doing his works. Thus being helped, he has hope in the Lord God who in the beginning trusted the heaven and the earth, the sea and all things in them. For he did not only those things, but also all things in them he himself made. And if his works endure, much more he himself is enduring and powerful.

Therefore, take courage, for the truth of both his words and the promises in the holy letters is confirmed, and he preserves his own promises for the whole age, so that his word and promises do not fail, as he promised to his own people. And what is the truth of the word? It is the coming judgment and the vengeance for those being wronged in the present life. For do not think, he says, that the pious are overlooked, nor that the blood of God-beloved men goes unavenged. For he is truthful who, having promised to perform their vengeance.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Inclusion of Gentiles and the Protection of New Believers
english: And they hunger and thirst according to the present life, and [He] gives eternal food to those being distressed, according to the Beatitudes: 'Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall themselves be filled' (Matt 5:6), and according to the prophetic word saying, 'Behold, my servants shall eat, but you shall hunger' (Isa 55:20).

If one wishes to perceive these things sensorially: He gave manna to those hungering in the wilderness, and nourished five thousand hungry men; and He gave also to Elijah and Daniel, the one through ravens, the other through the prophet Ambakum. And He made judgment for those being wronged: Joseph by the Egyptians, Susanna by the judges of Israel, and David being wronged by Saul and others more; the Scripture is most full of these. (Gen 42:21; Dan 13)

Those being broken are the same as those being laid low, differing only in thought; for they are hindered from acting and from running toward the truth, being laid low by wickedness, they fall from the height of virtue and happen to be broken. It must be said that those laid low and broken are those sinning in practice, being blind ones who cast away the seeing of the intellect, so that they do not see the beauties of the dogmas of the truth.

Just as he released the laid low and straightened the broken, desiring the forgiveness of sins, so he enlightened the blind, having enlightened the eyes of their hearts, he himself about whom Paul writes: 'The God who said, Let light shine out of darkness, has shone in your hearts to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God' (2 Cor 4:6).

Since the word spoken refers to the memory of the righteous among the converts: those loved by the Lord are called righteous, those having been pleasing to him according to the Old Scripture; but converts are those called from the Gentiles upon the teaching of the Gospel. And what the intellect questions, it is to be heard from the Savior saying, 'Many prophets and righteous men desired to see what you see and to hear what you hear' (Matt 23:37). Among these righteous ones is Abraham, concerning whom it is written: 'Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness' (Gen 15:6). And concerning the Gentiles as being converts, it is to be heard from Paul saying, 'Therefore remember...'

You used to be of the Gentiles, and once you were separated from the commonwealth of Israel (Eph 2:12). But now, you who once became distant, have become near in the eye of our Lord Jesus Christ; for He is our peace. Furthermore, you are no longer strangers and sojourners, but fellow citizens with the saints and members of the household of God (Eph 2:19), having been built up upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets (Eph 2:20).

Concerning these proselytes, Moses said to Israel, saying, 'If you do not obey the commandments of the Lord your God, the proselyte who is among you will be above you, but you will be below' (Deut 23:7), through the changing of circumstances. Indeed, before the coming of the Savior, those of the Gentiles who hurried to worship God approached Israel being instructed and obeying them; but now, those who wish to approach the faith of Christ from the Israelites are setting aside the evangelical commonwealth, approaching as sacrifices among those of the Gentiles who have believed.

In addition to this, take care lest the proselytes who are coming now through godliness—though those who have passed through and been perfected in it are called righteous—should be lost; for God loves the righteous, but He guards the proselytes. For those who have arrived immediately by the word of truth, lest they may not be strong and firm, need the guarding of the Lord so that they may remain unhurt, whereas the righteous are made members of Him and loved by Him through perfection.

He will take up the orphan and the widow (Ps 68:5)—not any widows, but those continuing in purity and reverence. Such is Anna, the daughter of Phanuel, whom the Gospel remembers (Luke 2:36). The Lord will take up such a widow through incorruptible prudence, along with her well-endured orphanhood, lifting them up and raising them by virtue, so that He may also lead them into the heavenly blessings.

It is possible to say of orphans being taken up that they are the godly who leave behind parents; such as Abraham, going out from the land and kindred and the house of his father at God's calling of him (Gen 12:1); and also James and John, having left Zebedee their father through the invitation of Jesus (Mark 1:19). Following these things also...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Allegorical Interpretation of Psalm 146/147
english: You say that widows are being taken after having been separated from men in perfect prudence, by the mutual consent of both, the man and the woman, for the same purpose as those who dissolved the marriage. But more allegorically, the souls that cast off the one who became their father, the devil, are orphans and widows being taken. Once these are taken, the way of the sinners, which is nothing other than wickedness, shall be destroyed by God (Ps 145:10).

Zion, the watchful and examining one of the truth, is the perfect soul, the church of the living God; your God shall reign forever (Ps 146:3), the end of the kingdom shall not be delayed, his rule extending from generation to generation. It is said in this psalm before this, concerning his unending kingdom extending through all ages and how he rules from generation to generation. Therefore, being satisfied with those, as they apply them also to the present words, we shall say nothing more.

Since the psalm is good and beneficial to the user, praising its honor, announce to him that in praising this psalm, there is no difference from that one, especially since the one singing in spirit and mind and singing with the heart does not differ. If, however, to sing signifies to act in practice, it is advised to those who have perfected this good psalm to also praise Christ through theology, so that, having been perfected in practice and thought, they may rejoice in God; for he says, 'A sacrifice of praise shall glorify me' (Ps 146:5), and the Spirit commands to bring it forward, as those who say, 'Offer to God a sacrifice of praise.'

He also takes up the meek (Ps 147:6), lifting them up to where they inherit the land. But that land they inherit is high above. Therefore it has also been written, 'He will bring you up upon the good things of the earth,' and 'He will lift you up to inherit the land.' He takes up the meek, but he humbles the sinners as those who carry the image of the earth, thinking of low things and those upon the earth. Just as Paul, the meek one, was taken up to the third heaven (2 Cor 12:2) and to be a participant in unutterable things as if in paradise. And all those who call upon their names upon their lands, being in the flesh and not having the Spirit of God, having departed from God upon the earth, are written [down].

For thanksgiving, awakening those who have received so many good things. 'Begin,' he says, 'in confession, hymning and glorifying him for those things on which he worked' (Ps 146:8-9). And allegorically, his divine word surrounds the heaven with noetic clouds pouring down a noetic rain: for the heaven above rejoiced, and the clouds (surrounding him) rained down righteousness. From these noetic clouds he prepares rain for the earth, which Jesus spiritually sowed to bring forth fruit divided into one hundred and sixty and thirty, bringing up grass in the deserts for the great-souled and providing for the soul a fresh green clover to be found upon the slavery of men to be fed as food.

But the slavery of men is the irrational animals. This is said concerning the things destined, as we saw in the hundred and third Psalm; let us see them further. He brings up and gives food to the simpler sheep and cattle of those having believed in Christ, which are being saved apart from men. But he gives food not only to these, but also to the high-flying ones, for he commanded the young ravens to call upon him. God gives food to these, since they call upon him, according to the perfect men, concerning whom it is said, 'They called upon the Lord, and he heard them' (Ps 145:4). And you will understand the young ravens to be those from the nations who have believed and because of this call upon the Lord, so that he may give them spiritual food. For the raven is unclean and gloomy. Such are the evil demons and those who have added to impiety, of whom they were formerly sons, but having believed they obtained the heavenly food.

The gates of Jerusalem are the introductory teachings, with the destructive words lying upon them, or the representing ranks of Jerusalem, having the capacity to silence those who contradict (Ps 147:2). 'For he has blessed your sons in you,' those who will act and will possess the capacity of thought; for because they become such sons of her, being blessed in her, they never cease to act, having learned to turn to the house of the Lord all the days of their lives. And the word interpreting [it] as the one who blessed the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Snow and Mist of Divine Word
english: He brings her children within her, he who sets your borders in peace, with all war having fled from her borders, against the wars that crush, the Lord setting the borders of the city in peace. By saying peace, he imparts to her spiritual food.

And if you wish to say that the educational words of God are fire (not that they are [something] by which one is filled?), you do not err. For it is said in the prophet, in the face of God toward the false prophets, 'What is chaff with grain?' Thus are my words, says the Lord; the words of himself are indeed grain, but theirs are chaff through the word. Just as the wisdom from God is not earthly, nor psychic, nor demonic, but descending from above Him, so also His word, not being from the earth, is sent into the earth, becoming for each of those able to serve Him the same thing as the word given by the Lord to those preaching the gospel with much power. If this thing given, being distributed, runs swiftly to more souls, the word of God, being fulfilled, 'Their voice has gone out into all the earth and their words to the ends of the inhabited world' (Ps 147:4). Truly his taking up has happened, and immediately the evangelical word passed through all the earth, to everyone under the heaven.

Regarding the things said before, it appears to us that these things have been set forth in a parabolic manner, by placing the works of the cosmic creation alongside the economy concerning the church by way of likeness. For just as snow is a layer covering a place, and after this a thaw occurs and water pours out, so the divine word, having dwelt among the Jews first, after this pours out upon all. Therefore also the mission of the word and the blowing of the Spirit are well indicated through the cosmic works: that just as the word comes into the world and the Spirit breathes, the word of the holy and saving teaching went out from Jerusalem to all the inhabited world. If one is to take this also up in allegory, since it stands forth spiritually regarding His running word: for indeed, 'You will wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow' (Ps 51:7), one should not think in terms of sensible snow...

How can the soul be made whiter than snow, which is beyond sensation, if it is not a participant in the brightness of the rational nature through the whiteness of the snow? To this thought the saying, 'If your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow' (Isaiah 1:18), contributes; for one cannot conceive of sins being whitened like physical snow.

Perhaps the most beautiful word cast upon the earth by the Lord is like wool, a garment to be fashioned for the soul, this wool being produced by the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world (John 1:29). Similarly, you will perceive those cast down like crystal flakes and the mist passing like ash. Farmers need snow and mist; for these, when they come upon the offspring, increase them. Just as even upon the good earth of the soul, if the seed has fallen, it is necessary that rain and dew fall, so too snow and mist must come upon our offspring, so that we may bear fruit being nourished by all these.

You will perceive the snow, the crystal, and the mist as temptations brought upon the saints for testing. For they are not being chilled in the love within them by opposing powers, just as 'as a pit cools, so does its wickedness cool' [allusion]. In the face of this cold, who will endure, if not he who, like Peter, Paul, Job, and James the speaker who said 'I became' (James 1:12), is joined with the heat of the day and the frost of the night?

Toward these things you will also take the things said by Moses: 'Let my speech drop as the rain, and my words descend as the dew, as the gentle rain upon the tender grass, and as the snow upon the herb' (Deuteronomy 32:2). For by the word, the sayings of Moses are made like these; by this word, the word sent to the land of God is logically divided into all things spoken. And what is this cold that no one can endure from its presence, to be seen as worthy? Perhaps his word, being fiery, is compared to fire, warming and making to boil those who have been chilled by wickedness, whose love was cooled by the abundance of lawlessness; again, against the souls being burned by the flame of pleasures and passions, the cold of God is called, not according to...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Abyss, Dragons, and the Creative Word
english: No one will be able to withstand those who are burned by passions, since their hearts have been kindled like a furnace, like the light of fire, since all are committing adultery and are being burned by lawless desires. To these things, the coming of pain from the storehouses and cold from the heights, as carried in Job, is appropriate.

The provident Word of God, being sent, will melt the snow and those counted with it, but also when He breathes, His spirit will flow (for He says the south wind), turning into these things the ones forenamed of the snow and those near it (Ps 147:7). And it is necessary even spiritually to hear these things: the clarifying Word of God, having been sent with concealment, will melt the mist, the crystal, and the snow, making them like a drink upon the watering place, but by His spirit, the spirit of this God breathing; but also the Word of God, being sent into the heart of those receiving Him, will melt the trials and make them invisible, those who, warming by the spirit, will courageously undergo such trials, will dissolve them.

To the one who has trampled and flapped the rulers and the authorities and the cosmic rulers of this darkness, mystically called Jacob, He sends His word, which is salvific and creative, in order to make all the true doctrines of piety clear to him (Ps 147:8-9). And after the victory having been achieved through insight and Israel having been shown to see by intellect God, His requirements and His judgments, He sent [the Word] to work all things determined and just. And upon these things, the greatness of the God's gift existing to the mortal, manifesting, He says: He did not do thus to every mortal, but only to Israel He performed the foretold things before the arrival of the Savior; however, the coming of Christ, the High Priest of truly good things, all mortals are filled with the divine Word (Ps 148:7-8). But—

Someone might say regarding this, as the very words show, that calling the multitude of the waters an abyss (for the Lord walked upon it) is as if there were another beginning: 'The gates of death open to you in fear,' and the following. If he says that the dragons were also named appropriately with the abysses, being more [terrible] than the creeping things upon the earth; and in another psalm, being called waters, it was said that dragons were in them, not other than the abyss named here. For it is also written in the seventy-third [Psalm]: 'You crushed the heads of the dragons upon the water,' and 'You crushed the head of the dragon.

It must be understood that evil powers are signified by these, as the Word of God crushed them, and through time has descended even unto the abysses. But observe, he says, how very strongly the Word does not command the dragons in the abysses to praise, but simply mentions them; for they are not worthy to praise God. They are called by necessity to obey the hymn being lifted up by all creation to the Lord, King, and God: fire, hail, snow, ice, wind of a storm, which do His Word (Ps 148:8).

All these things, existing around the air, were necessarily mentioned as parts of the whole cosmos and as subsisting through the Divine Word and serving Him. For apart from the creative Word, the whole cosmos would be moving aimlessly and without presiding over its days; neither snow, nor fire, nor ice, nor storm, nor wind would ever subsist, nor would they ever act apart from His will. Thus, these things doing His Word should not be heard [as acting independently].
It is also possible to say [of] kings and rulers and judges, those living loftily and approaching things critically and investigatively, and the lower peoples who have believed.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Two-Edged Sword of the Saints
english: The only-begotten Word of God is the horn of the people, to whom the holy ones, when they call out, say: 'We gore our enemies with you.' Therefore also the Word was named one-horned, according to the glory of being one-horned. Concerning this it is said: 'There I will cause a horn to rise up for David, I have prepared a lamp for my Christ' (Ps 131:17); for he showed in opposition that the Christ, who is to be born according to the flesh from the seed of David, is a horn, and he ordains it not as the sun and light to rise again. This, therefore, the horn says, will lift up his people, so that having been lifted up, it may become manifest to all the nations.

But it is for the holy alone to sing, not for the sinners, since: 'Not a beautiful song in the mouth of a sinner' (Ps 149:2); for praise is due to the upright. And who are the holy whose song it is, or the discerning sons of Israel who have God in their mind, or those who are called the people approaching God? Those having an enlightened mind and a pure soul approach God by relationship and disposition, being near the exhortation of the one who said: 'Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you' (James 4:8). And it is not by chance that this is so; for it is said concerning the hierophant Moses, what alone approaches God.

Only those having clothed themselves with the new man are able to attain the newness of mind and to do the things of the new covenant, serving by the newness of spirit and not by the oldness of the letter. These same also fulfill the assembly of the holy, accomplishing the faithful and holy things of David and having the most holy righteousness toward God; therefore also the praise does not attain the newness in the assembly of these.

The holy ones, having accomplished this, will rejoice in the glory that is to come and is eternal, even as they are called by that name from it (Ps 149:4). For we reckon, as the apostle says, that the sufferings of the present time are not worthy of the glory that is about to be revealed to us (Rom 8:18). And it is possible to hear of the glory in which the holy ones boast, concerning which it is said: 'The glory of the Lord shall be seen' (Isa 60:1), and 'The glory of your God has risen upon you' (Isa 60:1), not any other than the radiance of the glory of...

Of God. Therefore it is also written, 'Let him who boasts boast in the Lord.' Sleeping together with this glory and wisdom, the holy ones shall boast; for it is said, 'Whenever you sleep, let wisdom be with you'; appropriately to these things you say, 'Honor her, so that she may embrace you.' He who sleeps together with this is without fear and without care, and rejoices at his bed. Therefore all the souls of his holy ones, his brides, being joined together with God the Word, as a bride to the bridegroom of every rational nature, rejoice at their beds (Ps 149:6,7).

The elevations of God, demonstrated through them and through theology, in the noetic throat of the holy ones, happen to be lifting up His name to the same degree. For praising with much truth, they glorify and highly exalt Him, having in their hands two-edged swords, although they are not killing according to men, but are ready to avenge every disobedience, since the weapons of their warfare are not fleshly but are powerful through God, by which they cleanse every seductive fortification through the utterance of high words being raised against the knowledge of God.

And it is also possible to call the two-edged swords in their hands 'two-mouthed'; for the holy ones do not possess each word as two-mouthed, but according to the living and active Word of God, they are more two-mouthed than any sword. Therefore also those using the words of truth do not only cut away the false and the superfluous by loosening sophisms, but they also wound the hearers into the questions of the truth. It is possible to call both types of two-edged swords in the hands of the holy ones found in these practices. And it is possible to call even an exhortatory word a two-edged sword, doing both: rebuking the one who receives it unto repentance, and avenging and punishing the disobedient unto the end.

He does not say that the holy ones make vengeance that leads to destruction upon the Gentiles, but rather the vengeance that happens well upon them, just as the Gentiles and idolaters happen to be, so that, having cast off the life of the nations, they might become fellow-citizens of the saints and become members of God. Therefore
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Power of the Word and the Trumpet of Resurrection
english: And also reproaches will be active among the nations, since the vengeance upon the nations is a greater evil than the reproaches of the people, but the reproaches are against the better peoples. For [it is said]: Reprove the wise, and he will love you; make known to the righteous, and he will add to the receiving. For the peoples will not hate those reproving them because they do not happen to be evil, even if they sin through inadvertence, as opposed to those having a hateful disposition toward those reproving them because of perfected wickedness. If it is therefore said, Do not reprove the evil, lest they hate you.

You will find this same interpretation also in the Gospel, understanding the word of the Savior as saying: If your brother sins against you, go and reprove him between you and him alone; and if he listens to you, you have gained your brother; but if he does not listen to you, take one or two, and if he listens to them, announce it to the church; but if he even despises even the church, let him be to you as a Gentile and a tax collector (Matt 18:15-17). This one, having become evil, having despised through all, is not to be reproved; for he will hate everyone who reproves, if he happens to be unholy.

For they will not put their hands in iron shackles those who seem glorious among them, being unable to act before being bound wickedly and acting toward the harm of many (Ps 149:8-9). But the righteous do not perform the vengeance and the reproaches or the making of the enclosure of bonds in an imprecise way, but with written judgment, bringing about the construction of true dogmas from the written oracles and the overthrow of pseudonymous knowledge. And I do not ignore that some of those who have explained this historically have taken the interpretation for the sake of a victory and trophies and hymns of praise to themselves against certain sensual enemies.

But also the comprehension of God through the divine Scriptures is a stronghold of the power of God, but it is not the power of God itself that exists. And you will perceive also this: whether the power of God is in men, or whether one partakes of the Holy Spirit: For you shall receive power of the Holy Spirit coming upon you, to the apostles (Acts 1:8).

Words are spoken by the Savior, and 'You indeed shall sit in the city,' as if you would not put on power from the height. Therefore, if anyone firmly preserves this power given to him, watching over it with care, becoming in its stability a part of it, he praises God, from whom this divine power is, and he says, 'I am able to do all things in Christ who strengthens me' (Phil 4:13). Since they are ruled by the Savior of power, and in the stability they praise him, understanding that the all-ruling powers—through which he royally creates, provides, benefits, and corrects—they praise him upon his powers.

He who is the unsearchable judgments of God and the unsearchable ways of him, the wise man, knowing according to the multitude of the unsearchable judgments, will praise him (Ps 150:2b); not because of the incomprehensibility of the judgments and the ways, as it says, 'O depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God, and your wisdom was wondered at by me' (Rom 11:33); I was strengthened, yet I am not able toward it. For I cannot contemplate the multitude of it; it becomes stronger than me, as if I were not able to assist it, being infinite and incomprehensible.

He who is not ashamed of Jesus and his words, clearly and loudly bringing forth the things of theology with boldness, praises him and his Father in a trumpet; for even the heralds of the truth have the command to proclaim the teaching more boldly and clearly, having as a trumpet to lift up their voice. For words are indeed spoken to them, 'Sound the trumpet in the trumpet, proclaim in Zion in my holy mountain' (Ps 150:3). But also the resurrection of the dead, which becomes fearful to all those rising, is signaled by a trumpet, for he says, 'The trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible' (1 Cor 15:52), and in another epistle, 'With the voice of an archangel and in the trumpet of God he shall descend from heaven' (1 Thess 4:16), in order to raise those who have slept in Christ. As the command of the resurrection being revealed to all, in order to raise the righteous and the unrighteous, is made known by the loud voice of the instruments.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Breath of Life and the True Voice
english: Likewise, the minds of God follow to be carried forth by the same instrument. Praise him with psaltery and lyre. What is the psaltery and the lyre, and what difference is said to be held between them in those things previously leading up? God is to be praised, singing in spirit and mind; for this is the psaltery; for the spirit and the mind are held together from above by God through the loftiness of dogmas. And he is to be praised also with lyre; through every power of the soul and sensation, with strings stretched, they are struck with order. For the soul was given as a lyre in those things previously read. If, however, through every activity of each member, it is struck as an alien lyre, no one would err in praising God through every action of the body.

Those carrying about the death of Jesus in the body, through which the flesh was killed, praise him with a timbrel (Ps 150:4). It has been interpreted before that the timbrel is that which was destined to be the one among the young women, the timbrel-players. For this is the body, which the soul will take up from the resurrection; it is a young woman playing the timbrel in announcing the minds of God in the standing of the heavenly ones with the myriads of the celebrating angels, as this is made manifest through the approaching word sounding, 'Praise him with timbrel, and also with dance'; for the soul dances with the powers and with all the higher creation after the resurrection, instead of a corrupt and weak and dishonorable and psychic body, having taken up an incorruptible, powerful, glorious, spiritual body. And the praising with strings and instrument is able to be the same as the praising with psaltery and lyre; for perhaps the lyre is strings, and the psaltery is the instrument.

I think it is made manifest through the praising him with loud cymbals (Ps 150:5) that it is necessary also to commemorate the Lord with voice according to utterance through theology. And there appears to me to understand this from the word of the apostle writing thus: 'I have become a sounding brass or a clanging cymbal' (1 Cor 13:1); for if he says, 'If I speak not with mind but with tongue,' not interpreting the things said by the tongue for the understanding of the listener...

Having only a voice without possessing thought, so that the one speaking seems to be a barbarian, having sense of voice and sound only, he becomes to himself a bronze clanging or a resounding cymbal, striking and only making a noise in his hearing. Let us therefore glorify God, and imitating the perfect and righteous men in speech. For it is said concerning each of these: the discourse of a pious man is wisdom throughout; likewise, the mouth of the righteous shall meditate on wisdom, and his tongue shall speak judgment, the law of God being in his heart; that is to say, he praises God also with mind and tongue and mouth.

But the cymbal sounds well if it has a careful and well-modulated voice clearly signifying things. But he says the same cymbal is driven forth with a loud noise according to the falling and becoming under the feet of the enemies. When God becomes all in all, the foretold word shall be fulfilled. For assisting our weakness, He imparts to us the notion of divine breath, just as it has been written concerning the first man: He breathed into his face the breath of life, and he became a living soul (Gen 2:7). For life and the fountain of life is the one who said, 'I am the life' (John 14:6), and concerning life it has been said to the Father, 'From you is the fountain of life' (Luke 10:42).

This breath of life, which makes blessed and sanctifies, coming into the man, shall prepare his soul to live, or to say thankfully, 'My soul lives in him.' This gift alone all shall enjoy who has received the word of Jesus and has believed in the one who sent him to the Father. For the Savior says, 'The one hearing my words and believing in the one who sent me has eternal life' (John 6:47). God offers this breath to those who have ascended far above the sensible things and tread upon them, called His people, just as the prophet says concerning him: 'Thus says the Lord God who made the heavens and established the earth, who gives breath to the people upon it and spirit to those who tread upon it' (Ps 150:6); it is evident what [is] the earth. And it is said also toward something ancient: 'And the breath of the Almighty is the one teaching me' (Job 32:8).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
